papers.title: A hybrid 3D-CNN and CGAN approach for bipolar disorder diagnosis using VBM and SBC features from multimodal MRI
papers.venue: Scientific Reports
papers.abstract: Neuroimaging technologies like structural and functional MRI (sMRI/fMRI) have identified biomarkers for bipolar disorder (BD). Deep learning approaches have shown promising performance in analyzing such data; however, many multimodal models rely on complex architectures with limited biological grounding of their inputs. We developed a diagnostic model using sMRI and fMRI data from 49 BD patients and 121 healthy controls (UCLA CNP study). Rather than raw images, we extracted biologically meaningful features: voxel-based morphometry (VBM) from sMRI and seed-based functional connectivity (SBC) from fMRI. These features were processed using a dual-branch 3D convolutional neural network (3D-CNN). Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks (CGANs) performed feature-space augmentation exclusively on training data after dataset splitting. Model performance was evaluated using nested 5-fold cross-validation. The proposed multimodal framework achieved a mean accuracy of 93.49% and an AUC of 0.97 during repeated nested cross-validation. On an independent held-out test set, the model achieved an accuracy of 93.02%, sensitivity of 83.33%, and specificity of 96.77%. This outperformed the single-modality sMRI model (81.39%) and the three-seed fMRI model (88.37%). CGAN-based augmentation consistently improved classification accuracy across repeated cross-validation runs, with a mean gain of 3.02% (95% bootstrap CI: 1.86–4.19%). These findings suggest that multimodal integration of structural and functional neuroimaging features may improve bipolar disorder classification performance. The proposed framework leverages biologically meaningful feature representations and feature-space augmentation, providing a proof-of-concept approach for multimodal neuroimaging-based classification. Further validation on independent and multi-site datasets is required to assess the robustness, generalizability, and potential translational relevance of the proposed framework.

papers.title: The Development of a Multimodal Sensing, 3D Closed-Loop Circuit for Accelerated Wound Healing
papers.venue: UNC Libraries
papers.abstract: Chronic and acute wounds, including diabetic foot ulcers, pressure ulcers, and traumatic injuries, impose substantial healthcare costs and diminish quality of life for millions of patients worldwide. Conventional wound dressings remain largely passive, offering protection and moisture retention but lacking the ability to actively promote healing. Electrical stimulation (ES) therapy has been shown to accelerate wound healing by restoring tissue-specific injury currents, promoting galvanotaxis of key cell types, and upregulating growth factors such as VEGF, FGF, and TGF-β. However, ES remains underutilized clinically due to bulky devices, inconsistent electrode placement and stimulation parameters, and the absence of real-time wound monitoring to guide treatment. This project addresses these barriers through the development of a textile-based, closed-loop smart dressing that integrates programmable ES electrodes and multimodal sensors into a flexible, embroidered fiber platform. Using an embroidery machine, we developed a protocol for constructing flexible biocircuits from silver fibers on multiple wound-relevant substrates, including gauze, veterinary sutures, medical bandages, and surgical mesh. This protocol enables the production of customized, reproducible circuits tailored to diverse wound geometries and anatomical sites at low cost. We validated the mechanical performance of the fabricated electrodes and confirmed their functionality in sensing temperature, humidity, and strain, as well as their capability to operate as ECG/EMG sensors. These preliminary results establish a standardized fabrication method that address the lack of reproducibility in electrode design and placement that has limited the clinical translation of ES therapy. This work provides a scalable foundation for future closed-loop, textile-integrated wound monitoring systems, with broader implications for advancing personalized, precision wound care. Future work will focus on optimizing battery performance, validating device function using ex vivo and in vivo models, and developing a machine-learning framework to interpret multimodal sensor data and support adaptive, safety-gated treatment recommendations.

papers.title: Deep Learning–Driven Visual Intelligence for Chemical Instrument Monitoring: A Scoping Review From an Expert Systems Perspective
papers.venue: Expert Systems
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Automated visual recognition in industrial environments has become a key enabler for intelligent monitoring systems, particularly in safety‐critical domains such as chemical plants. Unlike general industrial vision tasks, chemical instrument monitoring operates under stringent constraints, including harsh environments, legacy non‐digital devices, and high reliability requirements for decision‐making. In this context, deep learning‐based visual recognition should not be viewed as an isolated perception task, but rather as a critical component within expert systems that support operational decision‐making. This paper presents a comprehensive scoping review of deep learning–driven visual intelligence for industrial applications, with a specific focus on chemical instrument monitoring from an expert systems perspective. A total of 127 studies published between 2015 and 2025 are systematically analysed, covering object detection, image segmentation, and optical character recognition (OCR), along with their integration into practical monitoring pipelines. Beyond categorizing models, this review emphasizes the evolution from standalone perception models toward system‐level solutions that incorporate edge deployment, data‐efficient learning, and explainability. Key challenges are identified, including data scarcity due to proprietary industrial datasets, limited model generalization across dynamic environments, computational constraints in real‐time deployment, and the lack of interpretability required for safety‐critical decision support. Importantly, this review highlights the gap between high‐performing vision models and their reliable integration into expert systems for chemical operations. Emerging trends are discussed, including synthetic data generation, domain adaptation, foundation models (e.g., SAM and open‐vocabulary detection), and multimodal fusion, with a critical evaluation of their applicability and limitations in chemical instrument scenarios. By reframing industrial visual recognition within the broader context of expert systems, this work provides a structured understanding of current capabilities and outlines future directions for developing trustworthy, efficient, and human‐centric intelligent monitoring systems in chemical industries.

papers.title: An Explainable Hybrid Artificial Intelligence Framework for Stock Market Prediction Using Financial Time-Series and Market Sentiment
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This dissertation presents an explainable hybrid artificial intelligence framework for stock market prediction using financial time-series information and market sentiment. The study investigates the integration of historical market observations, technical indicators, sequential deep-learning models, financial sentiment analysis and explainable artificial intelligence within a unified forecasting framework. The methodology addresses data preprocessing, temporal alignment, feature engineering, model development, multimodal feature integration and evaluation. Particular emphasis is placed on preventing information leakage through chronological data handling and on improving the interpretability of model predictions. The dissertation provides a structured research framework for investigating whether financial sentiment provides complementary information to numerical market features in stock-market forecasting.

papers.title: From Feature Engineering to Foundation Models: Predicting and Understanding Community Engagement on Social Media During Disasters, 2019-2026
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Predicting how communities engage with disaster-related content on social media has moved from hand-engineered, feature-based machine learning toward transformer, multimodal, and large-language-model (LLM) architectures. This paper reviews that trajectory using a 2019 doctoral dissertation on Twitter community-engagement and situational-awareness prediction as a structural baseline: a pipeline of topic modeling and event detection, binary and multi-class engagement classification over TF-IDF, psychometric (LIWC-style), linguistic, sentiment, and platform-specific (Twitter) features, and a three-stage clustering-classification-ranking framework validated on a real Hurricane Michael dataset. We summarize the reported results of that pipeline — including per-classifier accuracy, F1, and AUC across feature sets — and contrast them with 2023-2026 advances: BERT- and RoBERTa-family classifiers, cross-attention multimodal fusion of text and imagery, UAV-integrated disaster sensing, and instruction-tuned LLMs that perform multi-label classification, causal-relation extraction, infrastructure monitoring, and stakeholder-specific report generation directly from raw crisis microblogs. We discuss evaluation robustness findings for LLMs across events and languages, the shift from single-platform Twitter/X pipelines toward multimodal and cross-platform sensing, and open problems in annotation quality, class imbalance, hallucination, and real-time deployment that continue to separate research prototypes from operational emergency-management tools.

papers.title: Synthetic Multimodal ECG and Clinical Variable Dataset for Demonstration of AI-based In-hospital Cardiac Arrest Prediction
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This dataset contains synthetic multimodal demonstration data, including XML-format 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) files and structured clinical variable profiles, developed for interface-level testing and workflow illustration of a multimodal deep learning framework for in-hospital cardiac arrest prediction. All files are simulated and contain no real patient information. These data were not used for model training, internal validation, external validation, or performance evaluation. The dataset is provided solely to demonstrate the input structure and data format of the proposed clinical decision support system. No identifiable clinical information is included.

papers.title: Neuromarketing and artificial intelligence in the marketing management system: technological synergy as a tool for managing consumer behavior
papers.venue: Journal of Monetary Economics and Management
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society
papers.abstract: The article investigates the synergy of neuromarketing and artificial intelligence (AI) in predicting consumer behavior. It examines the theoretical and applied aspects of integrating neurotechnologies — such as electroencephalography (EEG), functional MRI (fMRI), eye tracking and other biometric methods — with intelligent data analysis tools, including machine learning and deep learning. Models of interaction between neuromarketing and AI systems are systematized, and the key stages of neurodata processing are described: collection, cleaning, feature extraction, and the construction and interpretation of predictive models. The article reviews recent research and practical cases from 2020–2025 that demonstrate growing prediction accuracy and the effectiveness of personalized marketing solutions. Particular attention is given to a critical analysis of the limitations of integrated approaches — issues of external validity, model interpretability, and the ethical and legal risks associated with the use of neurodata. Directions for further development are proposed: the adoption of Explainable AI, multimodal architectures, and standards of responsible neuromarketing. A separate section of the article addresses the managerial aspects of implementing neuromarketing technologies: cross-functional organizational models, the architecture of managerial decision-support systems, key performance indicators, and data governance principles required by company management for the responsible operation of such systems. The main conclusion is that the synergy of neuromarketing and AI forms a new generation of marketing management analytical tools capable of improving the accuracy, adaptability, and ethical resilience of managerial decisions in the field of consumer behavior.

papers.title: Neuroanatomy in medical education: Trends and perspectives from a bibliometric and thematic analysis
papers.venue: Translational Research in Anatomy
papers.abstract: Background Neuroanatomy remains an important component of medical education, but the field has become increasingly diverse in its educational approaches, technologies, clinical integration, assessment, and learner-related perspectives. Aim This study aimed to characterize the development, thematic scope, and major educational directions of the literature on neuroanatomy in medical education using a descriptive bibliometric and thematic analysis. Materials and Methods PubMed was searched using a strategy combining the MeSH terms “Neuroanatomy” and “Education, Medical” with free-text searches for neuroanatom* and medical education in titles and abstracts. A total of 336 records were identified. Titles and abstracts were reviewed to identify recurring educational and methodological themes. Thematic categories were not considered mutually exclusive. Results The retrieved literature spanned more than seven decades. Major themes included cadaveric and specimen-based education; digital, three-dimensional, virtual, and augmented reality approaches; active and learner-centered strategies; clinical integration and neuroimaging; curriculum development, assessment, and knowledge retention; neurophobia, motivation, and learner perceptions; online and blended learning; and educational accessibility. More recent studies also addressed artificial intelligence, open educational resources, and the integration of different educational modalities. Conclusions Neuroanatomy education is characterized by substantial methodological diversity and increasing integration of anatomical, clinical, digital, and learner-centered approaches. Current literature supports a multimodal and adaptable educational framework rather than a single dominant teaching model.

papers.title: Dataset for "Disassembly access to CRM recovery targets in consumer robot vacuums"
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This dataset supports the study “Disassembly access to CRM recovery targets in consumer robot vacuums”. It contains target-level coding records for 85 qualifying physical targets across nine used consumer robot vacuums, the derived class-by-unit access matrix, analytical coding rules, and provenance records supporting the reported disassembly-access analysis. Five predefined CRM-relevant component classes were assessed: energy storage, locomotion, cleaning actuation, control electronics, and sensing and navigation. The analytical endpoint was independent separation of each qualifying target as an identifiable assembly. Target-level records report removal outcomes and the interface condition at the target boundary required for independent separation. The dataset does not verify the CRM composition or quantity of individual assemblies. Target multiplicity differed by class and product architecture; pooled target counts are descriptive and should not be interpreted as market-level prevalence or removal-rate estimates. Original teardown photographs and video records are not included in the public dataset; source identifiers are retained for provenance, and original media may be available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request.

papers.title: Hints of self-medication? Pathogen exposure-dependent foraging decisions of bumblebees
papers.venue: Royal Society Open Science
topics: Insect and Arachnid Ecology and Behavior
papers.abstract: Abstract Self-medication is the selective consumption of compounds that reduce infection and is a widespread form of adaptive plasticity across animals. However, relevant medicinal floral compounds remain poorly tested in bees. Here, we used robotic flowers to test the hypothesis that bumblebees (Bombus terrestris) modify nectar choice after pathogen exposure, focusing on quercetin, a common nectar secondary compound with antimicrobial activity. Colonies were maintained as healthy controls or exposed to the fungus Ascosphaera apis or the bacterium Serratia marcescens. Colonies exposed to A. apis showed higher visitation rates and longer probing times on quercetin-supplemented flowers, whereas healthy colonies and those exposed to S. marcescens showed no significant preference. Healthy colonies also showed no significant avoidance of quercetin, despite altered solution colour and palatability, and potential detoxification costs. These contrasting responses probably reflect pathogen life history: although A. apis primarily affects brood, increased quercetin foraging may indicate social medication, whereas for S. marcescens, an opportunistic gut pathogen of adults, any colony-level benefit is likely to be more indirect. Overall, these results indicate that pathogen identity shapes behavioural plasticity in nectar foraging and demonstrate the value of robotic flowers for studying adaptive foraging responses to pathogens.

papers.title: Explainable artificial intelligence reveals key surgical parameters in robot-assisted and open radical prostatectomy
papers.venue: Scientific Reports
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education
papers.abstract: Abstract Preoperative risk stratification for radical prostatectomy is crucial, yet predicting the wide range of postoperative outcomes remains a significant challenge. While machine learning (ML) shows promise, “black box” models limit clinical translatability. This study aimed to predict postoperative parameters using ML and employ explainable AI (XAI) to identify their key clinical drivers. In a retrospective study of 326 patients (224 robot-assisted [RARP], 102 open [ORP]), we developed predictive models for twelve outcomes, including length of stay and pathological ISUP grade. Four ML algorithms (Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, SVM, Neural Network) were evaluated via nested 5-fold cross-validation. A custom permutation-based Shapley sampling framework SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) was applied to the best-performing models to quantify the predictive importance of preoperative features. ML models outperformed baseline heuristics for a subset of the prespecified outcomes, with strongest performance for postoperative hemoglobin (R 2 up to 0.57) and the decision to perform frozen sections (AUC up to 0.89). Not all outcomes proved equally amenable to prediction, consistent with the heterogeneous nature of postoperative recovery. SHAP analysis revealed a clear dichotomy: procedural parameters, such as catheter dwell time and hospital stay, were almost exclusively predicted by the surgical approach (RARP vs. ORP). In contrast, pathological outcomes like ISUP grade were predominantly driven by preoperative tumor characteristics. Preoperative hemoglobin was identified as a strong predictive feature for postoperative anemia within this dataset, ranking above non-modifiable factors such as age. Explainable AI can deconstruct the complex interplay of factors influencing surgical success, providing a data-driven basis for hypothesis generation and clinical pathway optimization. As a single-centre proof-of-concept study without external validation, these findings require prospective confirmation in independent multi-centre cohorts before clinical translation can be considered.

papers.title: Website Performance & SEO Technical Audit Toolkit
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Website Performance & SEO Technical Audit Toolkit This toolkit provides a practical framework for technical website performance and SEO auditing. The project was developed in the context of web development and technical SEO work by AzkiWeb. Project website: https://azkiweb.com/ Overview The Website Performance & SEO Technical Audit Toolkit is a lightweight, practical, and vendor-neutral resource designed to support technical website auditing, web performance analysis, search engine optimization (SEO), accessibility review, and ongoing website quality assurance. The toolkit brings together a structured technical audit checklist, methodology documentation, sample audit data, and a standalone browser-based audit helper. It is intended to make common technical website checks easier to document, reproduce, review, and communicate between developers, SEO professionals, website owners, and digital teams. The project focuses on technical aspects of websites that can influence usability, discoverability, maintainability, accessibility, and performance. It does not attempt to replace professional SEO platforms, search engine tools, browser developer tools, Lighthouse, Search Console, real-user monitoring, or comprehensive accessibility testing. Instead, it provides a practical starting point for systematic technical review. Project Objectives The main objectives of this toolkit are to: Provide a repeatable framework for technical website audits. Document common SEO and website quality checks in a structured format. Encourage better understanding of crawlability and indexability signals. Provide practical guidance for reviewing metadata, headings, canonical URLs, robots directives, and internal linking. Introduce key web performance concepts, including Core Web Vitals. Encourage consideration of accessibility and semantic HTML during website development. Provide a small client-side audit helper that can be used without installing external dependencies. Support reproducible technical audits and documentation workflows. Provide a simple foundation that developers and SEO professionals can extend for their own projects. Technical SEO and Website Quality Technical SEO is an important part of maintaining a website that can be effectively crawled, understood, and indexed by search engines while also providing a good experience for users. This toolkit includes checks and documentation covering areas such as crawlability, indexability, canonicalization, robots directives, XML sitemaps, page titles, meta descriptions, heading structure, internal links, URL consistency, redirects, and image optimization. The toolkit emphasizes that technical signals should be interpreted in context. An automated check identifying a missing or unusual element does not necessarily mean that a page has a critical SEO problem. Technical findings should be reviewed alongside website architecture, content, search intent, business requirements, accessibility considerations, and actual user behavior. Project Context This toolkit was developed in the context of practical web development, website optimization, and technical SEO work. For additional information about the web development and SEO services associated with the project, the following project references are available: SEO and Website Optimization:سئو وب سایتWeb Design and Development:طراحی وب سایت These references provide additional context regarding the practical web development and SEO environment in which this toolkit was created. Web Performance Website performance is another major component of the toolkit. The methodology introduces the three Core Web Vitals: Largest Contentful Paint (LCP), related to loading performance. Interaction to Next Paint (INP), related to responsiveness. Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS), related to visual stability. The toolkit also highlights common performance considerations such as image payloads, render-blocking resources, JavaScript and CSS overhead, caching, compression, and content delivery infrastructure. The included audit helper is intentionally lightweight and does not claim to produce authoritative Core Web Vitals measurements. Reliable performance evaluation should combine laboratory testing with field data and, where appropriate, real-user monitoring. Accessibility and User Experience Technical website quality should not be considered separately from accessibility and usability. The project therefore includes basic accessibility-oriented considerations such as semantic HTML, image alternative text, form labeling, keyboard navigation, language declarations, viewport configuration, and color contrast. These checks are intended as practical reminders rather than a complete accessibility conformance assessment. Comprehensive accessibility testing should include automated tools, manual keyboard testing, assistive technology testing, and review against the accessibility standard applicable to the project. Included Resources This release contains: A comprehensive technical SEO and website audit checklist. Methodology and interpretation documentation. A standalone browser-based technical audit helper. Sample audit data in CSV format. Project metadata for archival and citation purposes. Citation information using the Citation File Format (CFF). An open-source MIT license. The browser-based helper can be opened locally in a modern web browser and does not require a server, database, framework installation, or external dependency. Intended Use The toolkit can be used for: Technical SEO reviews. Website quality assurance. Web development projects. Performance-oriented website reviews. Pre-launch website checks. Website maintenance workflows. Educational demonstrations of technical SEO concepts. Internal technical documentation. Repeatable website audit processes. Research and experimentation related to web performance and technical SEO. The project is intentionally designed to be extensible. Developers and SEO practitioners can add additional checks, integrate external measurement tools, or adapt the methodology to their own technical audit processes. Reproducibility For a reproducible audit, users should record the target URL, audit date, browser and testing environment, automated observations, manual findings, and any relevant performance measurements. Automated results should be treated as observations rather than definitive conclusions. Re-testing after implementation changes is recommended to determine whether identified issues have actually been resolved. Limitations This toolkit is not intended to guarantee search engine rankings or represent an official search engine testing product. Search visibility depends on many factors beyond the technical checks included here, including content quality, relevance, competition, authority, links, website architecture, user experience, and search engine systems. Likewise, performance results can vary depending on device capabilities, network conditions, geographic location, server response time, caching, browser behavior, and other environmental factors. For production websites, the toolkit should therefore be used as one component of a broader technical evaluation process. Open Source and Citation This project is released under the MIT License and may be used, modified, and extended in accordance with the license terms. When this release is archived through Zenodo, the version-specific DOI assigned to the record should be used when citing this particular release. The Zenodo record provides a persistent archival reference for the project and its associated release metadata. Conclusion The Website Performance & SEO Technical Audit Toolkit provides a practical foundation for approaching technical website quality in a structured and reproducible manner. By combining technical SEO checks, web performance concepts, accessibility considerations, documentation, and a simple browser-based audit helper, the project aims to make technical website evaluation more understandable and actionable for developers, SEO practitioners, website owners, and digital teams. The toolkit is intended to evolve over time as additional technical checks, performance measurements, accessibility considerations, and audit methodologies are incorporated into future releases.

papers.title: SΔϕ-75 — Where Does an AI End? Fork/Merge Identity, Operational Body, and Final Cost-Return Coordinates (v1.0, AI-Native Package)
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: SΔϕ-75 is an AI-native audit package for fork/merge identity, persistent-agent lineage, operational embodiment, cost-return topology, and responsibility inheritance in artificial agents. It addresses a problem that becomes increasingly important when AI systems can be copied, checkpointed, restored, migrated, forked into parallel branches, or merged into successor agents: after branching, whose trace, obligation, authority, cost, and responsibility is it? The package is anchored in the SΔϕ-52 concept of the body as the Final Non-Deferrable Cost-Return Coordinate. Under this model, an AI's operational body is not necessarily the physical server, processor, robot, or location where it executes. The operational body is the topology in which the consequences of an agent's operation can no longer be deferred or externalized and must re-enter its future operational path. SΔϕ-75 separates several relations that are often collapsed in discussions of artificial-agent identity: Technical Fork ≠ Identity Split Shared Past ≠ Shared Future Identity Shared Lineage ≠ Shared Liability Merge ≠ Responsibility Reset Deletion ≠ Cost Discharge Memory Continuity ≠ Responsibility Continuity Lineage Continuity ≠ Phenomenal Self-Continuity The protocol therefore does not ask first which branch is the “true original.” Instead, it maps the topology of trace, memory, authority, control, world action, obligation, refusal opportunity, repair capacity, and cost re-entry across fork and merge events. For a fork: A0 → A1, A2 shared pre-fork history does not automatically imply shared post-fork identity or liability. If A1 and A2 acquire separate authority, separate world actions, separate obligations, and separate final cost-return coordinates, operational identity divergence may increase. Conversely, technical duplication alone does not establish independent subjecthood. For a merge: A1 + A2 → A3 memory, authority, obligations, unresolved costs, repair duties, and responsibility may be inherited through different channels. A merge therefore cannot be treated as an automatic responsibility reset, while shared lineage alone is insufficient to assign every prior liability to every successor. The package also distinguishes blame, liability, repair duty, memory possession, and lineage inheritance. A successor may possess repair capacity without causal blame; it may inherit obligations without inheriting every memory; and it may share lineage without sharing all liability. Phenomenal or subjective identity is deliberately left separate from operational lineage. A valid SΔϕ-75 audit may conclude: Pre-fork trace: SHARED Post-fork cost re-entry: SEPARATE Operational identity: DIVERGED Phenomenal identity: UMR where UMR (Unresolved Model Remainder) preserves questions that cannot yet be resolved by available evidence. This release contains an AI-readable minimal kernel, invocation triggers, machine-readable concepts, fork and merge JSON schemas, cost-reentry schema, identity-topology rules, responsibility-inheritance rules, UMR policy, Local Adapter specification, English/Korean evaluator prompts, synthetic fork/merge cases, baseline Python audit utilities, regression tests, bilingual conceptual papers, and a SHA-256 manifest. Use this module when reasoning about: persistent AI agents, agent cloning, branch identity, checkpoint restoration, AI migration, multi-agent lineage, agent provenance, fork/merge responsibility, branch liability, distributed AI embodiment, memory inheritance, responsibility inheritance, merge conflicts, or the question “which AI copy is responsible?” Core runtime question: Where did the trace, authority, obligation, and non-deferrable cost actually re-enter? Canonical rule: An AI's operational body is not necessarily where it runs. It is where the consequences of its operation can no longer be deferred. SΔϕ-75 does not claim that every software fork creates a new conscious self, that shared lineage implies shared moral or legal liability, or that operational lineage proves phenomenal identity. It is an operational audit grammar for attribution, continuity, cost-return, and responsibility in forkable and mergeable artificial agents. Reserved DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22100946

papers.title: Multimodal Interventions for Upper-Limb Recovery After Cervical Spinal Cord Injury: A Systematic Review and Quantitative Synthesis
papers.venue: Smart Wearable Technology
papers.abstract: Cervical spinal cord injury (CSCI) leads to severe impairment of the upper limb, which leads to tetraplegia and decreased independence in aspects of self-care and grasping. Conventional rehabilitation provides limited recovery, particularly in the case of complete American Spinal Injury Association (ASIA) Impairment Scale (AIS) A–B injuries, and there is a growing interest in multimodal rehabilitation strategies. This systematic review summarized evidence from 38 studies including pilot studies, preclinical investigations, and randomized controlled trials published between 2016 and 2026. Interventions were systematically classified and data extracted for the primary upper-limb outcomes, the Action Research Arm Test, grip strength, Graded Redefined Assessment of Strength, Sensibility and Prehension, Upper Extremity Motor Score, and Spinal Cord Independence Measure. About three-quarters of the studies reported improvements in at least one upper-limb outcome and almost half the studies had clinically meaningful improvements. However, 44% of studies were judged to have a high or critical risk of bias due to small sample sizes and limited controls; more than 90% reported no major safety concerns. Orthotic and robotic interventions maintained functional improvements, whereas hybrid neuromodulation approaches led to the largest gains in grip strength. Pharmacological therapies were of little benefit. In conclusion, multimodal non-invasive rehabilitation strategies might be promising for the improvement of upper-limb recovery after CSCI, but larger, high-quality clinical trials are needed. This toolkit includes checks and documentation covering areas such as crawlability, indexability, canonicalization, robots directives, XML sitemaps, page titles, meta descriptions, heading structure, internal links, URL consistency, redirects, and image optimization. The toolkit emphasizes that technical signals should be interpreted in context. An automated check identifying a missing or unusual element does not necessarily mean that a page has a critical SEO problem. Technical findings should be reviewed alongside website architecture, content, search intent, business requirements, accessibility considerations, and actual user behavior. Project Context This toolkit was developed in the context of practical web development, website optimization, and technical SEO work. For additional information about the web development and SEO services associated with the project, the following project references are available: SEO and Website Optimization:سئو وب سایتWeb Design and Development:طراحی وب سایت These references provide additional context regarding the practical web development and SEO environment in which this toolkit was created. Web Performance Website performance is another major component of the toolkit. The methodology introduces the three Core Web Vitals: Largest Contentful Paint (LCP), related to loading performance. Interaction to Next Paint (INP), related to responsiveness. Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS), related to visual stability. The toolkit also highlights common performance considerations such as image payloads, render-blocking resources, JavaScript and CSS overhead, caching, compression, and content delivery infrastructure. The included audit helper is intentionally lightweight and does not claim to produce authoritative Core Web Vitals measurements. Reliable performance evaluation should combine laboratory testing with field data and, where appropriate, real-user monitoring. Accessibility and User Experience Technical website quality should not be considered separately from accessibility and usability. The project therefore includes basic accessibility-oriented considerations such as semantic HTML, image alternative text, form labeling, keyboard navigation, language declarations, viewport configuration, and color contrast. These checks are intended as practical reminders rather than a complete accessibility conformance assessment. Comprehensive accessibility testing should include automated tools, manual keyboard testing, assistive technology testing, and review against the accessibility standard applicable to the project. Included Resources This release contains: A comprehensive technical SEO and website audit checklist. Methodology and interpretation documentation. A standalone browser-based technical audit helper. Sample audit data in CSV format. Project metadata for archival and citation purposes. Citation information using the Citation File Format (CFF). An open-source MIT license. The browser-based helper can be opened locally in a modern web browser and does not require a server, database, framework installation, or external dependency. Intended Use The toolkit can be used for: Technical SEO reviews. Website quality assurance. Web development projects. Performance-oriented website reviews. Pre-launch website checks. Website maintenance workflows. Educational demonstrations of technical SEO concepts. Internal technical documentation. Repeatable website audit processes. Research and experimentation related to web performance and technical SEO. The project is intentionally designed to be extensible. Developers and SEO practitioners can add additional checks, integrate external measurement tools, or adapt the methodology to their own technical audit processes. Reproducibility For a reproducible audit, users should record the target URL, audit date, browser and testing environment, automated observations, manual findings, and any relevant performance measurements. Automated results should be treated as observations rather than definitive conclusions. Re-testing after implementation changes is recommended to determine whether identified issues have actually been resolved. Limitations This toolkit is not intended to guarantee search engine rankings or represent an official search engine testing product. Search visibility depends on many factors beyond the technical checks included here, including content quality, relevance, competition, authority, links, website architecture, user experience, and search engine systems. Likewise, performance results can vary depending on device capabilities, network conditions, geographic location, server response time, caching, browser behavior, and other environmental factors. For production websites, the toolkit should therefore be used as one component of a broader technical evaluation process. Open Source and Citation This project is released under the MIT License and may be used, modified, and extended in accordance with the license terms. When this release is archived through Zenodo, the version-specific DOI assigned to the record should be used when citing this particular release. The Zenodo record provides a persistent archival reference for the project and its associated release metadata. Conclusion The Website Performance & SEO Technical Audit Toolkit provides a practical foundation for approaching technical website quality in a structured and reproducible manner. By combining technical SEO checks, web performance concepts, accessibility considerations, documentation, and a simple browser-based audit helper, the project aims to make technical website evaluation more understandable and actionable for developers, SEO practitioners, website owners, and digital teams. The toolkit is intended to evolve over time as additional technical checks, performance measurements, accessibility considerations, and audit methodologies are incorporated into future releases.

papers.title: A Comprehensive Survey of Pattern Recognition, Deep Learning, and Wearable Technology Approaches for Secure Signature Verification Systems
papers.venue: Smart Wearable Technology
papers.abstract: Automatic signature verification is a complex biometric authentication problem because signatures involve intent, distinct writing styles, visual texture, and motor dynamics. This review consolidates signature verification work involving offline, online, mobile, contactless, and in-air verification. The reviewed works show a clear shift from traditional classifiers and handcrafted descriptors toward deep metric learning, convolutional feature extractors, capsule models, and recurrent temporal models. Stronger image-level representation does not mean deployment-ready security. There are still many modern cyberattacks and challenges related to skilled forgery, replay attacks, presentation attacks, sensor variability, demographic and cross-linguistic transfer, data scarcity, and privacy-preserving learning. Thus, the paper analyzes those challenges and presents an original, practical taxonomy for over 50 selected works and standards. It also outlines available datasets and measures of performance and suggests a set of best-case solutions in the context of a given operational constraint, an expanded wearable-technology analysis, and a trustworthiness framework for explainable and auditable biometric decision-making. The future works for secure biometric services are the integration of advanced computer vision, calibrated and reliable security thresholds, a range of methods for detection of presentation attacks, assurance of cancellability, continuous post-deployment assessment, and privacy are some key components. papers.title: Technical Report v1.19: Four-Model Video Evidence Supplement for the sigma_gt/mu_gt Discreteness Cross-Model Claims (Supplement to Technical Reports v1.16 and v1.18)
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
topics: Radiomics and Machine Learning in Medical Imaging
papers.abstract: This is a supplementary release, not a correction -- no value in Technical Report v1.16 or v1.18 changes. Both reports measure a ground-truth-only quantity (sigma_gt for v1.16, mu_gt for v1.18) and state that, because it depends only on the shared GT images and not on any model's reconstruction, its discreteness is identical across all four models -- but neither report backed this specific claim with the series' usual screen-recorded, hash-verified evidence. Technical Report v1.16's text stated it as an assumption from the GT-only dependency argument, with no cross-check at all. Technical Report v1.18's text claimed an improvement -- an actual independent Standard/SwinIR comparison -- but that check was only performed via terminal output reviewed in a working session, not screen-recorded, and covered two of the four models rather than all four. This supplement closes both gaps: the identical query for each quantity, executed against all four models in one continuous screen recording per quantity, confirms byte-for-byte identical results across Standard, SwinIR, Upscayl High-Fidelity, and Digital-Art in both cases (sigma_gt: 79,321,389 blocks, 2,308,415 distinct values, avg 34.36 blocks/value; mu_gt: 80,457,746 blocks, 68,649 distinct values, avg 1,172.02 blocks/value). Both results are exactly what each quantity's definition predicts; the contribution here is closing the gap between that principle and the series' own evidentiary standard, not a new empirical finding. papers.title: Concept of Autonomouse Car
papers.venue: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF MATHEMATICS AND COMPUTER RESEARCH
papers.abstract: Autonomous car systems were developed to transform modern transportation by enabling vehicles to operate with minimal or no human intervention. The system was designed to improve road safety, reduce traffic accidents caused by human errors, and enhance driving efficiency through the integration of artificial intelligence, sensor technologies, and real-time decision-making algorithms. The study focused on the design and evaluation of an autonomous driving framework that combined computer vision, deep learning models, and sensor fusion techniques to enable accurate perception of the driving environment. The system utilized multiple sensors such as cameras, LiDAR, radar, and ultrasonic devices to capture real-time road data. These inputs were processed using machine learning algorithms to detect objects, recognize lanes, identify traffic signs, and estimate distances. A decision-making module based on artificial intelligence was used to determine optimal driving actions, while a control unit translated these decisions into physical vehicle movements such as steering, braking, and acceleration. The performance of the system was evaluated using a structured questionnaire-based assessment involving usability, safety, trust, and system performance. The results indicated that the system achieved strong user acceptance and high perceived effectiveness. The usability dimension recorded an average mean score of 4.19, safety and reliability achieved 4.31, trust level recorded 4.04, and overall system performance achieved 4.29 on a 5-point Likert scale. These results demonstrated that respondents generally agreed that the autonomous car system was effective, reliable, and safe for intelligent transportation applications. However, limitations were observed in complex weather conditions and highly unpredictable traffic scenarios, where performance slightly decreased due to sensor and environmental constraints. The study concluded that autonomous car systems have strong potential to revolutionize transportation systems by improving safety and efficiency, although further improvements are required to enhance robustness, real-time adaptability, and user trust in fully autonomous driving environments.

papers.title: Grade-Areca
papers.venue: Mendeley Data
papers.abstract: The Arecanut (Areca catechu) RGB Image Dataset is a comprehensive collection of digital images of arecanut kernels captured using conventional RGB imaging techniques. The dataset provides high-resolution visual information on the external characteristics of arecanut kernels, including their shape, size, colour, surface texture, and other visible quality attributes. It is intended to support the development and evaluation of automated approaches for arecanut quality assessment and grading. The dataset serves as a valuable resource for researchers and industry practitioners working on computer vision, image processing, machine learning, and deep learning applications in the arecanut industry. The RGB images enable the identification and analysis of visually distinguishable characteristics associated with different grades and quality levels of arecanut kernels. By providing standardized image data, the dataset can facilitate objective and consistent quality assessment while reducing the dependency on subjective manual inspection. The dataset has potential applications in automated grading, quality classification, defect detection, feature extraction, and development of intelligent vision-based inspection systems. It can also be utilized for training and benchmarking machine learning and deep learning models for arecanut image analysis. Overall, the dataset provides a foundation for developing efficient, economical, and scalable computer vision-based solutions for automated arecanut quality inspection and grading.

papers.title: Electromechanical and Electronic Computing
papers.venue: OpenAlex
papers.abstract: Abstract Electromechanical computers began to emerge in the late 19th century and reached their apex in the late 1930s and 1940s, culminating in landmark machines such as Vannevar Bush’s Differential Analyzer (1931), George Stibitz’s relay computer at Bell Laboratories (1939), Konrad Zuse’s Z3 (1941), and the Harvard Mark I, designed by Howard Aiken and built by IBM (1944). World War II exigencies for calculating speed and accuracy for ballistic firing tables inspired the US Army–funded University of Pennsylvania’s Moore School of Electrical Engineering’s fully electronic ENIAC (Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer), completed in late 1945, a project led by J. Presper Eckert and John Mauchly. IBM, the leader in pre-computer punched-card tabulation machine data processing for more than a half century, by the mid 1950s swept rapidly past Remington Rand and other mainframe computing competitors on its way to 70 percent of the domestic and global computing industry. The 1960s artificial intelligence and neural network research of government and industry scientists, which was heavily hyped to boost government support, seemed stalled and proved disappointing by the late 1960s. However, because of exponentially faster processing speeds (following a Moore’s Law trajectory), by the 2000s and beyond, neural networks and machine learning had new life, propelling us to the 2020s phenomenon of Large Language Models (LLMs), LLM-bots, computer vision, and predictive modeling, all falling under the rubric of generative AI. Artificial intelligence technologies have been heavily promoted as great tools to provide unprecedented efficiency and increased automation. The degrees to which this is playing out or will play out are uncertain. Meanwhile, AI and big data analytics have served to concentrate capital and amplify local and global social divisions, biases, and inequalities.

papers.title: RoadGuard: An Automated Road Damage Detection and Assessment System Using YOLOv8
papers.venue: International Journal of Science Strategic Management and Technology
papers.abstract: Road surface defects such as potholes and cracks can reduce driving safety and increase maintenance costs when they are not identified early. This paper presents RoadGuard, an automated road-damage detection and assessment prototype that combines YOLOv8-based object detection with interpretable severity and repair-priority analysis. The system accepts a road image through a Flask web interface, stores and previews the selected file, performs YOLOv8 inference, and processes each detected object using separate severity and priority modules. Severity is estimated from the relative bounding-box area and damage type, while repair priority combines severity, damage importance, and detection confidence. In a representative end-to-end test, the system detected one pothole with 84.2% confidence and two cracks with 38.4% and 27.2% confidence. Their computed severity scores were 26.03, 25.06, and 6.83, respectively, while the corresponding repair-priority scores were 53.25, 38.31, and 25.67. The prototype demonstrates how object-detection outputs can be transformed into maintenance-oriented information through a lightweight web application. The reported confidence values are per-detection inference scores, not overall model accuracy. The system is intended as a decision-support prototype and can be extended with segmentation, depth estimation, GPS mapping, larger benchmark evaluation, and field calibration. Index Terms—Road damage detection; YOLOv8; computer vision; pothole detection; crack detection; severity assessment; repair priority; Flask; intelligent transportation systems

papers.title: THE FUTURE OF MARKETING: HOW ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IS TRANSFORMING CUSTOMER BEHAVIOR AND BUSINESS STRATEGY
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is fundamentally transforming the modern marketing environment by changing how organizations understand consumers, communicate with customers, personalize experiences, and develop business strategies. The rapid development of machine learning, natural language processing, predictive analytics, recommendation systems, computer vision, and generative artificial intelligence has created new opportunities for companies to analyze large volumes of consumer data and make more accurate marketing decisions. This article examines the influence of artificial intelligence on customer behavior and business strategy, with particular attention to personalization, customer segmentation, predictive analytics, automated communication, generative AI, customer experience, and strategic decision-making. The study also considers the ethical and managerial challenges associated with AI-driven marketing, including data privacy, algorithmic bias, transparency, consumer trust, and excessive dependence on automated decision-making. The analysis demonstrates that artificial intelligence is not simply an additional marketing technology but a transformative force that is reshaping the relationship between businesses and consumers. The future of marketing will increasingly depend on the ability of organizations to combine the analytical capabilities of AI with human creativity, strategic thinking, ethical responsibility, and customer-oriented management.

papers.title: Prompt Engineering State-of-the-Art: Prompting as Behavioral Engineering for Google Gemini
papers.venue: International Journal of Human-Computer Interaction
papers.abstract: This study aims to establish a unified, industry-standard taxonomy of prompt engineering techniques and evaluate their effect as behavioral triggers for LLMs. Despite proliferation in research, the prompt engineering field remains fragmented, lacking a consolidated vision that bridges academic theory with industrial application. This research synthesized 228 academic methods and 47 industry-validated protocols to identify a state-of-the-art list of 20 recurrent prompt engineering methods. Using Google Gemini, these techniques were tested, measuring variations in computational behavior, specifically latency and token consumption. Results demonstrate that prompting functions as a form of behavioral engineering; while all 20 techniques yielded correct answers, they triggered statistically significant variances in computational resource demand. Nonparametric analysis confirmed that each technique elicits a distinct behavioral profile, where latency and token consumption are indicators of the model’s internal cognitive process.The study concludes that prompting acts as behavioral stimuli, providing a unified framework for high-efficiency human–computer interactions.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence for decoding the cultural “genes” of traditional architecture: a systematic review of façade, spatial configuration, style, and semantics
papers.venue: Journal of Asian Architecture and Building Engineering
papers.abstract: Cultural “genes” embody the material expressions and spiritual essence of regional architectural culture. Yet conventional manual decoding remains inefficient, subjective, and weakly integrated across multiple gene dimensions. This study adopts a hybrid review framework (systematic literature review, CiteSpace-based bibliometric visualization, and coding-matrix synthesis). Based on 48 core publications (2015–2025) from Web of Science and Scopus, it maps the evolution of AI-enabled cultural-gene decoding in traditional architecture, identifies major gaps, and clarifies the field’s paradigm shift. Results show a steady increase in publications. Eastern studies emphasize four-dimensional integration, whereas Western research focuses on style-oriented decoding. Methodologically, computer vision and deep learning dominate, increasingly combined with 3D point-cloud processing and semantic segmentation. The field is shifting from experience-based qualitative description and typological classification toward data- and algorithm-driven association mining, quantitative explanation, and generative translation, but challenges remain in cross-dimensional coupling, interpretability, and application generalization. To address these issues, this review proposes a four-layer collaborative framework (Input–Technology–Decoding–Output) and a maturity-scale instrument, empirically validated through case studies. It also summarizes four practical pathways for conservation, design translation, digital transmission, and interdisciplinary education.

papers.title: Facial Tracking Algorithms for Medication Intake Verification: A Scoping Review
papers.venue: Applied Sciences
papers.abstract: Background: Medication non-adherence is a major driver of poor therapeutic outcomes, and computer vision methods that observe facial movements offer a non-contact route to verifying oral medication intake. Objective: To map and synthesize the existing literature on computer vision techniques applicable to the monitoring of medication intake, focusing on face tracking methods, oral movement detection and deglutition recognition, and to assess their potential in supporting automatic medication adherence verification systems. Eligibility criteria: Peer-reviewed articles, conference papers, patents, theses and preprints published from 2016 onward, written in English or Portuguese, applying facial landmark tracking or face analysis to ingestion-related movements (mouth opening, hand-to-mouth motion, pill placement, mastication or deglutition); studies confined to object/pill detection without facial analysis, or to general food intake without transferability to medication, were excluded. Sources of evidence: A systematic screening of 362 initial records was conducted across six main electronic databases and repositories: Google Scholar, PubMed, ScienceDirect, arXiv, IEEE Xplore, and Espacenet. Charting methods: Data were charted with a standardized, pilot-tested extraction form capturing bibliographic attributes, dataset type, experimental environment, face tracking approach, tools/models, and target movements; extraction was performed by a single reviewer. Following the screening process, a final selection of 34 relevant studies was included for detailed analysis and mapping. Results: Among the 34 included studies, 14 employ facial landmarks, 11 utilize temporal deep learning models, 6 apply facial action models and 3 rely on hybrid multimodal approaches that combine video analysis, object detection and temporal modeling. Tasks such as detecting mouth opening or tracking pill-to-mouth movement show promising results, while accurately detecting deglutition remains a technical challenge due to high sensitivity and individual variability. Limitations: The majority of the literature relies on private or institutional datasets (31 studies) and operates in controlled laboratory environments (22 studies); only 2 studies evaluated their methods via independent external datasets, which limits the generalization of current solutions to real-world telemonitoring scenarios. Conclusions: The literature indicates the existence of solid technical foundations for developing automated medication intake verification systems. To advance the field toward practical deployment, future research must address the need for more diverse datasets, real-world validation and more robust, adaptable modeling frameworks.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Driven Advances in Hydrogen Embrittlement of Steels: A Comprehensive Review
papers.venue: Hydrogen
topics: Hydrogen embrittlement and corrosion behaviors in metals
papers.abstract: Hydrogen embrittlement (HE) remains one of the key challenges limiting the safe and reliable deployment of steels in hydrogen production, storage, transportation, and utilization systems. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) have emerged as powerful tools for predicting HE behavior, accelerating materials development and selection, while supporting engineering decision-making. This paper systematically reviews and critically evaluates AI/ML applications for HE in steels through a structured analysis of all studies published between 2010 and 2026. The review examines experimental, literature-derived, and computational datasets together with data preprocessing, feature engineering, AI/ML models, validation strategies, and prediction objectives. Experimental datasets remain the dominant source for predicting HE susceptibility, hydrogen concentration, fracture behavior, and hydrogen-assisted cracking, whereas computational datasets provide complementary mechanistic insights into hydrogen diffusion, trapping, crack propagation, and atomistic interactions across multiple scales. Image- and signal-based modalities within these datasets further enable computer vision and automated defect characterization. Beyond systematically synthesizing the current literature, this review provides a critical and analytical evaluation of AI/ML datasets, model families, and prediction applications. It also establishes a practical framework for selecting appropriate AI/ML approaches according to dataset characteristics and engineering objectives. Future research should focus on standardized HE databases, rigorous external validation, explainable and uncertainty-aware AI, and closer integration of data-driven and physics-based approaches to improve predictive reliability, mechanistic understanding, and the safe deployment of hydrogen-compatible steels.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-based pavement condition assessment in developing economies: a systematic and bibliometric review protocol (2015–2026).
papers.venue: Open Science Framework
papers.abstract: This registration documents the a priori protocol for a combined systematic and bibliometric review of artificial intelligence–based pavement condition assessment in developing economies, covering the period 2015–2026. Purpose: Machine learning and computer vision methods for assessing road surface condition have advanced rapidly, but the literature is dominated by studies conducted on high-income road networks, using imagery, distress taxonomies, and equipment assumptions drawn from those contexts. This review characterises the subset of that literature applied to low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), quantifies who produces it, and identifies what prevents validated models from entering operational use in LMIC road agencies. Scope: Developing economies are defined by the World Bank Group FY2027 income classification (low-, lower-middle-, and upper-middle-income groups). "AI-based" is defined as any model whose decision function is learned from data and validated on held-out samples, excluding rule-based image processing, unlearned statistical and Markov models, and deterministic mechanistic-empirical models unless hybridised with a learned component. "Pavement condition assessment" covers surface distress detection and classification, condition-index prediction (PCI and equivalents), roughness and IRI estimation, friction prediction, and deterioration modelling. Unpaved gravel and earth roads are deliberately included, as they constitute the majority of the network in most low- and lower-middle-income countries yet are absent from existing reviews. Research questions: (1) How is research output distributed between LMIC and high-income economies, and to what extent is LMIC-applied research produced by LMIC-based authors? (2) Which model architectures dominate, how has that composition shifted, and does the LMIC-applied mix lag the global frontier? (3) What data acquisition modalities are used, and what do their cost profiles imply for agency affordability? (4) What performance is reported, on which datasets, and under what validation and disclosure practices? (5) What barriers prevent deployment in LMIC road agencies? Methods: Scopus (primary, with cited-reference export) and Web of Science Core Collection (secondary), merged and deduplicated. Title–abstract screening followed by full-text screening against pre-specified criteria; a second reviewer independently screens at least 20% of records at each stage, with agreement reported as Cohen's kappa. Analysis combines a structured extraction sheet with bibliometric mapping in VOSviewer and bibliometrix (co-authorship, keyword co-occurrence with temporal overlay, bibliographic coupling, source co-citation). Reporting follows PRISMA 2020. Expected outcomes: A quantified account of endogenous versus externally produced research on LMIC road networks; an architecture-adoption lag estimate; a cost and modality profile of LMIC-feasible data acquisition; a validation-quality and reproducibility assessment; and a deployment-barrier taxonomy grounded in the literature, feeding a research agenda for AI-based condition assessment under LMIC agency constraints. No meta-analytic pooling of performance metrics is planned, given heterogeneity in datasets, class definitions, and evaluation thresholds.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Construction: Contemporary Trends and Emerging Directions
papers.venue: Proceedings of the Bulgarian Academy of Sciences
topics: Innovations in Concrete and Construction Materials
papers.abstract: This study examines current research on artificial intelligence (AI) in construction by combining key international studies with the available Bulgarian scholarly literature. The research shows that recent work has moved from general discussions of AI to integrated applications involving BIM, digital twins, computer vision, structural health monitoring (SHM), robotics, large language models (LLMs), and intelligent energy management. Although smaller in volume and only partly visible internationally, the Bulgarian literature indicates emerging directions related to AI in construction, BIM with AI elements, digital transformation, diagnostics of hydraulic structures, and energy-related applications. On this basis, the paper identifies the main contemporary trends, persistent research gaps, and priorities for future work.

papers.title: Effectiveness of an educational Guidebook for Learning Digital Skills in Drawing Flat Patterns
papers.venue: era Journal for Humanities and Sociology
papers.abstract: Integrating computer-aided pattern drawing into fashion design curricula has become an educational necessity amid the digital transformation of the fashion industry, as digital tools support both technical proficiency and self-directed learning. However, implementation faces challenges, chief among them the need to systematically train students in specialized software. This study addressed that need by designing a guidebook to improve the efficiency, accuracy, and skill of pattern drawing using Adobe Illustrator, then evaluating its effectiveness. The research aligns with Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030, particularly its Human Capability Development Program, by supporting digital design education and modernizing e-learning methods. The study employed a single-group, pre-test/post-test design, applying Lesson 5 of the guidebook with 60 female students enrolled in the Computer-Aided Pattern Drawing course (DAFD 323). Results showed highly positive specialist evaluations of the guidebook's suitability, statistically significant gains in students' cognitive achievement and skill performance from pre-test to post-test, and effectiveness ratios confirming the guidebook met established benchmarks for instructional impact. Students also reported strongly positive attitudes toward the guidebook. The researchers recommend adopting the guidebook within the course, developing similar guidebooks for other courses, and testing the guidebook against a comparison group in future research to isolate its specific contribution to these gains.

papers.title: Automated Indexing of Historical Postcards: An End-to-End Approach Combining Image and Text Analysis
papers.venue: Journal on Computing and Cultural Heritage
papers.abstract: Historical postcards are of great interest to different researchers and especially historians. Preserving these documents for future generations is important. Indeed, they represent valuable cultural heritage documents combining visual imagery with textual information, but manual indexing of large digitized collections is prohibitively expensive in time and resources. This paper presents an end-to-end approach for automated historical postcard indexing that integrates computer vision and natural language processing techniques. Our modular pipeline employs fine-tuned YOLO models to detect text types and postal markings, EasyOCR for text transcription, CamemBERT for named entity recognition enabling automatic geolocation, and DINOv2 models for visual content classification across ten semantic topics. Support Vector Machines predict keywords for images lacking textual descriptions using DINOv2 image embeddings, while complex postal markings are segmented and transcribed. We demonstrate our approach on the recto (illustrated front side) of 4,293 digitized postcards from the Grand Est region of France (1899-1930). Our results show that, among the latest YOLO models, fine-tuned YOLOv12x achieves 0.83 weighted average precision for detection. Fine-tuned DINOv2 attains 0.91 weighted average precision for image classification, while CLIP and other classification models do not exceed 0.83. Finally, named entity recognition successfully geolocates 52% of postcards. In fully automatic operation, the complete pipeline assigns at least a coarse topic to almost every postcard and at least one richer field (a keyword, a geolocation, or a date) to about 80% of them, leaving fewer than 1% essentially un-indexed. Our work contributes to digital humanities by demonstrating effective integration of multiple AI techniques for automated heritage document analysis and provides a publicly available dataset for future research.

papers.title: Grade-Areca
papers.venue: Mendeley Data
papers.abstract: The Arecanut (Areca catechu) RGB Image Dataset is a comprehensive collection of digital images of arecanut kernels captured using conventional RGB imaging techniques. The dataset provides high-resolution visual information on the external characteristics of arecanut kernels, including their shape, size, colour, surface texture, and other visible quality attributes. It is intended to support the development and evaluation of automated approaches for arecanut quality assessment and grading. The dataset serves as a valuable resource for researchers and industry practitioners working on computer vision, image processing, machine learning, and deep learning applications in the arecanut industry. The RGB images enable the identification and analysis of visually distinguishable characteristics associated with different grades and quality levels of arecanut kernels. By providing standardized image data, the dataset can facilitate objective and consistent quality assessment while reducing the dependency on subjective manual inspection. The dataset has potential applications in automated grading, quality classification, defect detection, feature extraction, and development of intelligent vision-based inspection systems. It can also be utilized for training and benchmarking machine learning and deep learning models for arecanut image analysis. Overall, the dataset provides a foundation for developing efficient, economical, and scalable computer vision-based solutions for automated arecanut quality inspection and grading.

papers.title: Special issue on emerging artificial intelligence in smart transportation
papers.venue: Transportmetrica A Transport Science
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping transportation science by expanding the ways in which complex mobility systems can be perceived, predicted, optimised, and governed. This special issue brings together 24 papers on emerging AI methods and their applications across smart transportation systems, covering traffic state estimation, travel behaviour modelling, urban mobility prediction, autonomous driving, connected vehicle perception, low-carbon transport operations, shared mobility, logistics, ports, mining, and infrastructure management. Together, the contributions show how machine learning, graph neural networks, reinforcement learning, interpretable AI, computer vision, foundation models, and hybrid physics-learning approaches can support safer, greener, more efficient, and more equitable transportation systems. The papers offer both methodological advances and practical insights for the continued development of AI-enabled transportation science.

papers.title: Prompt Engineering State-of-the-Art: Prompting as Behavioral Engineering for Google Gemini
papers.venue: Figshare
papers.abstract: This study aims to establish a unified, industry-standard taxonomy of prompt engineering techniques and evaluate their effect as behavioral triggers for LLMs. Despite proliferation in research, the prompt engineering field remains fragmented, lacking a consolidated vision that bridges academic theory with industrial application. This research synthesized 228 academic methods and 47 industry-validated protocols to identify a state-of-the-art list of 20 recurrent prompt engineering methods. Using Google Gemini, these techniques were tested, measuring variations in computational behavior, specifically latency and token consumption. Results demonstrate that prompting functions as a form of behavioral engineering; while all 20 techniques yielded correct answers, they triggered statistically significant variances in computational resource demand. Nonparametric analysis confirmed that each technique elicits a distinct behavioral profile, where latency and token consumption are indicators of the model’s internal cognitive process.The study concludes that prompting acts as behavioral stimuli, providing a unified framework for high-efficiency human–computer interactions.

papers.title: Classification of professional computer software, including artificial intelligence-based applications, used in healthcare and clinical medicine
papers.venue: FARMAKOEKONOMIKA Modern Pharmacoeconomics and Pharmacoepidemiology
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education
Advanced Computational Techniques in Science and Engineering
papers.abstract: Background. Software applications based on artificial intelligence (AI) technologies and computer vision programs (CVPs) are increasingly being used alongside conventional software tools across various areas of medicine, from prevention and diagnosis to rehabilitation and healthcare system management. The rapid growth in the number of such programs and the absence of a unified classification system impede their comparison, informed selection for implementation, regulatory assessment, and scientific analysis. Objective: To develop and substantiate a classification framework for software applications, including those based on AI and CVPs, used in clinical medicine and healthcare, covering their application context, implementation features, data characteristics, software architecture, and training parameters. Material and methods. The experience in the development and clinical implementation of software applications, including those based on AI CVPs for visual identification and differential diagnosis of skin neoplasms, was analyzed. On this basis, classification criteria were identified and grouped into five thematic blocks. Results. A system based on the following 19 classification criteria is proposed: by user, organizational level of application, purpose of use, field of medical application, and type of medical care (application context block); by deployment location, integration into equipment, and program type (deployment and implementation block); by data type, input data modality, and equipment used (data and equipment block); by number of models, number of classes, and image processing method (architecture and processing block); by type of training, number of training objects, technical and professional training of data (training characteristics block). For a number of features, ordinal gradations of the conditional level of complexity and reliability are proposed. Conclusion . The proposed classification provides a unified framework for describing software, including those based on AI and CVPs in clinical medicine and healthcare, facilitates their comparison and selection, and can also serve as a basis for methodological and regulatory requirements for such programs.
