papers.title: Mapping the Integration of Adaptive Learning and Learning Analytics in Education: A Bibliometric Study (2004 – 2025)
papers.venue: e-Jurnal Penyelidikan dan Inovasi
topics: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning
papers.abstract: This study presents a bibliometric analysis of research on the integration of adaptive learning and learning analytics in education from 2004 to 2025, based on 1,850 publications. Using publication and citation analysis, collaboration networks, keyword co-occurrence, and thematic evolution analysis, the study examines the development of this research area, its main contributors, research themes, and patterns of growth. The findings show a steady increase in publications and citation impact, reflecting growing interest in data-driven approaches and the increasing use of artificial intelligence in education. However, the high proportion of conference papers and the relatively small number of review studies suggest that this area is still developing, with rapid growth occurring faster than the development of a more structured knowledge base. Citation and authorship analysis indicates that research influence is concentrated among a relatively small group of active authors and institutions, while collaboration patterns highlight the strong role of the United States alongside increasing but uneven international participation. Thematic evolution analysis shows a shift from early research on intelligent tutoring systems and student modelling to more data-focused and learner-centred approaches, including learning analytics, machine learning, and Bayesian modelling, with growing attention in recent studies to multimodal learning analytics and explainable artificial intelligence. Overall, adaptive learning and learning analytics form an increasingly connected and interdisciplinary research area in education, although knowledge production remains concentrated in specific regions and research groups, indicating the need for broader collaboration and further theoretical development.

papers.title: ML and DL techniques to detect cyberattacks on multimodal databases
papers.venue: OpenAlex
papers.abstract: The increasing trend in multimodal databases in the Internet of Multimedia Things (IoMT) poses distinct cybersecurity vulnerabilities as multimodal systems combine text, image, audio, video, and sensor information. Conventional security tools are not effective at identifying advanced attacks, such as deepfakes, data poisoning, and cross-modal manipulations. This chapter discusses the use of machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) to identify cyber threats within this type of environment. CNNs, RNNs, Transformers, autoencoders, and generative models are discussed as well as supervised, unsupervised, and semi-supervised models with attack detection in specific modalities and in cross-modality. Strategies of data fusion and cross-modality consistency checks contribute to a high level of robustness, whereas accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score are used as evaluation measures to demonstrate the effectiveness. This chapter ends with a list of challenges, future research, and practical implementations in healthcare, smart cities, industrial IoT, and financial systems.

papers.title: Metode GASING Berbasis Multimodalitas untuk Meningkatkan Kemampuan Berhitung Perkalian Siswa Sekolah Dasar
papers.venue: Jurnal Pendidikan Dasar Flobamorata
papers.abstract: Abstrak: Kemampuan berhitung operasi perkalian merupakan kompetensi dasar yang perlu dikuasai siswa sekolah dasar karena menjadi fondasi bagi pemahaman konsep matematika yang lebih kompleks, namun pembelajaran perkalian masih sering dilakukan melalui hafalan dan latihan mekanistis sehingga siswa belum sepenuhnya memahami makna perkalian secara konseptual. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis peningkatan kemampuan berhitung operasi perkalian siswa kelas IV sekolah dasar melalui metode GASING berbasis pendekatan multimodalitas. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain pre-experimental one-group time-series pretest-posttest pada 103 siswa kelas IV dari lima sekolah dasar negeri di salah satu kabupaten di Provinsi Jambi yang dipilih melalui teknik purposive sampling. Data dikumpulkan melalui tes kemampuan berhitung operasi perkalian pada tiga sesi sebelum perlakuan dan tiga sesi setelah perlakuan, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan statistik deskriptif, uji beda berpasangan, N-Gain ternormalisasi, dan ukuran efek. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan peningkatan rata-rata skor yang signifikan dari pre-test ke post-test (selisih rata-rata 26,69 poin; p < 0,001), dengan tingkat peningkatan kategori sedang (N-Gain = 0,586) dan besar perubahan praktis yang sangat besar (Cohen’s d = 1,819). Temuan ini mengindikasikan bahwa pembelajaran perkalian yang memadukan tahapan GASING dengan berbagai moda belajar konkret, visual, verbal, kinestetik, dan simbolik dapat menjadi alternatif strategi yang membantu guru sekolah dasar merancang pembelajaran perkalian secara lebih konkret, bertahap, dan bermakna, sekaligus memberi dasar empiris bagi pengembangan media dan pelatihan guru. Hasil penelitian tetap perlu ditafsirkan secara hati-hati karena desain penelitian tidak melibatkan kelompok kontrol. Abstract: Multiplication skills are fundamental competencies that elementary school students need to master because they support the understanding of more complex mathematical concepts, yet multiplication learning is often conducted through memorization and mechanical drills, which may limit students’ conceptual understanding. This study aimed to analyze the improvement of fourth-grade students’ multiplication skills through the GASING method based on a multimodality approach. This study employed a quantitative approach with a pre-experimental one-group time-series pretest-posttest design involving 103 fourth-grade students from five public elementary schools in a district in Jambi Province, selected using purposive sampling. Data were collected using a multiplication skills test administered in three pre-treatment sessions and three post-treatment sessions, then analyzed using descriptive statistics, paired-difference tests, normalized N-Gain, and effect size. The results showed a significant increase in the mean score from pre-test to post-test (mean difference of 26.69 points; p < .001), with a moderate level of improvement (N-Gain = 0.586) and a very large practical change (Cohen’s d = 1.819). These findings indicate that multiplication learning that integrates the stages of the GASING method with concrete, visual, verbal, kinesthetic, and symbolic modes can serve as an alternative strategy that helps elementary teachers design multiplication instruction that is more concrete, gradual, and meaningful, while also providing an empirical basis for developing learning media and teacher training. The findings should still be interpreted cautiously because this study did not include a control group.

papers.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN DIGITAL BANKING: APPLICATIONS AND IMPLICATIONS FOR LABOR TRANSFORMATION
papers.venue: Tạp chí Khoa học Đại học Công Thương.
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society
papers.abstract: The research examines the primary applications of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in digital banking and evaluates their impact on labor market dynamics within the banking industry. The research combines bibliometric analysis using RStudio and VOSviewer, along with qualitative synthesis and content analysis. The results show a significant increase in research on AI and its impact on the banking workforce since 2019, with participation from many countries in both developed and emerging economies, including Vietnam. Furthermore, AI applications focus on three main technology groups: (i) machine learning, including supervised, unsupervised, and deep learning, used in fraud detection, credit risk prediction, and customer behavior analysis; (ii) chatbots and virtual assistants based on natural language processing that support customer service and text data processing; and (iii) robotic process automation (RPA) combined with AI and computer vision for document verification, identity authentication, and workflow management. The study also indicates that AI is driving a skill polarization trend in the banking industry, with a decrease in demand for routine tasks and an increase in demand for high-skill positions, such as data analysts, AI engineers, and cybersecurity specialists. At the same time, digital transformation requires skill restructuring through upskilling and reskilling programs to develop hybrid capabilities in finance, technology, and data. Therefore, the research recommends that banks strengthen digital skills training and assess the labor implications of AI deployment, while recommending policies to support workforce retraining and promote public-private partnerships to ensure sustainable labor transformation in the banking industry.

papers.title: Active Robot Learning from Demonstrations with Human Teachers
papers.venue: OpenAlex
papers.abstract: Learning from Demonstrations (LfD) enables robots to acquire new skills by imitating a domain expert, most commonly a human. In practice, however, human demonstrations are typically available only under a limited budget and rarely cover the full range of situations a robot may encounter. This limitation often induces a distribution shift between the states represented in offline demonstrations and those visited by the robot during online exploration, which can substantially degrade performance. Interactive Imitation Learning (IIL) mitigates this shift by keeping the human teachers in the learning loop, allowing them to provide online input such as feedback and corrections. Yet these benefits come at the cost of sustained human supervision and can be undermined by noise, inconsistency, and errors in human teaching. This thesis investigates Active Learning from Demonstrations (Active LfD) as a principled approach to reduce distribution shift while accounting for human factors in realistic human-in-the-loop settings. In Active LfD, the robot learner does not passively consume demonstrations. Instead, it optimizes its query decisions to selectively request demonstrations from a human teacher. By determining when and what to query, the learner aims to reduce reliance on continuous monitoring, focus human effort where it is most beneficial, and limit the impact of suboptimal human teaching decisions. The thesis is organized into three parts. In Part I, I lay the foundation for how a robot learner can actively shape human teaching by revisiting conventional offline LfD through the lens of demonstration distributions. After identifying biased human teaching strategies under unguided conditions, I develop an Active LfD algorithm that operates with offline demonstrations and guides the resulting demonstration distribution toward a more balanced one, or more generally toward any specified target distribution, so as to improve robot learning. Importantly, however, a ``balanced'' distribution (e.g., a uniform distribution used as a default) is not necessarily optimal for learning. The most beneficial demonstration distribution depends on the robot’s evolving policy and its online exploration, and is therefore difficult to specify a priori. To address this coupling, I present a second Active LfD algorithm that leverages online demonstrations, iteratively deciding both the timing and content of queries as learning progresses in order to optimize the demonstration distribution for the learner. In Part II, I explore how Active LfD extends to more realistic and complex scenarios of learning from human teachers. I first extend the paradigm to transfer learning for complex manipulation tasks, spanning a range of policy transfer scenarios. I then consider the practical case of non-expert human teachers, who may provide imperfect demonstrations relative to the task objective. To accommodate imperfect teaching, I develop an Active LfD framework that optimizes the query sequence by jointly accounting for both the expected improvement in the robot’s policy induced by a query and the teacher’s capability to provide informative guidance in the queried region. Part III closes the loop of human-robot interactive learning by examining how robot query design influences human teaching beyond user experience alone. I leverage Curriculum Learning to design an Active LfD algorithm that benefits both robot learning and human teaching, encouraging a reciprocal loop between the robot learner and the human teacher.

papers.title: BeyondMimic: From motion tracking to versatile humanoid control via guided diffusion
papers.venue: Science Robotics
papers.abstract: The humanlike form of humanoid robots uniquely positions them to achieve the agility and versatility in motor skills that humans have. Learning from human demonstrations offers a scalable approach to acquiring these capabilities. However, prior works either produced unnatural motions or relied on motion-specific tuning to achieve satisfactory naturalness. Furthermore, these methods are often motion or goal specific, lacking the versatility to compose diverse skills, especially when solving unseen tasks. We present BeyondMimic, a framework that scales to diverse motions and carries the versatility to compose them seamlessly in tackling unseen downstream tasks. A compact motion tracking formulation enables mastery of a wide range of highly agile behaviors, including aerial cartwheels, spin kicks, flip kicks, and sprinting, with a single setup and shared hyperparameters, all while achieving humanlike performance. Moving beyond the mere imitation of existing motions, we propose a unified latent diffusion model that empowers versatile goal specification, seamless task switching, and dynamic composition of these agile behaviors. Leveraging classifier guidance, a diffusion-specific technique for test-time optimization toward unseen objectives, our model extended its capability to solve downstream tasks never encountered during training, including motion inpainting, joystick teleoperation, and obstacle avoidance, and transferred these skills zero-shot to real hardware. Together, these components enable scalable acquisition of humanlike motor skills from human motion and motion synthesis that generalizes and adapts beyond the training setup.

papers.title: Polymer-inspired mechanical metamaterials
papers.venue: Nature Communications
papers.abstract: Metamaterials benefit from unique architected patterns to achieve lightweight with exceptional mechanical properties inaccessible to conventional materials. Typical mechanical metamaterials are inspired by crystal-like lattice structures, whose closely packed frameworks often exhibit a rigid mechanical nature. Here, we present polymer-inspired metamaterials (PIMs) by programming deformation and strengthening mechanisms that mimic the mechanical roles of key constituent elements in polymer networks. By combining metamaterial programmability with polymer-inspired structures, we design crosslinking, proto-crystalline order, and entanglement in PIMs to enable macroscale strengthening mechanisms inspired by crosslink, molecular-density, and pre-stretch strengthening in polymers, expanding the metamaterial structure-property design space. This macroscale polymer-inspired programmability also suggests that PIMs could serve as a design platform incorporating the programmability strategies to achieve desired deformation and strengthening responses, holding a potential for applications in soft robotic joints and compliant connectors.

papers.title: Computational analysis of Wikipedia editorial activity during the 2024 European Parliament election
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This record contains the complete, reproducible pipeline behind the computational analysis of Wikipedia editorial activity around the 2024 European Parliament election, together with the analysis-ready corpus it produces and the full set of figures it generates. It supersedes version 1, which contained only the English policy-shortcut allowlist and a README. Scope: 31 Wikipedia language editions, the 24 official languages of the European Union plus Catalan, Basque, Galician, Russian, Turkish, Arabic and Chinese, covering the pages of MEP candidates, national and European parties, and political groups. The observation window opens with the announcement of the election (23 May 2023), spans the campaign (6 February - 9 June 2024) and closes with the formation of the new mandate (1 December 2024). The analysis measures article and talk-page revisions, editors and editor activity tiers, reverts and vandalism, attention (pageviews), the vocabulary of the debate, and, the central question, how editors invoke Wikipedia's own content and conduct policies and guidelines when they moderate. Project: This work is part of DEM-Debate: Building an Enabling Environment for DEMocratic Debate, an 18-month participatory research project (September 2024 – February 2026) run by Wikimedia Europe, the University of Amsterdam (Institute for Information Law, IViR) and Eurecat, Centre Tecnològic de Catalunya, together with the Wikimedia communities in Europe. The project combines a legal and a computational analysis of the fact-checking and content-moderation practices Wikipedia used during the 2024 European Parliament election, and asks whether they can inform future EU policy on election disinformation. This deposit is the computational strand of that work, carried out at Eurecat. Contents: dem-debate-code-v2.zip. The pipeline: an eight-stage extraction and preprocessing library (demdebate/), one analysis module per figure group (analysis/), 60 tests, thin notebooks, and the exact pinned environment (pyproject.toml, uv.lock, Python 3.12, managed with uv). It also ships the small derived data needed for a quick start: policy-shortcut allowlist snapshots for 12 editions (the material published in version 1), an ISO stopword list, page-to-country and page-to-European-party maps, and page-level gender data from Wikidata. figures-*.zip contains every figure produced by the analysis, one archive per module (revisions, users, vandalism, attention, words, policies, moderation, expanded moderation), each covering all 31 editions. The remaining files are the corpus, deposited in full so that every stage boundary is archived rather than only the analysis-ready layer: the master page table before and after the Wikidata gender enrichment; article and talk-page revisions with word-level diffs, both as extracted and with the cross-language page identifiers added; editor metadata; the merged, labelled and cleaned per-language datasets the figures are computed from; and the policy-citation occurrences and counts, together with the shortcut allowlists generated for the 19 editions that had no published snapshot. Two pairs are deliberately redundant, wikipedia_pages_extraction_w_gender.csv adds a single gender column to wikipedia_pages_extraction.csv, and revisions_by_lang_2 adds lang and local_id to revisions_by_lang, so that the output of each stage can be inspected exactly as the next stage received it. Reproducing from scratch: The code archive is self-contained. Install with uv sync --locked, check with make tests, and run the whole workflow with make reproduce. Stages 1–6 query the public Wikimedia APIs: over the full language set they take days, not hours, and download several GB. The pipeline is deliberately serial, in line with the Wikimedia robot policy; please identify your run by setting DEMDEBATE_USER_AGENT to a string containing a contact address. Provenance. Because extraction reads the live APIs, a fresh run reflects Wikipedia as it stands at run time and cannot recreate a past state. The corpus deposited here is the August 2026 snapshot, and it is the one the deposited figures were computed from, which is why the data is archived alongside the code rather than left to be regenerated. Licensing. this deposit may not be used for commercial purposes Three licenses apply, one per kind of material. Source code: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0. Figures, README and documentation: CC BY-NC 4.0. Data derived from Wikipedia: CC BY-SA 4.0. The data is the one part that is not noncommercial, and that is not a choice this deposit makes: Wikipedia content is published under CC BY-SA 4.0, whose ShareAlike condition does not allow a NonCommercial restriction to be added to derivative works. Those files keep the upstream license, with attribution owed to the Wikimedia projects and their contributors. Wikidata statements are CC0. The code uses PolyForm Noncommercial rather than a Creative Commons license because Creative Commons advises against applying its licenses to software. Funding. DEM-Debate is supported by the European Media and Information Fund (EMIF), managed by the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation in partnership with the European University Institute. Contact: david.abella@eurecat.org, david.laniado@eurecat.org

papers.title: P1v.2026
papers.venue: Figshare
papers.abstract: Automated guided vehicle (AGV) systems in warehouses, used for transporting and sorting goods in automated production lines, are currently improving and automating each stage of the process using various AGV types. This paper presents a study on a converter designed for flexible and efficient wireless power conversion for multiple automated robots operating on a DC microgrid in a smart warehouse. The converter facilitates bidirectional power exchange via three ports integrated into one AGV and between different AGVs without requiring additional systems within the automated robot. The microgrid system will have a rigid structure, similar to a charging distribution grid for the automated robots. With wireless power transmission, flexible energy exchange is possible between the DC microgrid and the automated robots in both directions, and between the robots themselves when not near a fixed charging point within the DC microgrid during transport. A novel retractable coil design is being used in a proposed inductive wireless charging system, demonstrating that small deformations of the coil shape do not affect transmission efficiency. A prototype, five times smaller in size, has been deployed and tested. It successfully transmitted over 200 W of power over a distance of 18 cm with an efficiency of nearly 68.72\%. This principle can be applied to various mobile platforms with limited payload space, where remote power and renewable energy sources are required.

papers.title: Data-driven styling optimization of an intelligent medical waste recycling robot using AHP-CRITIC and SSA-ELM
papers.venue: Discover Computing
papers.abstract: Abstract To improve the attractiveness and practicality of intelligent medical waste recycling robots, this study proposes a data-driven styling optimization framework integrating Kansei Engineering, AHP-CRITIC weighting, and a Sparrow Search Algorithm-optimized Extreme Learning Machine (SSA-ELM). Factor analysis was first used to reduce affective vocabularies and extract core perceptual dimensions. AHP-CRITIC was then applied to identify five key styling features closely associated with user perception: side profile, front view, display screen, wheels, and body. Based on these features, SSA-ELM was employed to establish a nonlinear mapping between design variables and perceptual responses, and to predict the optimized styling combination. Model performance was evaluated using repeated 10-fold cross-validation. The results show that SSA-ELM generally outperformed GA-ELM, PSO-ELM, and conventional ELM in predictive accuracy and stability, with the most robust performance observed in the Balanced dimension. User evaluation further confirmed that the optimized design significantly improved ratings of balance, smoothness, perceived intelligence, reduced work burden, and safety. The proposed framework provides a quantitative and interpretable pathway for the affective design of intelligent medical service equipment.

papers.title: Dataset associated with "A Data-Driven and Theory-Guided Framework for Human–Robot Collaboration Workforce Training in Construction Engineering and Management"
papers.venue: Virginia Tech Data Repository
papers.abstract: The increasing integration of robotic systems into construction engineering and management is reshaping workforce requirements and creating demand for new forms of human-robot collaboration (HRC) competencies. However, existing construction workforce training approaches remain fragmented, with limited frameworks for systematically identifying, organizing, and validating the competencies required for effective HRC in construction environments. This study presents a data-driven and theory-guided framework for developing HRC workforce training modules in construction engineering and management. The framework integrates computational competency augmentation, Revised Bloom’s Taxonomy (RBT)-guided cognitive classification, learning-objective synthesis, semantic module formation, and expert-based validation. A baseline HRC competency framework derived from prior literature was augmented using industry-facing evidence sources, including construction robotics documentation, implementation case studies, and job advertisements. Extracted competency statements were classified into knowledge, skills, and abilities (KSA) categories, semantically clustered, and mapped to Bloom-aligned learning objectives using an ABCD-informed structure. Competencies and learning objectives were subsequently organized into theory-constrained training modules and evaluated through internal validation checks and a multi-round Delphi study involving experts from academia, industry, and learning sciences. The resulting dataset includes the augmented HRC competency framework, Bloom-level classifications, learning objectives, module assignments, semantic similarity outputs, dependency mappings, and expert validation results. The framework provides a reproducible and interpretable approach for competency-driven workforce training development in construction robotics and HRC contexts.

papers.title: Spot Autowalk Long-Term (SALT) Dataset
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The Spot Autowalk Long-Term (SALT) Dataset was collected by performing repeated Autowalks with a Boston Dynamics Spot robot across three different scenarios, including both indoor and outdoor environments. The main contribution is 217 traversals of an outdoor Autowalk around the Ontario Tech University campus over a 16 month period. The recorded data includes point clouds, local elevation and occupancy grids, dynamic object and staircase detection, odometry data, joint states, battery conditions and more. In total, the dataset contains 286 traversals and 193 km of walking over a period of nearly two years. The data is presented in multiple formats for ease of use, including: native format, a human-readable format, a KITTI Odometry format including pseudo ground truth poses, and an MCAP format for use with ROS2. This dataset aims to enable researchers to develop new algorithms for long-term mapping applications.

papers.title: Robot in a crib: How a playing robot helps us understand sensorimotor contingency learning
papers.venue: Science Robotics
papers.abstract: Learning sensorimotor contingencies—that is, the link between one’s actions and their sensory effects—is fundamental to developing body knowledge, understanding causality, and developing a sense of agency. In developmental psychology, this process is classically studied using the mobile paradigm, where infants learn that movement of a limb causes motion of a connected mobile. To expand our understanding of how infants learn this, we tested an embodied computational model that learns through two biologically inspired mechanisms: prediction and curiosity. Implemented on the child-sized iCub humanoid robot interacting with a mobile, the model detected sensorimotor contingencies across several experimental conditions using a variety of movement strategies. Our findings suggest that contingency learning cannot be captured by a single behavioral metric, such as the amount of movement, but instead emerges through a spectrum of exploratory behaviors. Analysis of the robot’s internal activity reveals that these behaviors emerge from the dynamic trade-off between prediction and curiosity—between exploitation and exploration. Our work provides a biologically motivated, physically embodied model of sensorimotor interaction that connects theories of infant learning with robotic implementations. The results allow us to generate testable hypotheses for developmental research and to inform the design of autonomous learning systems.

papers.title: Vision-Based Machine Learning voor Chemische Procescontrole: Een Haalbaarheidsstudie over Meerdere Toepassingen
papers.venue: Lirias
papers.abstract: This research is motivated by the increasing complexity of chemical processes and the growing demand for robust, non-invasive monitoring and control solutions in the context of the ongoing digitalization of the chemical industry. Many critical aspects of chemical processes, such as phase behavior, flow patterns, and fouling, are inherently visual and therefore difficult to capture using traditional point measurements. By leveraging computer vision as a sensing modality, this thesis addresses a critical gap between observable process behavior and advanced, data-driven process control. The proposed methodology aims to support the transition towards more autonomous and intelligent operation by emphasizing robustness, interpretability, and seamless integration with existing industrial control frameworks, thereby facilitating the practical adoption of vision-based process control in the chemical sector. The research is structured around three primary objectives. The first objective focuses on the development of machine vision methods for classification and segmentation in chemical production environments characterized by continuous operation and high intrinsic safety standards. As a result, truly abnormal or failure-related events occur rarely, leading to highly imbalanced and limited datasets that pose significant challenges for conventional supervised learning approaches. Moreover, the creation of labeled datasets in the chemical sector is often prohibitively expensive, as it requires the involvement of domain experts to accurately interpret and annotate complex process phenomena. To address these constraints, two novel methods are proposed. The first method employs generative adversarial networks for anomaly detection, incorporating tailored cost functions and the structural similarity index to enable automated segmentation. This approach outperforms conventional supervised segmentation models trained for task-specific detection problems. The second method combines original and synthetically generated data to optimize classifier performance while quantitatively assessing generalization through an explainable AI framework. This strategy demonstrates superior performance compared to standard data augmentation techniques, increasing classification accuracy for the chemical foam classification task from 57% to 91%. The second objective focuses on developing a vision-based closed-loop control strategy for process management in the chemical sector. A laboratory setup simulating a chemical foaming production process, in which foam is continuously generated and a vision-based dosing system has been implemented to control foam volume, was established to develop a strategy capable of maintaining effectiveness even when precise control input accuracy cannot be guaranteed. The results demonstrate the feasibility of vision-based process control for automated anti-foaming agent dosing. Furthermore, a sensitivity analysis was conducted to evaluate the impact of the detection system's performance on the control solution. The analysis revealed that the precision of the detector has a limited effect on the system's ability to mitigate foam formation, whereas recall plays a more critical role: if recall dropped below 50%, the system was no longer able to effectively combat foam formation. The thesis concludes with the introduction of a generic framework for the development and deployment of machine vision-based control applications in chemical settings. This framework provides guidance on addressing data acquisition challenges, selecting suitable models, and integrating them into live production environments for automated decision-making. The framework was validated through four use cases at BASF Antwerpen, showcasing its applicability in real-world environments and gave way for several cost savings. The contributions of this thesis significantly advanced the field of vision-based process control, particularly within BASF Antwerpen. The findings emphasize the importance of robust model development, effective use of synthetic data, and the integration of machine vision systems into closed-loop control processes. These advancements offer tangible benefits for automation, efficiency, and cost reduction in chemical production environments and has been applied in four different use cases at BASF Antwerpen.

papers.title: SightlineAI: AI-Powered Smart Glasses Framework and Edge Computer Vision for the Visually Impaired
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: SightlineAI is an open-source assistive technology platform utilizing edge computer vision, real-time spatial object detection, scene narration, and low-latency audio feedback designed for smart glasses hardware to assist visually impaired and blind individuals in navigating dynamic physical environments.

papers.title: Enhancing operational wind downscaling capabilities over Canada: Application of a Conditional Wasserstein GAN methodology
papers.venue: Artificial Intelligence for the Earth Systems
papers.abstract: Abstract Downscaling based on Artificial Intelligence (AI) has been demonstrated to be a powerful tool for improving the spatial resolution of weather forecasts. This study advances wind downscaling by extending the DownGAN framework introduced by Annau et al. to operational Canadian Numerical Weather Predictions (NWP), namely from the Global Deterministic Prediction System (GDPS) to the domain of the High-Resolution Deterministic Prediction System (HRDPS). We enhance the AI model by incorporating high-resolution static covariates, such as topography on the HRDPS grid, into a Conditional Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network with Gradient Penalty, implemented using a UNET-based generator. Following the DownGAN framework, our methodology integrates low-resolution GDPS forecasts (15 km, 10-day horizon) and high-resolution HRDPS forecasts (2.5 km, 48-hour horizon) with Frequency Separation techniques adapted from computer vision. Through robust training and inference over the whole Canadian region, we demonstrate the operational scalability of our approach, while achieving significant improvements in wind downscaling accuracy. Statistical validation highlights reduction in root mean square error (RMSE) and log spectral distance (LSD) metrics compared to the original DownGAN. High-resolution conditioning covariates and Frequency Separation strategies prove instrumental in enhancing model performance. This work underscores the potential for extending high-resolution wind forecasts beyond the 48-hour horizon, bridging the gap to the 10-day low-resolution global forecast window.

papers.title: smshagor-dev/wireless-Vision-Aid-for-the-blind: v2.0.0
papers.venue: Open MIND
papers.abstract: Wireless Vision-Aid for the Blind (WVAB) — v2.0.0 Release Type: Major Platform / Research Release Release Version: 2.0.0 License: MIT Status: Research and Assistive Prototype Baseline: v1.0.1 Overview WVAB v2.0.0 is a major evolution of the Wireless Vision-Aid for the Blind platform. This release expands WVAB from a primarily camera/object-detection application into a broader offline-first assistive computer-vision, secure edge-camera, mobile, mapping, and navigation research platform. The release adds a significantly stronger architecture around perception, focused spoken guidance, secure camera transport, mobile inference, local history, navigation safety states, Raspberry Pi/ESP32 deployment, packaging, CI validation, and reproducible research workflows. Important version note The overall WVAB Python/research platform release is v2.0.0. The standalone Flutter Android application intentionally remains visible version v1.0.0, internal build 8. This keeps the mobile application version contract separate from the repository/platform release version. What's New in v2.0.0 1. Offline-First Assistive Vision Platform WVAB now has a clearer offline-first architecture designed to perform primary perception locally rather than depending on cloud inference. New platform behavior includes: local real-time object detection; bounded spoken guidance; local detection history; local mobile settings and profile persistence; local-first Android phone-camera inference; explicit handling of degraded or unavailable navigation inputs. The core runtime flow is now organized around: capture -> validate -> infer -> interpret -> provide bounded feedback 2. Standalone Flutter Android Application A complete Flutter Android assistive application is now included under: mobile/flutter/ The application includes: first-run user-name/profile setup; language selection; phone-camera source selection; ESP32-CAM source support; trusted IP-camera source support; local ONNX object detection; 80 COCO detection classes; configurable detection classes; configurable confidence threshold; spoken object guidance; haptic feedback; approximate range/distance guidance; left / center / right scene positioning; visual route comparison; local detection history; history clearing; local settings persistence; Privacy Policy screen; Open Source Licenses screen; How It Works screen; Contact screen; About/navigation UI improvements. Current Android Runtime Contract | Item | Value | |---|---| | Visible app version | 1.0.0 | | Internal build | 8 | | Flutter | 3.47.0 | | Dart | >=3.11.0 <4.0.0 | | Android package | com.smshagor.wvab_mobile | | Minimum Android SDK | 24 | | Detector input | 1 x 3 x 320 x 320 | | Detector classes | 80 COCO classes | | Default confidence | 0.25 | | ONNX Flutter wrapper | flutter_onnxruntime 1.8.2 | | Android ONNX Runtime | 1.22.0 | | Camera backend | camera_android 0.10.11 | 3. Focused Spoken Guidance The speech system was redesigned to avoid announcing every detected object in sequence. Instead, WVAB now: ranks accepted detections by risk; selects one primary object; briefly holds focus to reduce rapid switching; allows a clearly nearer hazard to preempt the previous focus; produces one focused route/spatial cue; keeps all detections available in the UI and history. Example guidance: Chair, about 1.5 meters away, left. Right side appears clearer. Keep right carefully. This reduces stale speech queues and lowers cognitive load. 4. Improved Object Detection Coverage The Flutter detector now exposes all 80 COCO classes instead of a narrow subset. Detection behavior was also updated with: default confidence reduced to 0.25; migration of older stored confidence settings; improved filtering; more stable detection defaults; focused hazard selection; consistent normalized bounding-box processing. COCO detection does not automatically provide custom classes such as potholes, stairs, curbs, or arbitrary ground hazards. Those require a separately trained/custom model. 5. Approximate Distance and Range Guidance WVAB now provides more useful spatial context. For selected object classes with reasonably stable reference sizes, the mobile app can estimate approximate monocular distance using a pinhole-style relationship. The platform distinguishes between: qualitative visual proximity; approximate monocular distance; calibrated metric distance; unsupported/unreliable distance conditions. This avoids presenting heuristic values as certified measurements. 6. Safer Route and Navigation Semantics Navigation research behavior now uses explicit safety states: STOP DEGRADED GUIDANCE_AVAILABLE The system is designed not to silently convert missing, stale, or uncalibrated data into confident navigation commands. Route guidance uses conservative language such as: Right side appears clearer. rather than claiming that the ground is definitely safe. 7. Navigation Research Pipeline v2.0.0 introduces/expands an experimental navigation stack including: visual odometry; optional ORB-SLAM3 bridge; optional MiDaS depth path; metric-calibration gating; occupancy-grid mapping; A* planning; safety-state output; explicit degraded-mode handling. These components are research features and are not certified autonomous navigation functionality. 8. Secure ESP32 / Python Camera Transport The remote camera path has been significantly hardened. Security capabilities now include: AES-GCM encrypted UDP transport; authentication required by default; protocol-v2 authentication counters; non-zero sender session IDs; replay/order protection; persistent authentication replay state; authenticated UDP headers using AES-GCM AAD; bounded authentication/session/frame state; safer session handling; loopback WebSocket control by default. This is a major improvement over unauthenticated or loosely trusted camera-stream designs. 9. Raspberry Pi and Edge Deployment WVAB now has stronger support for edge-device deployment and research use, including: Raspberry Pi runtime paths; ESP32-CAM integration; secure remote camera transport; local/edge inference workflows; reproducible deployment checks; hardware-oriented validation in CI where possible. 10. Python Package and CLI WVAB is now structured as a distributable Python package. v2.0.0 packaging includes: wvab_system-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl wvab_system-2.0.0.tar.gz The package provides a command-line entry point: wvab --help Release packaging validates: package version 2.0.0; package name wvab-system; Python requirement >=3.10; MIT license metadata; installed entry point; packaged runtime resources; wheel installation outside the source checkout. 11. Reorganized Runtime Architecture The repository now separates active responsibilities more clearly. Important runtime areas include: core/ mapping/ navigation/ perception/ training/ tools/ mobile/flutter/ Important entry points include: | Component | Purpose | |---|---| | vision_server.py | Local/trusted camera detection | | udp_streaming.py | Secure remote camera streaming | | core/udp_runtime.py | UDP transport/session runtime | | core/udp_auth_state.py | Persistent authentication/replay state | | navigation_pipeline.py | Mapping/planning and navigation safety state | | smartphone_camera.py | Trusted smartphone/IP camera launcher | | main.py | Command dispatcher | | mobile/flutter/ | Android assistive application | Legacy duplicate/mock runtime paths were removed or reduced so fixed/mock measurements are less likely to be confused with real sensor output. Major Updates and Improvements Mobile Camera Stability The Android camera runtime was hardened with: serialized lifecycle transitions; stale controller invalidation; safer controller disposal; preview initialization before inference; camera_android Camera2 backend; medium-resolution image stream; YUV420 capture; inference throttling; lifecycle regression tests. These changes reduce race conditions around camera start/stop/resume behavior. ONNX Runtime Stability Android inference now uses a controlled runtime combination: flutter_onnxruntime: 1.8.2 onnxruntime-android: 1.22.0 Additional improvements include: CPU-only inference configuration; controlled thread counts; ONNX Runtime ProGuard/native rules; Android native ELF validation; runtime dependency verification; bundled model presence checks. Text-to-Speech Reliability Speech initialization and playback were hardened with: language availability checks; fallback to en-US; full output volume request; controlled speech rate; controlled pitch; current utterance cancellation before new speech; detection-to-speech regression coverage. The software tests verify that guidance reaches the TTS service path. Actual acoustic output still depends on the physical device, installed TTS engine/voice data, audio routing, and volume state. Settings Migration Older mobile installations now receive safer detection defaults without permanently overwriting later user choices. Updates include: detection-settings schema migration; legacy confidence migration to 0.25; preservation of explicit newer user settings; all 80 COCO classes enabled by default. UI and Accessibility The mobile UI received substantial completion and validation work, including: About navigation improvements; Contact page/navigation fixes; Privacy page validation; responsive/viewport-aware widget tests; profile/onboarding flow; settings persistence; history UI; accessibility-focused guidance wording. Documentation The main documentation was substantially rewritten and expanded. Documentation now covers: project goals; current capabilities; architecture; Android app; perception mathematics; distance estimation; focus selection; navigation safety semantics; secure UDP pr

papers.title: Multimodal Deep Learning for Participatory Public Art Assessment: Integrating Computer Vision and Behavioral Analytics for Community Engagement
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This repository contains the supporting source code accompanying the manuscript entitled: "Multimodal Deep Learning for Participatory Public Art Assessment: Integrating Computer Vision and Behavioral Analytics for Community Engagement." The repository has been prepared to facilitate the reproducibility of the methodology presented in the manuscript. It contains the implementation of the principal components of the proposed framework, including dataset preprocessing, spatio-temporal feature extraction, cross-attention-based multimodal fusion, transformer-based feature integration, training utilities, and evaluation modules. Repository Contents The repository includes: Dataset preprocessing pipeline Dataset loaders for benchmark datasets Spatio-temporal feature extraction module Cross-attention mechanism Multimodal transformer encoder Training and inference scripts Performance evaluation utilities Configuration files project structure

papers.title: Self-prompting segmentation framework: an advanced computer vision technique for electro-construction waste valorisation
papers.venue: Waste Management
topics: Innovations in Concrete and Construction Materials
papers.abstract: The effective recognition and sorting of Electro-Construction Waste (ECW) remain critical challenges in Material Recovery Facilities (MRFs), limiting resource valorisation and compromising worker safety. Computer vision shows strong potential for automated waste recognition and recycling. However, its application to recognising ECW components remains unexplored. This study introduces the “Self-Prompting Segmentation Framework” (SPSF), a parameter-efficient computer vision pipeline for precise part-level segmentation of ECW, enabling automated recognition, dismantling, and sorting in MRFs. The framework adapts a large-scale vision foundation model by integrating a detector for self-prompt generation, and Low-Rank Adaptation for efficient fine-tuning, updating only a small subset of parameters while preserving high segmentation fidelity. Validated on a curated dataset of real-world ECW images, SPSF achieves relative improvements of 39.17 % in mean Intersection over Union, 39.27 % in mean Dice-Sørensen Coefficient, and 28.15 % in mean Average Precision over the Segment Anything Model 2 baseline. These results demonstrate that SPSF can accurately identify individual components within different ECW categories. This capability provides a practical and scalable approach for automated waste component recognition, supporting more efficient material sorting and recycling.

papers.title: Computer Vision Powered Web Application to Identify Brick Fractures
papers.venue: TEM Journal
papers.abstract: The objective of this study is to improve fracture identification in bricks at a factory located in Virú through the use of a computer vision application during the year 2025. The study employed a pure experimental design. The population consisted of all brick quality inspection processes carried out by construction companies, with a sample size of 30 processes. The data collection technique employed was direct observation, and the instrument used was an observation form. The computer vision application was developed using Python 3.12 and the Flask framework, with MongoDB as the database management system and Mobile-D as the software development methodology. Descriptive analysis was performed using Microsoft Excel 2019, while inferential analysis was conducted using Jamovi 2.6.44. The results showed a 32.91% increase in fracture identification, a reduction of 114.4 seconds in the average time to identify brick fractures, and a 30.6% improvement in identification accuracy. In conclusion, the use of a computer vision application significantly improves fracture identification in brick factories.

papers.title: AZINDI: A Multi-Class Dataset for Deep Learning Based Azadirachta Indica Leaf Disease and Health Recognition
papers.venue: Mendeley Data
papers.abstract: Azadirachta Indica Leaf Disease and Health Classification Dataset is a curated image dataset developed for research in artificial intelligence, machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, and automated plant disease classification. The dataset contains leaf images of Azadirachta indica (Neem) collected from Rajbari and Ashulia, Dhaka, Bangladesh. The dataset is organized into three classes: Chlorotic, Disease, and Healthy. To support balanced model training, each class contains 1,000 training images, 150 validation images, and 150 test images, resulting in 3,000 training images, 450 validation images, and 450 test images, with 4,500 images in total. The dataset is intended for developing and evaluating deep learning and computer vision models for Neem leaf health assessment, disease classification, feature extraction, and explainable AI-based agricultural applications. The images can be used for benchmarking CNN, Transformer, and hybrid deep learning architectures.

papers.title: AI Specimen Intelligence Platform: A Framework for Predictive Risk Detection in Clinical Laboratory Workflows
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

The framework combines barcode validation, imaging, computer vision, predictive analytics, and operational decision support to help identify specimen concerns before downstream processing occurs. The paper discusses architecture, risk assessment models, operational workflows, implementation considerations, and future opportunities for predictive intelligence in laboratory operations.

papers.title: SMART DRIVER DROWSINESS DETECTION AND AUTOMATED EMERGENCY COMMUNICATION SYSTEM
papers.venue: International Journal of Engineering Research and Science & Technology
papers.abstract: Road traffic accidents caused by driver fatigue continue to be a major public safety concern, highlighting the need for intelligent and real-time monitoring systems. This paper presents a Smart Driver Drowsiness Detection and Advanced Emergency Communication System that combines computer vision, deep learning, and automated emergency response to enhance driver safety. The proposed system employs MediaPipe Face Mesh to accurately detect facial landmarks and localize the driver’s eye regions from live video captured through a standard webcam. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is utilized to classify the eye state as open or closed, while an adaptive eyescore mechanism continuously evaluates the driver’s alertness by analyzing consecutive eye-closure patterns. When signs of prolonged drowsiness are detected, the system immediately activates an audible warning to regain the driver’s attention. If the driver fails to respond after multiple warning cycles, the system initiates an automated emergency communication process by obtaining the current GPS location, generating a Google Maps navigation link, transmitting an emergency email to predefined contacts, and placing an emergency phone call using Android Debug Bridge (ADB). Unlike conventional driver monitoring systems that focus solely on fatigue detection, the proposed framework integrates an intelligent emergency response mechanism to provide timely assistance during critical situations. The system is entirely nonintrusive, operates in real time using inexpensive hardware, and does not require wearable sensors, making it practical for deployment in modern vehicles. Experimental evaluation demonstrates that the integration of MediaPipe and CNN enables reliable eyestate recognition with low computational complexity, providing an effective solution for reducing fatigue-related accidents and improving road safety.

papers.title: APPLICATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND IOT IN ENHANCING FISHERIES MANAGEMENT FOR BLUE ECONOMY SUSTAINABILITY
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The blue economy positions ocean and inland water resources as engines of inclusive growth, yet capture fisheries remain hampered by data scarcity, unreliable stock assessments, and the persistence of illegal, unreported and unregulated (IUU) fishing. This study examines how Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT) can be combined to strengthen fisheries management and advance blue economy sustainability. Drawing on a structured review of literature published between 2019 and 2026, the study synthesises evidence across four thematic domains: sensing and data acquisition, machine learning for stock assessment, computer vision for species and vessel monitoring, and integrated decision-support architectures. A four-layered AI–IoT framework is proposed, linking distributed sensing, low-power connectivity, intelligent analytics, and adaptive management feedback. The findings indicate that convergence of these technologies improves the timeliness, granularity, and reliability of fisheries information, while reducing monitoring costs. The study concludes that realising these benefits at scale depends on resolving challenges of data interoperability, connectivity in remote waters, equity of access for small-scale fishers, and governance of automated decision-making

papers.title: Similarity Across Layers and Resolutions: A Theory of Difference, Identity, and Asymmetric Transport
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper develops a mathematical framework in which similarity, difference, and identity depend jointly on descriptive layer and observational resolution. It introduces the Layer–Resolution similarity function S(A,B;ℓ,r)S(A,B;\ell,r), distinguishes visible from hidden differences, and derives asymmetric cross-layer transport laws under exact and approximate compatibility. The framework is further connected to potential applications in mathematical analogy discovery, computer vision, and large language models.

papers.title: Sign sense
papers.venue: OpenAlex
papers.abstract: This research explores the development and implementation of an AI-based sign language interpreter aimed at eliminating communication barriers between the hearing and deaf or hard-of-hearing communities. Utilizing advanced deep learning techniques such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and computer vision algorithms, this system interprets hand gestures and facial expressions in real time, converting them into spoken or written language. The project not only contributes to inclusive communication but also enhances accessibility in areas like education, workplaces, and public services. This chapter details the architecture of the model, dataset preparation, model training, and real-world deployment results. The aim is to contribute a robust solution that is affordable, user-friendly, and scalable. The implications of this research extend beyond communication—it represents a meaningful step toward equity, empowerment, and inclusion through artificial intelligence.

papers.title: Robotics and autonomous systems
papers.venue: OpenAlex
papers.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) with robotics and autonomous systems creates revolutionary industrial changes through better operational efficiency along with precision and flexibility improvements. This chapter discusses the shifting capabilities of modern robotics through a study of machine learning together with deep learning, computer vision, and natural language processing (NLP) technologies. Robotics has benefited from these technological developments, which allow robots to perform independent complex operations, including automated manufacturing functions and intelligent supply chain operations. The chapter evaluates how AI-driven robotic applications in manufacturing, healthcare, logistics, and agriculture generate various production effects and workforce distribution patterns. It provides solutions for both technical challenges and ethical problems, along with safety issues that arise from extensive autonomous system deployment. The chapter discusses the upcoming trends of AI-powered robotic technology, which combines 5G with edge computing and the Internet of Things (IoT) to enhance the operating potential of autonomous systems in industrial applications. The chapter also delivers extensive insights into AI’s impact on robotics evolution, which creates framework innovations for Industry 4.0’s future development.

papers.title: Advancing Library Automation and Digital Transformation Through Artificial Intelligence
papers.venue: Advances in computational intelligence and robotics book series
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming how libraries operate, manage, and deliver information by enabling automation, personalization, and digital innovation. This chapter examines the integration of Machine Learning (ML), Natural Language Processing (NLP), and Computer Vision in automating cataloging, metadata generation, and indexing. It highlights AI's role in digital preservation, intelligent search, and predictive analytics for resource management. Real-world applications, including chatbots and AI-driven library systems, are discussed alongside ethical challenges such as bias, privacy, and sustainability. The chapter concludes with strategies and future directions for building inclusive, intelligent, and ethically governed smart library ecosystems.

papers.title: Selective Adaptation against Domain Shift in Visual Learning Systems
papers.venue: University of Liverpool
papers.abstract: Deep learning models have achieved remarkable success in a wide range of computer vision tasks, demonstrating exceptional performance in environments where the training and test data share similar distributions. However, in real-world applications, models are often confronted with a fundamental issue: domain shift. This occurs when the distribution of test data differs from that of the training data, leading to a significant performance degradation. This discrepancy between source (training) and target (deployment) domains presents a critical challenge for deploying robust, reliable, and scalable artificial intelligence systems in dynamic and unpredictable real-world environments. To address this challenge, this thesis proposes innovative selective adaptation strategies, which focus on adapting deep learning models to target domains with minimal additional data or human intervention. We tackle the domain shift problem from two complementary perspectives: Active Domain Adaptation (ADA) for label-efficient domain transfer and Test-Time Adaptation (TTA) for source-free online adaptation. In the ADA setting, existing approaches suffer from biased initialization driven by noisy pseudo-labels and unreliable sample selection, where entropy metrics fail to identify 'wrong' predictions under large domain shifts. To overcome these limitations, we propose a framework that constructs reliable pseudo labels guided by source–target prototype relationships. Furthermore, we introduce a hybrid uncertainty metric that combines prediction entropy with perturbation-based model stability, enabling more informative sample selection and faster domain alignment. For TTA, naively updating parameters leads to catastrophic forgetting and vulnerability to spurious correlations. Furthermore, when extending TTA to large-scale Vision-Language Models (VLMs), the web-scale pre-training amplifies feature redundancy, entangling causal features with domain-specific noise. To mitigate these issues, we design two frameworks: one selectively fine-tunes domain-sensitive layer groups while freezing domain-invariant ones, supported by a dual-metric filtering criterion that excludes unreliable samples; the other targets VLMs through dynamic feature purification, which disentangles visual representations into meaningful and redundant components under a contrastive learning objective. Extensive experiments on standard benchmarks, including Cityscapes, CIFAR10/100-C, ImageNet-C, and several cross-domain datasets, demonstrate that our methods achieve competitive performance. Overall, this thesis establishes selective adaptation as a robust and effective paradigm for mitigating domain shift in modern visual learning systems.

papers.title: DAMS-Mamba: integrating dynamic attention and multi-scale modelling for cerebral vessel segmentation
papers.venue: Connection Science
papers.abstract: Recent developments in the fields of deep learning and computer vision have significantly impacted the segmentation of medical images, especially in the challenging task of cerebral vessel segmentation. The complexity of vascular structures and the need for high clinical accuracy present unique difficulties, particularly in segmenting small, thin blood vessels. This paper introduces DAMS-Mamba, a novel deep learning model designed to significantly improve the precision and efficiency of brain vessel segmentation. By leveraging advanced techniques such as multi-scale feature extraction, dynamic context-aware modelling and dynamic weighted feature fusion, DAMS-Mamba effectively utilises both local and global context information. This allows the model to capture the fine details of small vessels while maintaining the overall vessel structure, thus improving segmentation results in complex scenarios. The model was evaluated using publicly available datasets, including the Cerebral MRA Dataset Annotations and TubeTK public brain 3D vessel dataset, demonstrating an overall performance improvement of approximately 5% to 10% compared to existing methods. The experimental results underscore the potential of DAMS-Mamba for clinical applications, providing a powerful tool for vascular segmentation in the medical field. The study also suggests promising directions for future research, including optimising computational efficiency and extending the model to other medical image analysis tasks, further advancing the application of artificial intelligence in medical image analysis.

papers.title: AI-Based 3D Visualization in Libraries
papers.venue: Advances in computational intelligence and robotics book series
papers.abstract: The convergence of artificial intelligence and three-dimensional visualization technologies represents a transformative paradigm shift in contemporary library services. This chapter examines how machine learning algorithms, computer vision systems, and extended reality technologies reshape information access and user engagement within library environments. Through systematic analysis of current implementations across academic, public, and special libraries, this work establishes a comprehensive framework for understanding AI-enhanced spatial technologies in library contexts. Key areas explored include virtual and augmented reality applications, digital twin concepts for library spaces, AI-driven navigation systems, and accessibility considerations for inclusive design. The chapter synthesizes research from library science, computer science, and human-computer interaction to provide practical guidance for implementing AI-based 3D visualization initiatives.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Sports Motion Analysis (2011–2025): A Bibliometric and Evolutionary Review of Methods, Modalities, and Sports Science Applications
papers.venue: Applied Sciences
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has rapidly reshaped sports motion analysis through advances in wearable sensing, computer vision, and deep learning. However, existing reviews often focus on isolated techniques and lack a systematic evolutionary perspective. This study presents a 15-year bibliometric and evolutionary review of AI in sports motion analysis (2011–2025), integrating scientometric mapping with quantitative content analysis across modalities, methods, and applications. A comprehensive multi-source dataset of 2602 publications was analyzed using VOSviewer and CiteSpace to examine knowledge structures, collaboration patterns, co-citation networks, and emerging research fronts. In addition, each study was categorized by modality (wearable, visual, and multi-modal), AI method (traditional machine learning, deep learning, and transformer-based), and task type (activity recognition, performance analysis, rehabilitation, and others). The results reveal exponential growth and a clear three-stage evolution: a sensor-driven phase dominated by wearable devices and traditional machine learning (2011–2015), a deep learning expansion phase centered on vision-based modeling (2016–2019), and a recent deep learning consolidation phase characterized by emerging transformer-based methods, increasing multimodal integration, real-time monitoring, and application-oriented sports analytics (2020–2025). The field has shifted from signal-based recognition toward vision-centered performance evaluation, rehabilitation-related movement assessment, and injury-informed applications. This data-driven review provides an integrated evolutionary framework and future research roadmap to support the continued development of AI-driven analytics in sports science, athlete monitoring, and health-related human movement analysis.

papers.title: AI-driven motion planning for efficient oil palm harvesting with robotic manipulators
papers.venue: OpenAlex
papers.abstract: The oil palm sector is a major part of the global farming sector. The procedure of gathering the fruit remains very laborious, takes a long time, and is often dangerous due of the poor working conditions and the physical demands on workers. This project created an AI-based motion planning system for robotic manipulators to automate oil palm harvesting. It improves the picking speed, accuracy, and safety. The study describes a complete robotic tool system design that leverages cutting-edge sensor and vision technology to understand its environment. This technique employs an AI-based motion planning system with deep learning and reinforcement learning algorithms to optimize robotic arm movement. This ensures they can move and control things efficiently in a shifting, obstacle-filled environment. This framework provides effective methods for avoiding barriers and adapting to environmental changes including uneven ground, tree structures, and workers or machinery. New methods are developed to capture and manipulate oil palm fruit bunches without harming the crop or tree, thereby solving one of the key issues in automating this process. A well-selected array of gathering circumstances was used for training, which helped the neural network or reinforcement learning model perform successfully in real life. Extensive computer studies show that this model can plan safe and efficient paths, and real-world use of the method proves that it can be used and modified in real-life areas. The results are much better than those from standard human methods and current robotic solutions when it comes to the gathering cycle time, target identification accuracy, and operating safety.

papers.title: Low-latency multicamera 3D tracking of insects with Braid
papers.venue: bioRxiv (Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory)
papers.abstract: Advances in camera technology and computer vision techniques have allowed researchers to track animals in 3D in ways which previously were difficult or impossible. Many such 3D tracking tools make use of multiple cameras, but unfamiliarity with the principles and technology involved can make it difficult to employ such techniques. In this protocol, we describe Braid, open-source software for live, multi-camera 3D tracking of insects. Using background-subtraction, Braid performs detection of objects without requiring the use of physical markers affixed to the insect. Braid constructs low-latency 3D position estimates using Kalman filtering and nearest neighbor data association. We document in detail the process of tracking freely flying bees within a flight arena using Braid. This protocol includes instructions on installation, configuration of cameras, setup, calibration, and operation. Within the system described here, we demonstrate that Braid can achieve position estimates accurate to <1 millimeter (within a 0.3 cubic meter volume). These factors make Braid suitable for tracking small, fast-flying animals like insects. Braid's low latency allows live tracking, removing the necessity to collect large video files and making it suitable for integration in closed loop systems such as virtual reality. Code is available at https://github.com/strawlab/strand-braid

papers.title: cengizapaydin/AI-Powered-Video-Scene-Extractor: AI-Powered Video Scene Extractor
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This project is a Python desktop application that analyzes YouTube videos or local .mp4 files to automatically detect scene transitions (cuts) using computer vision algorithms. The application extracts a user-defined number of sample frames (1, 2, or 3) from each continuous shot and saves them to your computer, naming them with their exact timecodes. It reduces a manual screen-capturing process that would normally take hours down to mere seconds, making it especially useful for film editing analysis, virtual production reference studies, and academic visual deconstructions. Bu proje, YouTube videolarını veya bilgisayarınızdaki yerel .mp4 dosyalarını analiz ederek, videodaki sahne geçişlerini (cut) yapay görme algoritmalarıyla otomatik olarak tespit eden bir Python masaüstü uygulamasıdır. Uygulama, tespit ettiği her bir kesintisiz plandan kullanıcının belirlediği sayıda (1, 2 veya 3) örnek kareyi (frame) alır ve bunları gerçek zaman kodlarıyla (timecode) isimlendirerek bilgisayarınıza kaydeder. Özellikle film kurgu analizleri, sanal prodüksiyon referans çalışmaları ve akademik görsel çözümlemeler için manuel olarak saatler sürecek ekran görüntüsü alma işlemini saniyelere indirir. papers.title: Single-Channel EEG Dataset: UI Visual Complexity and Cognitive Load
papers.venue: Open Science Framework
papers.abstract: Single-channel EEG recorded from 47 participants performing a visual search task on screenshots of real web interfaces spanning three levels of visual complexity. DEVICE NeuroSky MindWave Mobile 2, a consumer-grade dry-electrode headset. Active electrode at Fp1 (left frontopolar, 10-20 system), reference and ground via a left earlobe clip. Raw waveform sampled at 512 Hz; the device also reports eight sub-band powers and an eSense attention score at 1 Hz. TASK AND STIMULI Each trial presented one full-screen interface screenshot and asked the participant to locate a specified target element. Stimuli were drawn from the public website-aesthetics-datasets repository (Calista AI), built on the large-scale study of Reinecke et al. Perceived visual complexity scores were split at their tertiles (P33 = 4.31, P67 = 5.32) into Simple, Moderate and Complex. The final set comprised 70 interfaces: 24 simple, 20 moderate, 26 complex. PARTICIPANTS 47 male undergraduates, aged 21-25, all with normal vision, no known neurological conditions, and regular computer use. Sessions were run individually in participants' residential halls. FILES 49 CSV files for 47 participants: P01.csv through P47.csv, plus P24_run2.csv and P34_run2.csv, which are second recording sessions from two participants. Analyses combine each participant's sessions into a single record, giving 47 distinct participants. COLUMNS subject_id participant code (P01-P47) timestamp Unix timestamp type record type (raw sample or band-power packet) value signal value in microvolts alpha, beta, band powers reported by the device at 1 Hz gamma, theta attention NeuroSky eSense attention score (0-100) image stimulus filename, or instruction_screen label complexity class of the stimulus phase trial phase (instruction, fixation, task) target_instruction the target the participant was asked to find reaction_time time to locate the target, in seconds is_artifact flag for samples exceeding the artifact threshold PROCESSING STATE Signals are preprocessed rather than raw: converted from 12-bit ADC units to microvolts, band-pass filtered 1-50 Hz (fourth-order Butterworth, zero-phase), notch filtered at 50 Hz, denoised with a Daubechies-4 wavelet over five levels, and screened for residual artifacts with a sliding 5-second z-score step. Samples exceeding +/-100 microvolts are flagged in is_artifact. PRIVACY Participants are identified only by code. All personal identifiers were removed from filenames and from every field before deposit. The name-to-code key is not part of this deposit and is held privately by the corresponding author. papers.title: An Integrated Framework for Weldability of Metallic Materials
papers.venue: Preprints.org
topics: Microstructure and Mechanical Properties of Steels
papers.abstract: Steel weldability remains a central issue in materials engineering, affecting structural integrity, manufacturing reliability, and lifecycle performance across many industries. This paper examines weldability from an integrated perspective that combines metallurgical fundamentals, quality assurance methodologies, and emerging artificial intelligence (AI) tools. Key metallurgical aspects including phase transformations, heat-affected zone behavior, grain refinement, and microstructural heterogeneity—are discussed in relation to weld quality and mechanical performance. Limitations of conventional destructive and non-destructive inspection methods are considered in the context of increasingly complex welding requirements. The study further analyzes the role of AI-assisted approaches, such as machine learning, computer vision, and predictive modeling, in improving defect detection, process monitoring, and weld evaluation. By linking microstructural information with performance indicators and incorporating intelligent monitoring systems, the work outlines a data-driven framework for adaptive quality control and more reliable welding processes.

papers.title: A Comprehensive Review of Deep Learning in Agricultural Visual Perception: Progress, Bottlenecks, and Emerging Trends
papers.venue: Agriculture
papers.abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive review of deep learning in agricultural visual perception. Climate change and land degradation demand a shift from experience-driven to data-driven intelligent agriculture. Traditional manual inspections remain subjective and unscalable. Computer vision offers a non-invasive solution for precision crop and livestock management, while challenges also exist. Its application in actual agricultural scenarios faces specific challenges such as severe occlusion, drastic changes in lighting, and non-rigid deformation of biological targets. To systematically summarize how these perception bottlenecks are being resolved, this review explores deep learning architectures featuring spatial extraction and spatio-temporal modeling. This comprehensive review first constructs a progressive analytical framework from low-level data augmentation and static spatial cognition to high-level dynamic spatio-temporal reasoning, and then systematically classifies existing literature. In-depth analysis reveals that these three core challenges can be computationally resolved using three unified technologies. Domain drift and label scarcity, rather than baseline accuracy, are the main obstacles to practical deployment. We further identified four priority research directions, i.e., architectural efficiency, data-level annotation efficiency, deployment-level privacy and simulation, and trust-level security, to guide future research.

papers.title: Reproducibility materials for "Reconstructing Research Fields under Vocabulary Drift: An Auditable Boundary-Aware Bibliometric Workflow Applied to Empirical Legal Studies (2015–2026)"
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This repository contains the complete reproducibility materials associated with the study “Reconstructing Research Fields under Vocabulary Drift: An Auditable Boundary-Aware Bibliometric Workflow Applied to Empirical Legal Studies (2015–2026)” The deposited materials support an updated bibliometric reconstruction based on OpenAlex records retrieved in 2026. The package includes the raw bibliographic records, documented screening decisions, processed corpora, methodological and applied subsets, computational-frontier sensitivity data, co-citation network data, bibliometric tables, analysis scripts, metadata, and documentation required to reproduce the main analyses. The study distinguishes a methodological core of Empirical Legal Studies from applied empirical legal research and from the emerging computational frontier involving natural language processing, machine learning, and large language models. The repository is intended to provide a transparent and auditable record of data retrieval, screening, classification, network construction, and bibliometric analysis. The deposited OpenAlex-based reconstruction should not be interpreted as a Scopus or Web of Science dataset. Database provenance, search strategy, inclusion criteria, and methodological limitations are documented in the accompanying files.
