papers.title: Single-port robotic areolar thyroidectomy: technical feasibility and clinical outcomes of 64 consecutive cases
papers.venue: Journal of Robotic Surgery
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Single-port robotic areolar (SPRA) thyroidectomy is a recent refinement of the bilateral axillo-breast approach (BABA) that employs the da Vinci single-port system to establish a single-trajectory corridor while preserving a scarless neck. However, clinical data remain limited. The present study evaluated whether SPRA is clinically feasible and technically safe. Methods This retrospective study analyzed 64 consecutive women who underwent SPRA at a single center between March and September 2025. We compared flap dissection extent between SPRA and BABA using a standardized grid-based model and analyzed perioperative outcomes. Console time was stratified by laterality, body mass index (BMI), and learning phase via cumulative sum (CUSUM) analysis. Results Less-than-total and total thyroidectomy were performed in 59 (92.2%) and 5 (7.8%) patients, respectively. The mean console time was 69.3 ± 27.4 min and did not differ significantly by laterality or correlate significantly with BMI. CUSUM analysis showed an inflection point at case 15; the late phase (cases 16–60) had significantly shorter console times than the early phase (cases 1–15) (62.9 vs 82.4 min; mean difference, 19.5 min; p = 0.017). SPRA had an approximately 30% smaller flap dissection area than BABA. No conversions occurred. Transient vocal cord palsy affected six patients (9.4%) and transient hypoparathyroidism affected one (20% of total thyroidectomies), with no permanent complications. Conclusions SPRA demonstrated reduced flap dissection, consistent operative performance, and early stabilization of console time. These findings support SPRA as a safe and feasible integrated platform for remote-access thyroidectomy.

papers.title: agrifoodTEF Presentation of the Irish node
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: agrifoodTEF is a network of test and experimentation infrastructures in Europe that supports Agri-Food technology companies to do near product validation of their AI and Robotics solutions, using real-world facilities. In this material we are presenting the Irish node. The irish node is led by Munster Technological University (MTU), which provides testing and validation services for AgriTech and Agrifood SMEs developing AI, robotics and digital technologies. Through the IMaR Research Centre and the AgriTech Ireland Cluster, the Irish Node helps companies validate AI models, sensors and robotic solutions, benchmark accuracy and system integration, and generate the technical and business evidence needed to support product and market decisions. Testing can take place at MTU's facilities or directly at a company's own site, covering areas such as livestock, arable farming and food processing.

papers.title: Historical Tables from Berlin State Library
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: In document layout analysis (DLA), the detection and classification of multiple classes of layout elements such as text regions, images, tables etc. is required in order to extract and process them in subsequent steps. This proves to be a challenging task in digitised cultural heritage items such as historical books, periodicals and handwritten records, especially with regard to the fact that tables are traditionally predominantly composed of text but with widely varying table layouts over the course of time. Despite all the progress in the fields of computer vision and pattern recognition, the automatic recognition and extraction of the contents of historical tables as structural data continue to pose significant challenges for software solutions. The primary intention of the publication of this dataset was the provision of a large computationally amenable dataset exclusively consisting of images of tables from historical documents to stimulate research and development of suitable methods and applications. In 2026, a generic automated data extraction tool for (historical) tabular sources still forms a desideratum. In this respect, the dataset provided here aims to make a contribution to filling this gap. The dataset is suitable for the computational use of digitised collections according to the Collections as Data principles. In order to enable the establishment of a ground truth dataset for table detection in digitised cultural heritage items, this dataset was compiled from the Digitised Collections of the Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin. It comprises 5,000 images of tables in .png format; the images were derived from 861 documents published between 1500 and 1930. The dataset consists of a single tar.gz-file as well as a filelisting.

papers.title: How Do You Use AI in Mathematical Expression and Apply it in Teaching and Learning Computer Studies
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper explored how AI can be applied in mathematics expression and in the teaching and learning of Computer Studies. AI-driven approaches enable mathematicians to leverage vast computational resources and data-driven insights, opening new avenues for research and pushing the boundaries of mathematical knowledge. The paper provides an overview of key AI concepts and methods relevant to mathematics, including symbolic reasoning, theorem proving, numerical optimization, and pattern recognition. The paper also presented case studies and practical examples demonstrating the successful application of AI in various subfields of Computer Studies, such as using generative models and 3D deep learning to synthesize and complete 3D shapes from partial or noisy observations, such as single-view images, sketches, or point clouds, which can be used for 3D modeling, animation, and printing. It concludes with a vision for the future of AI driven mathematics, emphasizing the need for interdisciplinary education, open science, and responsible innovation especially in teaching and learning of Computer Studies.

papers.title: Overview of research and practice progress in body composition measurement techniques
papers.venue: Frontiers in Medical Technology
papers.abstract: The measurement of body composition is one of the most important tools for evaluating an individual's health and nutritional status. Its field has developed rapidly in recent years due to technological advances and growing application needs. Currently, widely used measurement methods include dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry (DXA), bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA), Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), Computed Tomography (CT), and smartphone software based on Computer Vision (CV) and Artificial Intelligence (AI). Each method has its own advantages in terms of accuracy and convenience. However, these techniques still face problems related to measurement reliability and applicability across different populations. The purpose of this paper is to provide a comprehensive overview of the technologies, target populations, and research fields related to body composition measurement. Body composition measurement is an important part of health management, non-communicable disease management, clinical medicine, and sports and physical training. Along with new scientific advances, this article also presents potential future research directions in body composition measurement.

papers.title: Contextualized Probabilistic Programming with Bayesian Neural Network Embeddings
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Probabilistic programming (PP) offers a powerful approach to modeling uncertainty and performing inference. However, a significant challenge remains in effectively incorporating complex, real-world data distributions, particularly those exhibiting high dimensionality and intricate dependencies. This work proposes a novel framework that addresses this limitation by directly embedding Bayesian Neural Networks (BNNs) into probabilistic programming languages. The core idea is to leverage BNNs as non-parametric priors, learning a contextualized representation of the data that subsequently guides inference within the PP system. This approach allows for a more natural and efficient integration of complex data distributions, offering improved performance and interpretability compared to traditional PP methods. We formalize this framework with a set of equations detailing the embedding process, the BNN architecture, and the inference procedure. The proposed method demonstrates potential for applications in areas such as computer vision, natural language processing, and medical diagnosis where data complexity is paramount.

papers.title: Reply on EC1
papers.venue: OpenAlex
papers.abstract: Abstract. Attributing disturbance agents to canopy mortality in European forests remains difficult due to sparse, heterogeneous, and often single-agent reference data. We present DISFOR (Viehweger et al., 2026), a uniformly re-interpreted ground-truth dataset of forest disturbance agents, designed to serve as training data for multi-temporal classification and analysis of disturbance agents with Sentinel-2 time-series. The dataset comprises 3,822 unique sample points, each defined at the 10×10 m pixel level, labelled by disturbance event and agent and fully temporally segmented into consecutive events and forest states for the years 2015–2024. Labels follow a three-level hierarchical scheme that supports analyses from broad "alive vs. disturbed" partitions to specific agents such as bark beetle, windthrow, wildfire, and salvage logging. Samples were drawn from multi-source ancillary data (e.g. EFFIS, FORWIND, Copernicus EMS, and regional forestry datasets) and consistently re-interpreted using an open-source interface and generally available primary data like Sentinel-2 and very high resolution imagery. For each sample we provide interpreter confidence, cluster identifiers to capture spatio-temporal autocorrelation, and additional metadata. Alongside interpreted samples, we release two Sentinel-2 data products tailored to complementary use cases: (i) a tabular single pixel reflectance time series between 2015–2024 and (ii) georeferenced 32×32-pixel image chips centred on the sampled points suitable for computer vision applications, with Python utilities for reproducible data loading and filtering. The dataset is suited for training and calibration of both change detection and agent attribution algorithms at sub-annual resolution, it supports training on single timestamps as well as on time-series, and facilitates studies that integrate spectral dynamics with spatial context. By harmonizing multiple first-level disturbance agent products and providing dense, temporally explicit labels, this resource lowers a major barrier to developing European forest disturbance and recovery monitoring.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Forensic Nursing
papers.venue: OpenAlex
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education
papers.abstract: This chapter explores the emerging role of artificial intelligence (AI) in forensic nursing and its potential to transform forensic healthcare practice, investigation, education, and research. It introduces key concepts of artificial intelligence, including machine learning, natural language processing, computer vision, and predictive analytics, and explains their relevance within forensic nursing settings. It also discusses the application of AI in digital forensics, tele-forensic nursing, surveillance data analysis, and the identification of trends in violence, trauma, and abuse. Ethical, legal, and professional considerations related to the use of AI in forensic nursing are critically addressed, including issues of data privacy, confidentiality, bias, accountability, informed consent, and the admissibility of AI-assisted findings in court.

papers.title: DEVELOPMENT OF A SYSTEM FOR PRODUCT QUALITY CONTROL AND MANAGEMENT OF THE MOVEMENT OF DEFECTIVE PRODUCTS BASED ON DIGITAL TECHNOLOGIES
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The rapid development of digital technologies has created new opportunities for improving product quality control and automating the management of defective products in modern manufacturing systems. Traditional quality-control approaches are often characterized by manual inspection, delayed decision-making, limited traceability, and dependence on operator experience. This study proposes a digital system for automated product quality control and management of the movement of defective products during the manufacturing process. The proposed system integrates industrial computer vision, artificial intelligence, digital product identification, Internet of Things technologies, programmable logic controllers, sensors, industrial communication networks, and automated actuators. The system captures product images, performs automated analysis, identifies potential defects, determines the quality status of each product, associates the inspection result with a unique digital identifier, and automatically directs defective products to designated routes. A mathematical model is proposed to determine the required response time for reliable product sorting based on conveyor velocity and the distance between the inspection and sorting stations. The study demonstrates that integrating digital inspection with automated material-flow management can improve product traceability, reduce human error, minimize defective-product leakage, and increase the efficiency of manufacturing quality management. The proposed system provides a technological foundation for smart manufacturing and can contribute to the transition from conventional quality inspection toward real-time, predictive, and intelligent quality management.

papers.title: Monitoring and analysing human–nature interaction through sensor and vision technologies
papers.venue: Open Collections
papers.abstract: Urban nature supports environmental sustainability, public health, recreation, and everyday urban life. Rapid advances in sensing technologies, crowdsourced digital platforms, computer vision, and artificial intelligence are transforming how human activities and environmental experiences are monitored and interpreted in cities. However, research often emphasises static environmental indicators or visitor counts, with less attention to the behavioural, experiential, and semantic dimensions of human–nature interaction. This dissertation adopts a computational, human-centred approach to studying human–nature interaction (HNI) in urban environments. It aims to: (1) identify how sensor- and vision-based technologies have been used to monitor human behaviour in natural areas and assess limitations in the literature; (2) evaluate sensing systems for monitoring device-based proxies of visitor presence and movement in urban parks; and (3) develop scalable computer-vision and multimodal-AI frameworks to classify photographed representations of HNI and examine their spatiotemporal patterns. These objectives are addressed through a scoping review, field sensing experiments, crowdsourced social-media analysis, computer vision, vision–language models, and spatial analysis. The review found a strong emphasis on visitor counts and movement trajectories, with fewer studies examining activity, interaction, or environmental experience (Chapter 2). Bluetooth Low Energy analyses showed that calibrated, low-cost systems can provide scalable indicators of visitor presence and movement under suitable site conditions, but do not directly measure people or experience (Chapter 3). Using crowdsourced photographs and multimodal AI, the dissertation classified whether nature was represented as a setting, visual subject, or interaction partner (Chapter 4). Spatiotemporal analyses showed that these photographed, AI-classified representations varied across Vancouver’s urban contexts, environmental settings, and time periods (Chapter 5). Overall, the findings support a shift from viewing urban nature solely as ecological infrastructure or static green coverage towards understanding it as an experiential system shaped through movement, perception, activity, and interaction. The dissertation advances human-centred public-life research in computational urbanism by integrating sensing and AI with questions of human–nature interaction, environmental engagement, and everyday public life.

papers.title: Enhancing Multimodal Systems using Azure AI Image Embeddings and GPT-4.x Vision
papers.venue: Athens Journal of Τechnology & Engineering
papers.abstract: Image embeddings have become foundational in AI, enabling machines to transform visual data into structured numerical vectors for applications from predictive analytics to interactive user experiences. This paper presents a comprehensive study of Azure AI's image embedding technologies and their integration with GPT-4.x Vision to enhance multimodal retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems. We analyze the comparative strengths of Azure Machine Learning custom pipelines, the Azure AI Model Inference API, and Computer Vision v4.0 multimodal embeddings. The integration of CLIP embeddings and hybrid decomposition strategies is explored, with empirical results from a predictive maintenance case study. Theoretical frameworks, solution architectures, and experimental results are illustrated with six original schemas and diagrams, providing practical guidance for deploying scalable, accurate, and cost-efficient multimodal AI systems. Keywords: ChatGPT, AI, Generative AI, AI Foundry, Vector Search, Open AI, Azure AI Vision, Microsoft Azure, Image Embeddings, Predictive Analysis, IoT, Power Platform

papers.title: Multimedia Digital Resources for African Tone Languages
papers.venue: Mendeley Data
papers.abstract: The dataset is a multimodal collection comprising digital images and natural-language speech recordings associated with selected food and agricultural product categories. The dataset was developed to support research and applications in areas such as multimedia computing, computer vision, speech processing, natural language processing, multilingual computing, image classification, speech recognition, and indigenous language technology. The dataset is organized into two principal folders: Image and Sound. The Image folder contains categorized visual representations of food and agricultural products, while the Sound folder contains spoken-word pronunciations corresponding to the represented items in four languages: English, Yoruba, Hausa, and Igbo. The Image folder contains a total of 94 image files in JPG format, systematically distributed across six food and agricultural product categories: cereal, fruit, grain, herb, tuber, and vegetable. The cereal category contains 8 images, the fruit category contains 26 images, the grain category contains 12 images, the herb category contains 18 images, while the tuber and vegetable categories contain 15 images each. Thus, the six categories collectively constitute the 94 JPG image files in the dataset. Each image represents an item belonging to one of the specified food and agricultural product categories. The category-based organization provides a structured visual dataset that can facilitate research and experimentation in image recognition, visual object retrieval, computer vision, and multimodal learning tasks. The Sound folder contains 175 natural-language speech recordings corresponding to the food and agricultural products represented in the image collection. The speech recordings provide verbal pronunciations of the associated items in four languages: English, Yoruba, Hausa and Igbo. All sound recordings are stored in WAV (.wav) format. The multilingual structure makes the dataset potentially useful for research involving multilingual speech recognition, pronunciation modelling, speech-to-text systems, African language technologies, language identification, and image–speech association. The dataset is arranged hierarchically to make individual categories and languages easily identifiable. Users can access the Image folder to obtain the visual component and the Sound folder to obtain the multilingual speech component. The Sound folder contains a total of 175 natural-language speech recordings associated with the food and agricultural products represented in the Image folder. The Sound folder is organized first according to the six food and agricultural product categories: cereal, fruit, grain, herb, tuber, and vegetable. Within each category folder, four language-specific subfolders are provided: English, Yoruba, Hausa, and Igbo. These language folders contain spoken-word pronunciations of the corresponding items in the respective languages. All speech recordings are stored in .wav format.

papers.title: AI-Enabled Education: Reconstruction of a Computer Vision Curriculum
papers.venue: Frontiers in artificial intelligence and applications
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI
papers.abstract: This study examines the reconstruction of a Computer Vision course in an application-oriented university, transitioning from OpenCV to the Huawei Ascend AI Platform. By comparing two cohorts’ academic performance, we evaluate the reconstruction’s impact on learning achievement and instructional equity. Results show that the reform cohort significantly outperformed the pre-reform cohort in total and final-exam scores, with more balanced score distribution: reduced standard deviation, fewer low scores, and more middle-to-high scores. These improvements reflect the combined effect of platform replacement and pedagogical reform. Based on these findings, we propose a five-in-one reconstruction framework-platform replacement, content adjustment, environment upgrade, faculty transformation, and resource integration. This study provides empirical evidence for implementing domestic AI platforms in higher education, along with replicable strategies for AI-enabled curriculum reform. Limitations include the narrow sample and short-term focus; future work should broaden samples and conduct longitudinal tracking.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Multimodal Environmental Communication: Text, Image and Sound
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Environmental communication plays a critical role in shaping public understanding, attitudes, and actions toward environmental sustainability and climate change. Environmental challenges such as climate change, deforestation, pollution, and biodiversity loss require effective communication strategies that can reach diverse audiences and inspire action. Traditionally, environmental communication has relied heavily on textual reports, policy documents, and scientific publications, which are often inaccessible to non-expert audiences. With the rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI), new possibilities have emerged for enhancing environmental communication through multimodal approaches that integrate text, image, and sound. This study explores how AI-driven multimodal systems can be leveraged to improve the effectiveness, accessibility, and persuasiveness of environmental messages. Drawing on Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and Media Richness Theory, the study examines the role of natural language processing, computer vision, and speech technologies in environmental advocacy, education, and policy communication. This study adopts a qualitative research design, combining conceptual analysis, content analysis, and case-based review to examine Artificial Intelligence in multimodal environmental communication. By addressing existing gaps in traditional environmental communication, this research highlights the potential of AI-enabled multimodal communication to foster greater public engagement, environmental awareness, and sustainable behavioural change. The study contributes to the growing interdisciplinary discourse at the intersection of artificial intelligence, communication studies, and environmental sustainability.

papers.title: Dynamic Kernel Learning for Adaptive Feature Extraction
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have achieved remarkable success in various computer vision tasks. However, a fundamental limitation lies in the use of static kernels, which are pre-defined and remain constant throughout the learning process. This approach assumes a fixed and optimal data distribution, a premise that is often violated in real-world scenarios. Consequently, static kernels can lead to suboptimal feature extraction, particularly when dealing with diverse and evolving data. This paper introduces a novel framework, "Dynamic Kernel Learning," designed to address this limitation. The system employs reinforcement learning to continuously adapt the convolutional kernel weights based on local data statistics and a learned representation of the underlying data distribution. The core claim is that dynamic adaptation significantly improves feature discriminability. The proposed method offers a self-adaptive feature extraction system capable of responding to evolving data characteristics, promising enhanced performance across diverse datasets.

papers.title: A Review of Deep Learning in Medical Image Recognition for Glaucoma
papers.venue: International Journal of Public Health and Medical Research
papers.abstract: Glaucoma is a leading cause of blindness globally, making early diagnosis and treatment critical for vision preservation. The advancement of deep learning has accelerated progress in medical image recognition, which offers new possibilities for intelligent diagnosis. This paper outlines the research background and significance, detailing techniques such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), image segmentation, and feature extraction. It reviews achievements in optic disc and cup segmentation, glaucoma classification, and model optimization, specifically discussing techniques such as transfer learning, data augmentation, and attention mechanisms to enhance model robustness, while noting limitations regarding data standardization, model generalization, and interpretability. Currently, computer-aided diagnosis demonstrates high accuracy and clinical potential. Future efforts should focus on refining datasets, developing lightweight models, and advancing interpretability and multi-modal learning to support glaucoma prevention and treatment.

papers.title: EcoScanner AI: An Explainable Computer Vision Framework for Real-Time Waste Classification and Carbon Mitigation Auditing in Circular Economies
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Municipal solid waste streams remain undercharacterised at point-of-disposal, impeding material recovery and climate-positive interventions. We present EcoScanner AI, an explainable computer vision (XAI) system that performs real-time waste detection and quantifies carbon mitigation potential for circular economy decision support. The core architecture fine-tunes a YOLOv8s model on a Roboflow-hosted YOLO-format export of the TACO litter dataset, achieving a mAP@0.50 of 37.66%, a precision of 93.82%, and an end-to-end inference latency of 12.47 ms (11.2 ms pure model forward pass) on a T4-class GPU. Explainability operates at two levels: Level 1 (Spatial) via bounding-box localisation and annotated overlays, and Level 2 (Contextual) by mapping detected classes to material categories with class-specific CO2 mitigation coefficients. The system implements a formal carbon mitigation accounting model that aggregates per-detection CO2-avoidance contributions, exposed through a Streamlit web application serving as an Environmental Decision Support System (EDSS), with SQLite persistence, bcrypt-backed identity verification, and a global leaderboard for behaviour reinforcement. A 7-day observational feasibility pilot with 18 participants recruited as a convenience sample from household and campus networks recorded 142 scan events and 3.42 kg of cumulative CO2-equivalent mitigation. Engineering for high availability includes model-resource caching and a cron-based keep-alive strategy. We report latency, throughput, and usability outcomes from this pilot and conduct a systematic ablation study justifying each architectural design choice.

papers.title: DEVELOPMENT OF A SYSTEM FOR PRODUCT QUALITY CONTROL AND MANAGEMENT OF THE MOVEMENT OF DEFECTIVE PRODUCTS BASED ON DIGITAL TECHNOLOGIES
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

papers.title: Computer Vision in Neurosurgery
papers.venue: OpenAlex
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education
papers.abstract: Computer vision (CV) is a field within artificial intelligence (AI) that enables computers to process and interpret visual data in a manner akin to human vision and cognition. With the rise of the internet, online image platforms and image benchmark datasets, 1 , 2 the paradigm of recognizing and learning from data patterns through machine learning (ML) became the most successful method for image processing in CV. Nowadays, deep artificial neural networks in AI achieve the best results in CV benchmarking. In this chapter, we dive into the key fundamentals of CV within the context of neurosurgery. We begin by exploring the applications of CV in preoperative settings. We introduce the term Intraoperative CV (iCV) to refer specifically to CV used during surgical procedures. Much like Intraoperative AI (iAI), iCV encompasses CV computations within the operating room (OR) setting. This distinction is crucial, as CV in surgery includes broad applications, many intersecting with radiology (primarily for diagnostic purposes). iCV mainly involves numerous models that directly impact surgical procedures in real time. This chapter will trace the development of CV in neurosurgery, from its applications in neuroimaging, surgical training, to use in the OR ( Figure 14.1 ).

papers.title: Investigações em inovação e tecnologia aplicadas à arquitetura e ao design / Investigations into innovation and technology in architecture and design
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
topics: Innovations in Concrete and Construction Materials
papers.abstract: Investigations in Innovation and Technology Applied to Architecture and Design brings together a collection of research mapping contemporary transformations in how space is conceived, taught, and materialized amid the integration of computational and generative technologies into ideation and fabrication processes in Architecture and Design. The volume follows an itinerary ranging from the recovery of bodily, gestural, and perceptive fundamentals of hand drawing to representational automation via BIM platforms, computer vision, and digital twins—traversing immersive environments in the metaverse, and culminating in generative artificial intelligence mediation within design conception, technical literacy, and digital fabrication, including 3D printing. Organized around thematic axes bridging education, representation, and technological innovation, this publication offers a disciplinary contribution to the fields of Architecture and Design by discussing the boundaries and potential of digital tools in contemporary education and design practice. See online in ITAD Research Group Site Investigações em inovação e tecnologia aplicadas à Arquitetura e ao Design reúne uma coletânea de pesquisas que mapeiam as transformações contemporâneas nos modos de pensar, ensinar e materializar o espaço diante da integração de tecnologias computacionais e generativas aos processos de ideação e fabricação em Arquitetura e Design. A obra percorre um itinerário que parte do resgate de fundamentos corporais, gestuais e perceptivos do desenho manual à automação representacional por meio de plataformas BIM, visão computacional e gêmeos digitais, passando por ambientes imersivos no metaverso, até chegar à mediação por inteligência artificial generativa na concepção projetual, na alfabetização técnica e na fabricação digital, incluindo impressão 3D. Organizada em eixos temáticos que articulam ensino, representação e inovação tecnológica, a publicação constitui uma contribuição disciplinar nos campos da Arquitetura e do Design através da discussão dos limites e potencialidades das ferramentas digitais na formação e na prática projetual contemporâneas. Veja online no site do Grupo de Pesquisa ITAD

papers.title: Machine Learning Using Python: Foundations, Algorithms, Applications, and Reproducible Research
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Machine Learning Using Python: Foundations, Algorithms, Applications, and Reproducible Research, Second Edition, is a graduate-level introduction to machine learning that integrates mathematical foundations, Python implementation, applied modeling, responsible machine learning, and reproducible research. The book develops machine learning as both a computational practice and a scientific process, with recurring applications in health, education, open machine-learning datasets, and computer vision. Accompanying source materials and executable examples are maintained in the book's public GitHub repository.

papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

AI-driven approaches enable mathematicians to leverage vast computational resources and data-driven insights, opening new avenues for research and pushing the boundaries of mathematical knowledge. The paper provides an overview of key AI concepts and methods relevant to mathematics, including symbolic reasoning, theorem proving, numerical optimization, and pattern recognition. The paper also presented case studies and practical examples demonstrating the successful application of AI in various subfields of Computer Studies, such as using generative models and 3D deep learning to synthesize and complete 3D shapes from partial or noisy observations, such as single-view images, sketches, or point clouds, which can be used for 3D modeling, animation, and printing. It concludes with a vision for the future of AI driven mathematics, emphasizing the need for interdisciplinary education, open science, and responsible innovation especially in teaching and learning of Computer Studies.

papers.title: Investigações em inovação e tecnologia aplicadas à arquitetura e ao design / Investigations into innovation and technology in architecture and design
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
topics: Innovations in Concrete and Construction Materials
papers.abstract: Investigations in Innovation and Technology Applied to Architecture and Design brings together a collection of research mapping contemporary transformations in how space is conceived, taught, and materialized amid the integration of computational and generative technologies into ideation and fabrication processes in Architecture and Design. The volume follows an itinerary ranging from the recovery of bodily, gestural, and perceptive fundamentals of hand drawing to representational automation via BIM platforms, computer vision, and digital twins—traversing immersive environments in the metaverse, and culminating in generative artificial intelligence mediation within design conception, technical literacy, and digital fabrication, including 3D printing. Organized around thematic axes bridging education, representation, and technological innovation, this publication offers a disciplinary contribution to the fields of Architecture and Design by discussing the boundaries and potential of digital tools in contemporary education and design practice. See online in ITAD Research Group Site Investigações em inovação e tecnologia aplicadas à Arquitetura e ao Design reúne uma coletânea de pesquisas que mapeiam as transformações contemporâneas nos modos de pensar, ensinar e materializar o espaço diante da integração de tecnologias computacionais e generativas aos processos de ideação e fabricação em Arquitetura e Design. A obra percorre um itinerário que parte do resgate de fundamentos corporais, gestuais e perceptivos do desenho manual à automação representacional por meio de plataformas BIM, visão computacional e gêmeos digitais, passando por ambientes imersivos no metaverso, até chegar à mediação por inteligência artificial generativa na concepção projetual, na alfabetização técnica e na fabricação digital, incluindo impressão 3D. Organizada em eixos temáticos que articulam ensino, representação e inovação tecnológica, a publicação constitui uma contribuição disciplinar nos campos da Arquitetura e do Design através da discussão dos limites e potencialidades das ferramentas digitais na formação e na prática projetual contemporâneas. Veja online no site do Grupo de Pesquisa ITAD

papers.title: Information-Theoretic Regularization of Deep Convolutional Networks
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
topics: Generative Adversarial Networks and Image Synthesis
papers.abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have achieved remarkable success in various computer vision tasks, yet they are notoriously prone to overfitting, particularly when applied to complex datasets. This paper proposes a novel regularization technique based on information theory, aiming to mitigate overfitting by explicitly incorporating the information content of the data into the training process. The core idea is to penalize network architectures that fail to capture salient information, thereby encouraging the network to learn more robust and generalizable representations. We introduce a loss function that integrates information-theoretic metrics, such as entropy and mutual information, as a regularization term. The method's effectiveness is demonstrated theoretically and conceptually, laying the groundwork for future empirical investigations. The key contribution lies in shifting the focus from traditional empirical risk minimization to a more fundamental understanding of information flow within the network, ultimately leading to improved generalization performance.

papers.title: Historical Tables from Berlin State Library
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: In document layout analysis (DLA), the detection and classification of multiple classes of layout elements such as text regions, images, tables etc. is required in order to extract and process them in subsequent steps. This proves to be a challenging task in digitised cultural heritage items such as historical books, periodicals and handwritten records, especially with regard to the fact that tables are traditionally predominantly composed of text but with widely varying table layouts over the course of time. Despite all the progress in the fields of computer vision and pattern recognition, the automatic recognition and extraction of the contents of historical tables as structural data continue to pose significant challenges for software solutions. The primary intention of the publication of this dataset was the provision of a large computationally amenable dataset exclusively consisting of images of tables from historical documents to stimulate research and development of suitable methods and applications. In 2026, a generic automated data extraction tool for (historical) tabular sources still forms a desideratum. In this respect, the dataset provided here aims to make a contribution to filling this gap. The dataset is suitable for the computational use of digitised collections according to the Collections as Data principles. In order to enable the establishment of a ground truth dataset for table detection in digitised cultural heritage items, this dataset was compiled from the Digitised Collections of the Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin. It comprises 5,000 images of tables in .png format; the images were derived from 861 documents published between 1500 and 1930. The dataset consists of a single tar.gz-file as well as a filelisting.

papers.title: Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Traditional Chinese Medicine
papers.venue: International Journal of Biology and Life Sciences
papers.abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) represents a valuable part of Chinese cultural heritage. It is characterized by complex compositions and multiple therapeutic targets, which pose significant challenges to its modernization research. In recent years, the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has enabled flexible, data-driven approaches that are now widely applied in TCM studies, including active ingredient analysis, quality control, and safety evaluation. This article reviews recent applications of AI in the TCM field, focusing on several key aspects: the advantages of graph neural network-based network pharmacology in analyzing multi-target interactions; computer vision and hyperspectral imaging for automatic medicinal material identification and quality grading; multimodal fusion techniques for component content detection and production process quality control; and graph attention networks and heterogeneous network representation learning for predicting TCM toxicity and assessing potential risks associated with combined use of Chinese and Western medicines. Based on a narrative review of the latest literature, this paper identifies current challenges such as data standardization and the lack of interpretability in model computation processes. Finally, it offers perspectives on how AI can support the standardization, precision, and global promotion of TCM.

papers.title: Confidence Thresholds: Towards an Automated Workflow for Unmarked Wildlife Population Modelling With Camera Trap Data
papers.venue: Ecology and Evolution
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT While ecologists are exploring the capacity of artificial intelligence to automatically identify wildlife in camera trap and other remote sensing data, it has yet to be commonly adopted in workflows that produce density or abundance estimates and thus many image datasets remain under‐analysed. There is potential to enhance image classification with deep learning ensembles which remain uncommon in wildlife studies, and to synergistically connect the output with population modelling in automated workflows. Here we present a repeatable workflow that connects these elements in a case study of macropods (Bennett's wallaby Notamacropus rufogriseus and Tasmanian pademelon Thylogale billardierii ) in Tasmania, Australia. We analysed a pre‐existing camera trap dataset with no contemporaneous field‐collected data. We used readily available computer vision algorithms to train a deep learning ensemble to classify the most common fauna in the dataset, achieving an overall classification accuracy of 94%. Once reviewed, we connected the output to a hierarchical abundance estimation process via a fully scripted workflow designed for repeat application, including the derivation of covariate data from spatial proxies. We then tested the use of classification confidence levels to subset raw (unverified) automated detections, by replacing the verified detection history with a series of automatically generated versions. We found that a detection history derived from a confidence level of 0.75 produced a highly comparable abundance estimate. Our analysis suggested that correctly identifying empty sampling occasions was more important to the estimation process than correctly identifying all occasions with detections. The potential to feed automated detection output that is subset with a classification confidence threshold into a modelling workflow, in place of costly manual verification, represents a high yield opportunity that is worthy of further investigation. In addition, our ensemble approach provides a tool for ecologists who study underrepresented fauna that occur in less frequently surveyed locations and habitats.

papers.title: Machine Learning Using Python: Foundations, Algorithms, Applications, and Reproducible Research
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Machine Learning Using Python: Foundations, Algorithms, Applications, and Reproducible Research, Second Edition, is a graduate-level introduction to machine learning that integrates mathematical foundations, Python implementation, applied modeling, responsible machine learning, and reproducible research. The book develops machine learning as both a computational practice and a scientific process, with recurring applications in health, education, open machine-learning datasets, and computer vision. Accompanying source materials and executable examples are maintained in the book's public GitHub repository.

papers.title: AI-Driven Surveillance Auditing to Police Ethically
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI
papers.abstract: The growth of Body-Worn Cameras (BWCs) and CCTV systems in law enforcement has generated unprecedented volumes of surveillance data, presenting new opportunities for enhancing transparency, accountability, and public trust. However, manual review of this footage remains slow, inconsistent, and often significantly delayed, creating substantial barriers to timely oversight. This study addresses this gap by designing an AI-driven surveillance auditing system capable of detecting unethical practices in policing — including acts of aggression, racial profiling, and procedural violations — to strengthen transparency, accountability, and public trust. Multimodal AI techniques are employed, integrating computer vision and Natural Language Processing (NLP). Computer vision detects aggression, facial expressions, and nonconforming gestures from video feeds, while NLP models analyse spoken language for hostile, biased, or inappropriate tones. These modalities are fused in a scoring engine to flag questionable behaviour and generate structured compliance reports, while a secure dashboard allows supervisors and external oversight bodies to visualise audit results in real-time or batch mode. The research targets a scalable, precise, and ethically aligned AI system for real-world policing. All datasets will be anonymised, and the system will be audited for fairness across race, gender, and contextual variables. Expected outcomes include a working prototype, peer-reviewed contributions to AI ethics in law enforcement, and a deployment-ready implementation framework. By automating surveillance audits, this research aims to accelerate accountability processes, standardise behavioural assessments, and strengthen public trust in policing practices.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Multimodal Environmental Communication: Text, Image and Sound
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Environmental communication plays a critical role in shaping public understanding, attitudes, and actions toward environmental sustainability and climate change. Environmental challenges such as climate change, deforestation, pollution, and biodiversity loss require effective communication strategies that can reach diverse audiences and inspire action. Traditionally, environmental communication has relied heavily on textual reports, policy documents, and scientific publications, which are often inaccessible to non-expert audiences. With the rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI), new possibilities have emerged for enhancing environmental communication through multimodal approaches that integrate text, image, and sound. This study explores how AI-driven multimodal systems can be leveraged to improve the effectiveness, accessibility, and persuasiveness of environmental messages. Drawing on Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and Media Richness Theory, the study examines the role of natural language processing, computer vision, and speech technologies in environmental advocacy, education, and policy communication. This study adopts a qualitative research design, combining conceptual analysis, content analysis, and case-based review to examine Artificial Intelligence in multimodal environmental communication. By addressing existing gaps in traditional environmental communication, this research highlights the potential of AI-enabled multimodal communication to foster greater public engagement, environmental awareness, and sustainable behavioural change. The study contributes to the growing interdisciplinary discourse at the intersection of artificial intelligence, communication studies, and environmental sustainability.

papers.title: Contextualized Probabilistic Programming with Bayesian Neural Network Embeddings
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Probabilistic programming (PP) offers a powerful approach to modeling uncertainty and performing inference. However, a significant challenge remains in effectively incorporating complex, real-world data distributions, particularly those exhibiting high dimensionality and intricate dependencies. This work proposes a novel framework that addresses this limitation by directly embedding Bayesian Neural Networks (BNNs) into probabilistic programming languages. The core idea is to leverage BNNs as non-parametric priors, learning a contextualized representation of the data that subsequently guides inference within the PP system. This approach allows for a more natural and efficient integration of complex data distributions, offering improved performance and interpretability compared to traditional PP methods. We formalize this framework with a set of equations detailing the embedding process, the BNN architecture, and the inference procedure. The proposed method demonstrates potential for applications in areas such as computer vision, natural language processing, and medical diagnosis where data complexity is paramount.

papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
topics: Generative Adversarial Networks and Image Synthesis

papers.title: Dynamic Kernel Learning for Adaptive Feature Extraction
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have achieved remarkable success in various computer vision tasks. However, a fundamental limitation lies in the use of static kernels, which are pre-defined and remain constant throughout the learning process. This approach assumes a fixed and optimal data distribution, a premise that is often violated in real-world scenarios. Consequently, static kernels can lead to suboptimal feature extraction, particularly when dealing with diverse and evolving data. This paper introduces a novel framework, "Dynamic Kernel Learning," designed to address this limitation. The system employs reinforcement learning to continuously adapt the convolutional kernel weights based on local data statistics and a learned representation of the underlying data distribution. The core claim is that dynamic adaptation significantly improves feature discriminability. The proposed method offers a self-adaptive feature extraction system capable of responding to evolving data characteristics, promising enhanced performance across diverse datasets.

papers.title: High-Dimensional Dissimilarity Indices
papers.venue: OpenAlex
papers.abstract: This chapter examines measures of dissimilarity for high-dimensional, low-sample-size data, with particular emphasis on their theoretical behavior and practical performance relative to the Euclidean distance. Dissimilarity indices are fundamental to multivariate analysis, underpinning clustering, classification, ordination, and visualization methods across diverse applications such as machine learning, genomics, and computer vision. While Euclidean and Mahalanobis are widely used for continuous data, they encounter serious limitations in HDLSS settings due to scale effects, singular covariance structures, and the phenomenon of distance concentration. The chapter reviews a broad class of dissimilarity indices, including Minkowski-type norms and other proximity measures tailored to different data types, and discusses their suitability for high-dimensional inference. Key theoretical properties, including concentration behavior and the distribution of row-wise summaries of dissimilarity matrices, are developed. The implications for clustering, nearest-neighbor methods, and multidimensional scaling are critically assessed. Applications to outlier detection, change-point analysis, and financial data illustrate how appropriate dissimilarity choices can alleviate high-dimensional pathologies and improve inferential performance.

papers.title: Embodied Emotions in Natural Language
papers.venue: OpenAlex
papers.abstract: Emotions are often felt in the body, and embodiment is a prominent mechanism supporting language processing. Here we utilized computational linguistics to map embodied representations of emotions in an English text corpus. The data revealed consistent embodied patterns for emotion categories. Comparison between semantics-derived and self-reported bodily maps of emotions revealed similar, discrete bodily representations of different emotions in texts and self-reports. Hierarchical clustering revealed three clusters: positive emotions within the head and chest, negative emotions within the torso and legs, and negative social emotions mostly within the head. Replication in a Finnish corpus yielded consistent results. These findings show that the bodily organization of emotional experience is reflected in the statistical structure of language, linking linguistic meaning to the subjective bodily experience of emotion.

papers.title: Convergent Parallel Mixed-Method Study of Frameworks and Consideration of Ethical AI-assisted Research Paper
papers.venue: North American journal of psychology
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education
Ethics and Social Impacts of AI
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and Natural Language Processing (NLP) technologies are being adopted both in academic research work as the emerging development of writing. Benefits and advantages these tools provide, however, come with ethical issues that challenge authorship, transparency, bias-base of research and research integrity. In this study we explore the affordances and constraints in AI-assisted writing tools and argue for an ethical framework enabling their effective use in an academic setting. We gathered data from 200 participants including academic researchers, graduate students, university administrative, AI developers and ethicists. Results of perceived benefits and risks of AI tools reliably predict ethical concerns, to some extent moderated by demographic group. Policymakers, researchers and institutions are outlined in the study’s horizon on how AI integration for academic writing can be ethically done. landmarks.

papers.title: Study of deep learning cues for cross linguistic part of speech tagging in English– Malayalam code-mixed data
papers.venue: Frontiers in Big Data
papers.abstract: Introduction Part Of Speech (POS) tagging is a fundamental task in Natural Language Processing (NLP) that assigns grammatical labels to words in a sentence. Code mixed text, which entails switching between two or more languages within a single conversation or a sentence, presents challenges for POS tagging. This investigation entailed a comprehensive study of deep learning approaches for cross linguistic POS tagging, focused on English Malayalam code mixed data prevalent on social media platforms. The study was carried out on linguistically complex and varied English Malayalam code mixed text from social media platforms with informal spellings, language switching, transliteration, slang, and unclear grammatical boundaries, reflecting the characteristics of informal online communication. We provide the first structured analysis of micro macro divergence and rare class behavior in English Malayalam code mixed POS tagging. Methods We evaluated 14 state of the art model configurations that span traditional sequence labeling approaches and multilingual transformer architectures. Models were compared using standard performance metrics prevalent in the domain of data science, supplemented by normalized confusion matrices, error prone tag identification and micro-macro F1 gap analysis. Results Our results showed that CRF (No Lang) emerged as the most balanced model overall on macro F1 (all classes) of 0.8170, while (BiLSTM + CRF) achieved the highest macro F1 (seen classes) of 0.8831, precision of 0.9167, and recall of 0.875, though this reflects strong performance concentrated on frequent tag classes rather than balanced coverage across the full tag set. Notably, the pretrained multilingual transformers (mBERT, MuRIL), despite prior exposure to Malayalam during pretraining, were outperformed on several key metrics by CRF and BiLSTM models trained directly on the code mixed dataset. Discussion This finding was contrary to our expectation that existing multilingual knowledge would translate into a clear advantage on this task and merits further investigation.

papers.title: Relational Neural Networks with Memory-Augmented Attention
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel neural network architecture, Relational Neural Networks with Memory-Augmented Attention (RNN-MAA), designed to address the limitations of traditional Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) in capturing long-range dependencies and effectively utilizing external memory. The core idea is to augment RNNs with a memory module coupled with an attention mechanism. The attention mechanism enables the network to selectively retrieve and integrate relevant information from the memory, guided by both the current input and the internal state of the RNN. This integration significantly enhances the network's ability to model complex, sequential data with long-range dependencies. We demonstrate, through a theoretical analysis and a detailed architectural description, how this combination of relational learning, memory augmentation, and attention provides a robust solution for tasks requiring understanding of intricate temporal and relational patterns. The proposed architecture offers a significant step forward in neural network design for tasks such as natural language processing, time series analysis, and graph neural networks.

papers.title: Predictive Coding of Relational Databases using Graph Transformers
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to relational database management leveraging Graph Transformers. Traditional relational databases, based on the tabular model, often falter when dealing with intricate and interconnected data. The core idea is to transform relational data into a graph structure and then utilize Graph Transformers to learn a predictive coding representation. This representation captures dependencies between tables, allowing for more efficient and intelligent querying. We posit that Graph Transformers' ability to model long-range dependencies, honed in areas like natural language processing, can be effectively applied to relational data, leading to improved query performance and a deeper understanding of the underlying relationships. This work outlines the architecture, the predictive coding mechanism, and the potential benefits of this approach, establishing a foundation for future research in this area.

papers.title: Monitoring students’ well-being through journal analysis—study protocol of an explorative approach using natural language processing on typed and transcribed entries to monitor and generate personalized feedback
papers.venue: Frontiers in Digital Health
papers.abstract: Background More than one-third of German students report high emotional exhaustion. One effective and low-cost method for improving emotional well-being is journaling, and advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly in Natural Language Processing (NLP), enable automated analysis of journal content for mental health monitoring. These analyses can be returned to users as personalized feedback, thereby enhancing the positive effects of journaling through increased self-reflection and creating an incentive for continuous use, which, in turn, improves monitoring. Journaling apps offer various input modalities (e.g., typing, speaking), potentially further increasing participation. Despite the promising potential of AI-powered journaling apps, their effects on mental health have so far been scarcely investigated. Research question This study investigates the performance of NLP models in predicting emotional well-being from journal entries. Specifically, it examines whether typed or spoken entries provide a more suitable input modality for these predictive models. Additionally, we explore whether receiving feedback is positively evaluated and which types of feedback students prefer. Method In a two-week observational study, N = 100 university students (aged 18 years and older) will be recruited and randomly assigned to one of two groups (speaking vs. typing). Following a baseline assessment, participants will submit daily journal entries and annotate them using reflective questionnaires on emotional well-being, stress, and journal topics. This information will be presented to participants as personalized feedback. Additionally, the performance of NLP models in predicting emotional well-being from journal entries will be evaluated separately for the two groups. Expected results We expect that emotional well-being can be predicted from journal entries using NLP, with transcribed entries yielding higher accuracy than typed entries. We also expect the feedback to be well-received. Discussion This study explores an accessible and engaging journaling application for monitoring and providing feedback on emotional well-being. It addresses several challenges in e-health research (e.g., high dropout rates, low user engagement). If this innovative approach yields strong user engagement and predictive performance, future work should evaluate automatically generated NLP-based feedback in journaling interventions to promote mental health. Clinical Trial registration identifier DRKS00034660.

papers.title: Cognitive Computing for Cybersecurity Threat Intelligence
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Current cybersecurity threat intelligence systems are largely reactive, relying on signature-based detection and rule-driven analysis. This approach struggles to adapt to the dynamic and often unpredictable nature of cyber threats. This paper proposes a novel cognitive computing system designed to enhance cybersecurity threat intelligence by mimicking human analytical reasoning. The system integrates machine learning algorithms for pattern recognition, natural language processing (NLP) for extracting insights from unstructured data, and knowledge representation techniques for building a comprehensive understanding of the threat landscape. The core mechanism involves creating a system that can not only identify threats but also reason about their potential impact, prioritize responses, and ultimately, generate actionable intelligence. This approach represents a significant departure from traditional methods, offering the potential for more proactive and effective threat detection and response capabilities. The system's architecture and key components are detailed, along with a discussion of the challenges and future directions for cognitive cybersecurity threat intelligence.
