papers.title: Revisión del estado actual de la Inteligencia Artificial en Bolivia
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This study presents a review of the current state of artificial intelligence in Bolivia between 2024 and 2026, covering adoption, research and development, computing infrastructure, human resource development, governmental and business applications, governance, and regional positioning. The review draws on government sources, multilateral organizations, regional indicators, scientific publications, technical repositories, university initiatives, and records of digital infrastructure. The evidence is analyzed according to different levels of technological capability, distinguishing between the consumption of AI tools, the integration of existing models, machine learning applications, fine-tuning, and the development of foundation models. The results indicate an ecosystem that is still classified as exploratory within the Latin American context, characterized by growing adoption of generative AI and institutional applications, but limited capacity in research, specialized training, data governance, and accelerated computing infrastructure. Local initiatives were identified in computer vision, natural language processing, applied machine learning, remote sensing, and economic analysis, alongside professional data centers and an emerging regulatory agenda. However, no public evidence was found of the training of Bolivian foundation models or of GPU clusters operating at a scale comparable to the leading AI hubs in Latin America. The review indicates that Bolivia is transitioning from a stage of fragmented adoption toward the early construction of an institutional AI ecosystem, while remaining strongly dependent on technologies, models, and infrastructure developed abroad.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence for microplastic pollution monitoring, predictive modeling, and risk assessment: advances, challenges, and future perspectives
papers.venue: Environmental Earth Sciences
topics: Effects and risks of endocrine disrupting chemicals
papers.abstract: Abstract Microplastic (MP) pollution constitutes a pervasive and complex environmental crisis, with particles infiltrating ecosystems globally and posing multifaceted risks to ecological integrity and human health. The inherent heterogeneity of MPs (in size, shape, polymer type, and degree of weathering) coupled with their presence in complex matrices, presents formidable analytical challenges that constrain traditional detection, quantification, and source-tracking methods. This review synthesizes the transformative potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) in overcoming these bottlenecks and advancing every facet of MP research. This review details how AI-driven computer vision automates the morphological analysis of MPs, while ML algorithms enhance the speed and accuracy of spectroscopic polymer identification. Beyond analytics, AI facilitates predictive modeling of MP fate and transport, enables intelligent source apportionment, and optimizes emerging remediation technologies. Using the United States as a critical case study, we examine the interplay between a fragmented regulatory landscape and AI innovation. However, significant challenges persist, including data scarcity, algorithmic limitations, and the gap between laboratory validation and field deployment. The reviewed findings argue that the integration of AI represents a necessary paradigm shift, moving from descriptive observation to predictive and prescriptive science. For this potential to be fully realized, concerted efforts in standardized data generation, interdisciplinary collaboration, and the development of transparent, robust AI frameworks are urgently required to inform effective mitigation policies and remediation strategies on a global scale.

papers.title: An Autonomous Guided Vehicle System for Smart Campus with Optimal Path Planning and Voice Interaction Using YOLO Network and LiDAR
papers.venue: Applied System Innovation
papers.abstract: Navigating large, unfamiliar campuses can be challenging for visitors, even with campus maps available. To address this issue, this study proposes an intelligent, autonomous campus navigation system to help users reach their destinations efficiently. The proposed system integrates computer vision, LiDAR, speech recognition, global positioning, and path-planning technologies to provide accurate, user-friendly guidance in complex environments. A YOLO-based neural network performs real-time building recognition, while a speech recognition module interprets users’ spoken destination requests and commands. GPS data are mapped to campus map coordinates to improve localization accuracy, and Dijkstra’s algorithm computes optimal navigation paths. All components are integrated into a graphical user interface that provides real-time visual feedback, including recognized building names and current location. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed system achieves reliable building recognition, accurate speech understanding, and effective route planning, significantly reducing navigation time for users unfamiliar with the campus. The proposed framework not only enhances smart campus navigation but also shows strong potential for extension to other large-scale environments such as hospitals and shopping malls.

papers.title: CrossMeta-ViT: Concomitant Cross-Attention Guided Multimodal Fusion for Skin Lesion Classification
papers.venue: Alfa Mühendislik ve Uygulamalı Bilimler Dergisi
papers.abstract: Skin cancer is one of the most prevalent and deadly malignancies, necessitating early and precise diagnosis to improve patient survival rates. While recent advancements in deep learning have produced robust computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) systems, the majority of these models rely exclusively on visual features extracted from dermoscopic or clinical images. Conversely, dermatologists synthesize visual cues with patient clinical metadata (e.g., age, gender, continuous bleeding, and itchiness) to reach an accurate diagnosis. Prior research attempting multimodal fusion has largely depended on black-box concatenation-based late-fusion strategies or simple neural compression modules, obscuring clinical reasoning. To bridge this gap toward Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI), we propose CrossMeta-ViT, a deep vision-transformer metadata-fusion framework designed for transparent skin lesion classification. The core contribution of this architecture is a Cross-Attention Fusion module. Instead of sequentially concatenating features, CrossMeta-ViT utilizes encoded patient tabular metadata as a Query (Q) to dynamically attend to visual image patches acting as Keys (K) and Values (V). This mechanism ensures that structural image features are selected and weighted under the direct guidance of the patient's clinical history. We evaluated the framework on the smartphone-captured PAD-UFES-20 dataset for binary classification (Benign vs. Malignant). Using 5-fold cross-validation, CrossMeta-ViT achieved a macro F1-score of 0.8723 ± 0.0009, malignant recall of 0.9927, specificity of 0.7651, and an AUC of 0.955, while the held-out single-split evaluation yielded an accuracy of 0.90. These results support the model as a recall-oriented and interpretable multimodal aid for telemedicine pre-triage rather than as a universally dominant classifier.

papers.title: Adaptive Topological Auto-generation
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper explores the application of Adaptive Topological Auto-generation (ATAG) to the modeling of complex geometric structures. The core objective is to generate novel topological structures with enhanced complexity and specific properties, opening up new avenues for both graph theory and computer vision. We propose a neural network-based model that learns the underlying topology from data and autonomously generates new topological structures. The paper details the model's architecture, training methodology, and initial validation results, demonstrating its potential for creating intricate and customized geometric representations. The focus is on the inherent flexibility and automated nature of ATAG compared to traditional methods.

papers.title: Applications of Artificial Intelligence in the Identification, Prediction, and Mitigation of Biofilms: A Scoping Review
papers.venue: Open Science Framework
papers.abstract: Background: Chronic wounds, including venous leg ulcers, pressure injuries, and diabetic foot ulcers, frequently fail to progress through the normal stages of healing due to the establishment of highly resilient, polymicrobial bacterial biofilms. These biofilms are protected by a dense extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) matrix, which renders them up to 1,000 to 10,000 times more tolerant to standard antimicrobials than free-floating bacteria. Traditional clinical diagnostics often fail to detect biofilms early or accurately at the bedside. Consequently, there is an urgent clinical need for innovative, non-invasive digital tools to enhance diagnostic accuracy. Objective: To map, characterize, and synthesize the available scientific evidence regarding the applications of Artificial Intelligence (AI)—including machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, and predictive digital models—for the detection or prediction of bacterial biofilms in patients with chronic wounds across various clinical practice settings. Methodology: This scoping review will be conducted in accordance with the PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews) guidelines and the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology [6]. The PCC (Population, Concept, Context) framework is defined as: • Population (P): Individuals with chronic wounds of any etiology (e.g., venous ulcers, pressure injuries, diabetic foot ulcers) . • Concept (C): AI-driven applications for biofilm detection or prediction, including machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, and digital predictive models . • Context (C): Clinical practice settings, including hospital, outpatient, primary care, and specialized wound care services. A systematic search will be executed across major bibliographical databases [6]. Two independent reviewers will perform study selection (screening and full-text reading) and data extraction using a standardized charting form. The extracted data will capture study characteristics, wound etiologies, AI architectures, input data types (such as clinical wound images or metagenomic sequencing data), and clinical outcomes. Synthesis and Significance: The gathered evidence will be synthesized using the PAGER framework, analyzing five key dimensions: Patterns, Avances, Gaps, Evidence for practice, and Research recommendations. By bridging advanced computer science and bedside clinical practice, this scoping review will provide a critical roadmap to guide personalized therapeutic interventions, improve clinical decision-making, and accelerate wound healing rates.

papers.title: Object Detection in Computer Vision: A Comprehensive Review of Algorithms, Datasets, and Evaluation Techniques
papers.venue: Preprints.org
papers.abstract: Object detection has evolved dramatically over three decades, transitioning from handcrafted features to deep learning, transformers, and now large language models. This paper provides a comprehensive systematic review of this evolution, covering traditional methods (SIFT, HOG, Viola-Jones), CNN-based single- and two-stage detectors (R-CNN family, YOLO v1–v12, SSD), transformer-based architectures (DETR, ViT, Swin), and emerging LLM-driven approaches (GPT-4V, Grounding DINO, YOLO-World). We benchmark and compare these methods using key metrics—mAP, IoU, FPS—and analyze over 50 datasets across generic, autonomous driving, medical, remote sensing, and agricultural domains. Our critical synthesis identifies persistent research gaps: lightweight edge deployment, sensor fusion for real-time systems, bias and fairness in AI, and multimodal vision-language integration. By consolidating three decades of progress and outlining future challenges, this survey serves as a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners developing accurate, efficient, and reliable object detection systems.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence for crop disease detection and management: A bibliometric analysis of global research trends
papers.venue: Plant Science Today
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative technology for crop disease detection and management by enabling rapid, accurate and automated disease diagnosis to support sustainable agricultural production. This study presents a bibliometric analysis of global research trends in AI-based crop disease detection and management from 2016 to 2026. Bibliographic data were retrieved from the Scopus database using a structured search strategy. A total of 3729 records were initially identified and 605 publications were retained after applying predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. Bibliometric indicators and VOSviewer software were employed to analyse annual publication trends, leading contributors, collaboration networks, keyword co-occurrence patterns, bibliographic coupling relationships and co-citation structures. The results reveal a substantial increase in research output, particularly after 2021, indicating growing scientific interest in AI-enabled crop protection technologies. Keyword analysis identified deep learning, machine learning, computer vision, transfer learning and plant disease detection as the dominant research themes. In contrast, co-authorship and co-citation analyses revealed strong international collaboration and a well-established intellectual foundation.

papers.title: Deep white balance and dark channel prior fusion: Toward efficient and natural low-light image restoration
papers.venue: Journal of Intelligent & Fuzzy Systems
papers.abstract: Image enhancement in low-light conditions is a challenging problem within the field of computer vision, since underexposed images generally lead to poor visibility, low contrast, noise amplification, and color distortion. Recent deep learning approaches have indeed shown promising performance, yet most of them adopt computation-heavy architectures and do not treat the luminance enhancement and color restoration separately; as a result cause unnatural restorations. To this end, in this paper, we present an efficient low-light image enhancement framework based on the Deep White-Balance (DWB) with Dark Channel Prior guidance in the YCbCr color space. The proposed framework separates luminance and chrominance components, making it easier to manage brightness enhancement and color restoration separately. This method aims to generate visually consistent enhanced images while preserving color fidelity and avoiding common enhancement artifacts. We evaluate the performance of the proposed method on reference benchmark datasets (LOL, LOLv2-Synthetic, and LIME) as well as a no-reference benchmark dataset (DICM). The experimental results demonstrate that, although state-of-the-art deep learning methods achieve higher numerical scores, qualitatively, the framework produces enhanced images with consistent contrast and illumination, while retaining color fidelity, all requiring less computational resources. Moreover, it does not require any further training or fine-tuning since the proposed approach is based on a pretrained Deep White Balance model and only uses inference. Experimental results show that the proposed method provides a convincing quality-efficiency compromise for low-light image enhancement.

papers.title: Self-Supervised Learning for 3D Shape Reconstruction
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: 3D shape reconstruction remains a challenging problem in computer vision and graphics, frequently hindered by the requirement for extensive, accurately labeled 3D data. This paper proposes a novel self-supervised learning framework designed to address this data scarcity issue. The core idea revolves around training a model to reconstruct 3D shapes from incomplete or noisy views, capitalizing on the underlying geometric structure inherent in 3D shapes. The framework utilizes a contrastive loss function to learn representations that are invariant to view variations and noise. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and a detailed description of the algorithm. The primary contribution lies in minimizing the need for manual labeling, significantly enhancing the practicality and scalability of 3D shape reconstruction. The resulting model demonstrates improved reconstruction accuracy compared to supervised approaches when limited labeled data is available. This work opens new avenues for applying 3D shape reconstruction to diverse domains, including robotics, medical imaging, and cultural heritage.

papers.title: DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION OF A REAL-TIME SMART ATTENDANCE CONTROL SYSTEM BASED ON ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, IN EDUCATIONAL ENVIRONMENTS
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Conventional attendance management approaches used in educational institutions are often time-consuming and vulnerable to recording errors, leading to incomplete or unreliable attendance data. To address these limitations, this study introduces an intelligent Smart Attendance System (SAS) that leverages Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Computer Vision techniques for automated attendance tracking and classroom surveillance.

papers.title: Urban Waste Detection Dashboard — Goiânia
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Initial public release of the GeoAI decision-support dashboard for visualization and spatial analysis of YOLO-based urban-waste detections in Goiânia, Brazil. papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Commerce: Transforming Business Operations, Decision-Making, and Competitive Advantage
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as one of the most transformative technologies influencing modern commerce. The rapid development of machine learning, natural language processing, predictive analytics, computer vision, generative AI, and intelligent automation is fundamentally changing how businesses operate, make decisions, interact with customers, and compete in domestic and international markets. In commerce, AI enables organizations to process large volumes of structured and unstructured data, identify patterns, predict market trends, automate routine activities, personalize customer experiences, optimize supply chains, detect fraud, and support strategic decision-making.This article examines the role of Artificial Intelligence in transforming commercial activities, with particular emphasis on business operations, managerial decision-making, customer relationship management, marketing, finance, supply chain management, human resource management, and competitive advantage. The study adopts a conceptual and descriptive research approach based on secondary sources, including academic literature, industry reports, books, and institutional publications. The article argues that AI can generate significant improvements in operational efficiency, cost optimization, innovation, responsiveness, and customer value. However, the adoption of AI also creates challenges involving data privacy, cybersecurity, algorithmic bias, workforce displacement, transparency, ethical responsibility, regulatory compliance, and implementation costs. The article proposes a responsible and strategically integrated approach to AI adoption in commerce, emphasizing human oversight, data governance, employee development, ethical standards, and continuous technological evaluation. The study concludes that AI should not merely be viewed as an automation technology but as a strategic capability that can reshape business models and create sustainable competitive advantage when effectively integrated with organizational resources and human expertise.

papers.title: "SCIMD-25: Source Camera Identification \u2014 Mobile Devices 25"
papers.venue: IEEE DataPort
papers.abstract: "SCIMD-25 (Source Camera Identification \u2014 Mobile Devices 25) is a large-scale real-world image dataset comprising approximately 25,000 images captured using 25 different mobile cameras. The dataset extends the previously developed SCIMD-17 by incorporating eight additional mobile camera devices, thereby increasing the diversity of camera hardware, imaging characteristics, acquisition conditions, and associated metadata. The increased device diversity makes the dataset suitable for investigating source-camera identification, camera model recognition, image forensics, device attribution, domain generalization, robustness evaluation, and metadata-aware machine learning. SCIMD-25 can also support research in multimedia security, computational photography, privacy-aware image analysis, and trustworthy computer vision. The dataset is intended to serve as a reproducible benchmark for researchers developing algorithms that analyze the relationship between image content, acquisition devices, and camera-specific imaging characteristics.\ud83d\udcf1 Smartphone Models Used in SCIMD-25The images in SCIMD-25 were manually captured by volunteers using the following 25 different smartphone models:\ud83d\udcf1 Xiaomi_M2101K6P\ud83d\udcf1 Infinix_Note40_Pro\ud83d\udcf1 IQZ9X_5G\ud83d\udcf1 MotoG45_5G\ud83d\udcf1 MotoG64_5G\ud83d\udcf1 MotoG85_5G\ud83d\udcf1 Nothing_A001\ud83d\udcf1 Nothing_Phone1\ud83d\udcf1 Oneplus_Nord_C3lite\ud83d\udcf1 Realme_6i\ud83d\udcf1 Realme8_Pro\ud83d\udcf1 redmi_9_prime\ud83d\udcf1 Redmi14C_5G\ud83d\udcf1 SamsungM13_5G\ud83d\udcf1 Vivo_V50_5G\ud83d\udcf1 VivoT1_5G\ud83d\udcf1 VivoY56_5G\ud83d\udcf1 Moto_g54_5G\ud83d\udcf1 Oppo_A17\ud83d\udcf1 Poco_M6_5g\ud83d\udcf1 Realme_11pro+\ud83d\udcf1 Realme_Narzo_N53\ud83d\udcf1 Redmi_9_power\ud83d\udcf1 Vivo_Y02T\ud83d\udcf1 Vivo_Y21G\ud83d\uddbc\ufe0f Image Pre-processing: All captured images were subsequently pre-processed and resized to a uniform resolution of 224 \u00d7 224 pixels, ensuring compatibility with commonly used deep learning and vision-language model (VLM) architectures. papers.title: Title: Non-Euclidean Regularity in Digital Images
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Digital images often exhibit irregularities, deviations from perfect uniformity, that can significantly impact image processing and analysis. This paper explores the concept of non-Euclidean regularity, a challenging problem in computer vision that aims to quantify and detect these deviations. We propose a novel method predicated on leveraging geometric properties to identify and characterize these irregularities. The core mechanism centers on identifying and quantifying patterns of non-uniformity within digital images, offering a robust approach to improve image quality and facilitate advanced analysis. The investigation focuses on developing a practical algorithm for detecting and measuring irregularity, with a clear focus on enhancing image processing and offering a new toolset for image analysis. This work represents an advancement in identifying subtle, often imperceptible, deviations from perfect uniformity, potentially leading to significant improvements in various computer vision applications.

papers.title: 基于动态拓扑的图像生成与重建
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel image generation and reconstruction algorithm based on dynamic topology. The algorithm leverages the power of dynamic topology to generate images with complex topological structures, offering a significant advancement over traditional image generation techniques. We detail the core mechanism of the algorithm, which involves dynamically adjusting the image based on topological transformations, enabling the creation of intricate and realistic visuals. The research explores the potential of this approach to produce high-quality images and highlights its novelty through the avoidance of static image generation methods. This work contributes to the field of computer vision by proposing a fundamentally new method for image synthesis and reconstruction.

papers.title: Axes of Greatest Variance: A Narrative Review of Principal Component Analysis
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Principal component analysis is statistics' most durable instrument: a linear algebra theorem that became data analysis's default first look. This article presents a narrative review of the primary literature of that instrument. The synthesis is organized around three themes: the founding formulations, in which Pearson's lines and planes of closest fit, Hotelling's principal components, and the multivariate canon of Mardia, Kent, and Bibby fixed the two definitions --- least-squares orthogonal regression and maximum-variance projection --- as one spectral problem solved by the covariance matrix's eigenstructure; the computational and applied consolidation, in which Golub and Van Loan's matrix computations, Wold's chemometrics tutorial, Jackson's user's guide, and Jolliffe's definitive monograph fixed the SVD's numerics, the scaling's choices, and the retention's rules --- from scree plots to cross-validation; and the modern extensions, in which Roweis's EM algorithms, Tipping and Bishop's probabilistic PCA, Bishop's machine-learning synthesis, Turk and Pentland's eigenfaces, and Abdi and Williams's survey carried PCA into missing data, latent-variable modeling, computer vision, and the general linear algebra of data analysis. It is concluded that the literature describes a single instrument's three lives --- theorem, tool, and model --- whose unity is the spectral decomposition: PCA's axes are where the data's variance lives, and every modern method that seeks structure in high dimensions still begins where Pearson and Hotelling began.

papers.title: Design of Computer Vision Algorithms Based on Multi-scale Analysis
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
topics: Advanced Image and Video Retrieval Techniques
papers.abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to computer vision algorithm design, centered around the concept of multi-scale analysis. Traditional computer vision methods often focus exclusively on extracting features from a single scale of an image, leading to limitations in performance, particularly in scenes with significant variations in object size and complexity. We argue that effective computer vision requires the ability to analyze information at multiple scales simultaneously. This paper proposes a framework for building computer vision algorithms that explicitly incorporates multi-scale analysis. The core mechanism involves decomposing images into feature maps at various scales and subsequently fusing these multi-scale features to enhance representation learning and improve overall algorithm performance. This approach addresses a critical gap in current computer vision techniques and offers a promising direction for developing more robust and accurate algorithms across a wide range of applications. The presented framework is theoretically sound and provides a practical guide for designing computer vision systems capable of handling the inherent complexities of real-world visual data.

papers.title: Adaptive Neural Network based on Geometric Structure
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel neural network architecture, the Adaptive Neural Network (ANN), designed to dynamically adjust its parameters and structure based on geometric features. The core principle of the ANN is to leverage geometric information to guide the learning process, leading to improved model performance and generalization capabilities. We explore a self-adaptive learning framework that continuously refines the network's connections and neuron activation based on the inherent geometric properties of the input data. The proposed method addresses limitations of traditional neural networks by offering a mechanism for fine-grained parameter optimization and a more robust representation of complex data. The research presents a framework that can effectively handle data with varying geometric characteristics, opening up possibilities for applications in areas such as image recognition, computer vision, and structural analysis.

papers.title: DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION OF A REAL-TIME AI-BASED SMART ATTENDANCE AND CLASSROOM MONITORING SYSTEM
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Conventional attendance management approaches used in educational institutions are often time-consuming and vulnerable to recording errors, leading to incomplete or unreliable attendance data. To address these limitations, this study introduces an intelligent Smart Attendance System (SAS) that leverages Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Computer Vision techniques for automated attendance tracking and classroom surveillance.

papers.title: Revisión del estado actual de la Inteligencia Artificial en Bolivia
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This study presents a review of the current state of artificial intelligence in Bolivia between 2024 and 2026, covering adoption, research and development, computing infrastructure, human resource development, governmental and business applications, governance, and regional positioning. The review draws on government sources, multilateral organizations, regional indicators, scientific publications, technical repositories, university initiatives, and records of digital infrastructure. The evidence is analyzed according to different levels of technological capability, distinguishing between the consumption of AI tools, the integration of existing models, machine learning applications, fine-tuning, and the development of foundation models. The results indicate an ecosystem that is still classified as exploratory within the Latin American context, characterized by growing adoption of generative AI and institutional applications, but limited capacity in research, specialized training, data governance, and accelerated computing infrastructure. Local initiatives were identified in computer vision, natural language processing, applied machine learning, remote sensing, and economic analysis, alongside professional data centers and an emerging regulatory agenda. However, no public evidence was found of the training of Bolivian foundation models or of GPU clusters operating at a scale comparable to the leading AI hubs in Latin America. The review indicates that Bolivia is transitioning from a stage of fragmented adoption toward the early construction of an institutional AI ecosystem, while remaining strongly dependent on technologies, models, and infrastructure developed abroad.

papers.title: A Probabilistic Programming Language for Multi-Modal Data
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic programming language designed specifically for handling multi-modal data. The core of the language leverages probabilistic models, data fusion mechanisms, and a powerful inference engine to facilitate probabilistic programming and machine learning tasks involving diverse data types such as images, text, and audio. Current programming languages often lack the necessary tools and abstractions to effectively manage and reason about complex relationships within multi-modal datasets. This language addresses this gap, offering a streamlined approach to integrate and analyze information from various sources, ultimately leading to more robust and accurate models. The paper outlines the key features and design principles of this language, emphasizing its potential for advancing research and applications in areas such as computer vision, natural language processing, and audio analysis.

papers.title: Adaptive Topological Auto-generation
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper explores the application of Adaptive Topological Auto-generation (ATAG) to the modeling of complex geometric structures. The core objective is to generate novel topological structures with enhanced complexity and specific properties, opening up new avenues for both graph theory and computer vision. We propose a neural network-based model that learns the underlying topology from data and autonomously generates new topological structures. The paper details the model's architecture, training methodology, and initial validation results, demonstrating its potential for creating intricate and customized geometric representations. The focus is on the inherent flexibility and automated nature of ATAG compared to traditional methods.

papers.title: Implementasi Metode WP dalam Pemilihan Skincare Menggunakan Computer Vision Berbasis Mobile
papers.venue: LOFIAN Jurnal Teknologi Informasi dan Komunikasi
papers.abstract: Selecting the right skincare products tailored to one's skin condition is challenging due to the vast array of available products and users' limited understanding of their own skin characteristics. Improper selection can lead to issues such as irritation, acne, and damage to the skin barrier. This study developed the "SkinPick" mobile application as a decision support system to assist users in obtaining skincare recommendations based on their facial skin type and condition. The Weighted Product (WP) method was employed to generate recommendations by considering six criteria: normal, dry, oily, sensitive, combination, and acne-prone skin. Additionally, the application utilizes Roboflow-based Computer Vision technology to identify skin conditions through facial scanning. SkinPick was developed using Flutter, Dart, and Firebase and subsequently tested using the Black Box Testing method. Test results confirmed that all application functions operated as intended. WP calculations identified Niacinamide as the optimal alternative with a score of 0.1899, followed by Hyaluronic Acid at 0.1880. Expert validation yielded a 93.33% agreement rate. The Computer Vision model achieved an overall accuracy of 90.1%, mAP of 89.2%, precision of 91.5%, recall of 87.4%, and an F1-score of 89.4%. These results demonstrate that SkinPick is capable of providing skincare recommendations in a more objective and targeted manner.

papers.title: Research on Five-Category Classification of Comment Emotions Based on the Multi-agent RAG Framework
papers.venue: Applied and Computational Engineering
papers.abstract: Because text comment sentiment analysis plays an essential role in applications such as online public opinion monitoring, user experience analysis, and intelligent customer service, it is rightly considered a core task of natural language processing with both great practical value and considerable research significance. However, it is also well known that current mainstream single-text sentiment classification models have inherent limitations.Because existing approaches suffer from superficial semantic understanding, insufficient logical reasoning capabilities, vulnerability to model hallucinations, and low precision in fine-grained sentiment classification, they are not suitable for complex comment sentiment recognition tasks. Hence, this paper naturally and elegantly proposes a dual-agent RAG framework combined with Coherence Theory (CoT), where a Q-Agent is charged with senthe paper presents a framework combining sentiment analysis and reasoning guidance with an RAG-Agent for knowledge retrieval and information enhancement, thus naturally and elegantly achieving precise five-category sentiment classification. More importantly, comparative experiments on a balanced sentiment dataset show that the proposed framework attains optimal improvements on all evaluation metrics relative to baseline models, and therefore achieves substantially better sentiment classification performance. As such, the work provides new technical insights for fine-grained text sentiment classification and clear practical guidance for agent technology applications in natural language understanding.

papers.title: Machine Intuition
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI
papers.abstract: Can an artificial intelligence system select the right action before it can articulate a valid reason for that action? Addressing this question at the intersection of reasoning, interpretability, agent safety, and latent computation, we develop a non-anthropomorphic definition of machine intuition as pre-explanatory competence: an action-relevant internal state that is sufficiently informative and causally involved to support a correct decision before a faithful natural-language explanation is available. Synthesizing evidence from chain-of-thought prompting, faithfulness interventions, hidden-state probing, activation steering, mechanistic interpretability, and latent-reasoning systems through 8 August 2026, we note that while final answers and tool-use choices can sometimes be decoded from activations before explicit reasoning begins, difficult multi-step problems are often solved during the generated reasoning trace itself - making token-level deliberation computationally consequential rather than merely explanatory. To separate these regimes, we introduce the Action-Explanation Timing (AET) framework and MINT-Eval, a causal evaluation protocol that distinguishes the earliest causally validated action state from the earliest sufficient, faithful, and interventionally supported explanation, while categorizing faithful latent competence, opaque success, rationalized error, and genuinely deliberative reasoning. The resulting answer is qualified: AI can sometimes act correctly before explaining why, but correctness alone does not establish human-like intuition or trustworthy reasoning; because the same timing gap can arise from useful latent computation, learned heuristics, shortcut features, or post-hoc rationalization, explanations must be treated as evidence to test rather than automatic proof of process, requiring high-consequence actions to undergo external verification, authority controls, and causal audits even when the model's first move is right.

papers.title: Research on Text Information Extraction and Imbalanced Classification Methods for Enterprise Profiling
papers.venue: Applied and Computational Engineering
papers.abstract: This research focuses on enterprise profiling in scenarios where large volumes of diverse texts—such as registration records, annual reports, news articles, and bidding notices—are continuously generated. Instead of relying solely on a single data representation or classification model, we developed a comprehensive natural language processing (NLP) pipeline for extracting key information and identifying industries. The pipeline consists of several steps. First, we use a BERT-BiLSTM-CRF model to identify core e/nterprise entities. Then, we combine TF-IDF with BERT embeddings to create a hybrid feature scheme that captures both lexical cues and contextual semantics. To address the challenge of imbalanced industry labels, we apply SMOTE in the dense semantic space and pair it with Focal Loss to enhance learning for minority classes. Additionally, we introduce a Stacking strategy to integrate outputs from different models, making predictions more stable. Tests on a self-compiled dataset covering ten national economic sectors and about 50,000 enterprises show that our method achieves a macro-F1 score of 95.4%. It outperforms traditional machine learning baselines and single deep learning models, offering more reliable recognition for minority classes. These results suggest that our framework is well-suited for applications such as supply chain partner discovery, industrial mapping, and targeted investment promotion.

papers.title: IndianConstitution: Programmatic Access, Search, and Analysis of the Constitution of India in Python
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: IndianConstitution is an open-source Python framework that provides structured, type-safe, and programmatic access to the Constitution of India. The package includes the complete constitutional corpus, covering the Preamble, all Articles, Schedules, and amendments through the Constitution (One Hundred and Sixth Amendment) Act, 2023. The framework offers fast full-text search through an inverted-index engine, typed data models based on Pydantic, graph-based analysis of constitutional relationships, multi-format export capabilities, and optional semantic search functionality for artificial intelligence and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) applications. IndianConstitution is designed for legal informatics, constitutional research, civic technology, legal education, natural language processing, legal AI systems, and computational social science. The package supports reproducible research through a versioned constitutional corpus, deterministic outputs, and offline-first operation. Key features include: Structured access to constitutional Articles, Parts, Schedules, and the Preamble High-performance constitutional text search Graph-based constitutional relationship analysis Data science integration through pandas and NetworkX AI and RAG-ready semantic retrieval capabilities Multi-format export to JSON, CSV, and Markdown Fully offline and reproducible operation The source code is openly available on GitHub and distributed through PyPI under the Apache License 2.0.

papers.title: Database of Byzantine Book Epigrams - Archive
papers.venue: Ghent University Academic Bibliography (Ghent University)
papers.abstract: This dataset is an extension of the publication of the Database of Byzantine Book Epigrams (2023). The 2023 publication is a copy of the data used for the live application on dbbe.ugent.be. The present dataset aims to offer a simplified structure of the DBBE data, facilitating computational research and data analysis. The dataset provides structured access to the data behind dbbe.ugent.be, enabling intuitive exploration and reuse. It is based on production PostgreSQL and Elasticsearch instances and is organized around six core concepts. The data is updated weekly to reflect the latest research and additions. Occurrences:Individual epigrams reproduced as faithfully as possible from manuscripts, preserving orthography and punctuation. Types: Normalized or critically established texts linked to one or more Occurrences, enabling comparison across similar Occurrences and providing interpretive metadata such as translations, genres, and subjects. Verses: Verses of Occurrences, grouped in Verse Groups to record textual parallels across Occurrences. Manuscripts: Metadata on the context of manuscripts, including provenance and related documentation. Persons: Information on authors, scribes, editors, and other historical or modern contributors linked to Occurrences, Types, or Manuscripts. Bibliographies: Structured references connecting literature and publications to the relevant entities in the corpus. Exploring the Dataset The dataset can be explored and analyzed in multiple ways: Web-based viewing: Tools such as SQLite Viewer allow users to simply upload the SQLite file and inspect its contents directly in the browser, requiring no technical setup. Graphical interface and export: DB Browser for SQLite offers an intuitive interface for browsing the data and exporting tables to CSV for further analysis without need for scripting based interaction. AI-assisted semantic querying: The database file can be uploaded to a large language model for natural language queries. For example, one could ask: "Give me five occurrences from the eleventh century discussing harbours." To protect sensitive data, consider using self-hosted models or paid, secure AI services rather than free online tools. Custom development: The structured SQLite format provides a robust foundation for programmatic analysis, integration with other tools like datasette, or the development of custom applications tailored to specific research questions. Database schema For a full visual of the database schema, please visit yED live. 1. Occurrences This table stores individual Occurrences (= short epigrams or poems, literally how they have been found in a manuscript, including marks for gaps and missing text.) Columns include: id, created, modified, public_comment, incipit, text_stemmer, text_original, location_in_ms*, completion_date_floor, completion_date_ceiling, palaeographical_info, contextual_info, manuscript_id, title *Note that, in the current version, the location of occurrences within the manuscript is given as plain text (ex. p. 394-395 for pages or f. 18r-18v for folia). For manuscripts that have more than 1 way of numbering pages, the alternative location is marked as f. 14r -- (alt.) p. 27. Related tables: occurrence_person_role: Links Occurrences to Persons, indicating which Role a Person plays in the given Occurrence. Example: Scribe ( = historical person), transcriber (=modern person), contributor (=modern person)... occurrence_genre: genre attributed to this Occurrence (Can be more than 1) occurrence_metre: metre attributed to this Occurrence (Can be more than 1) occurrence_management: Internal information. For example: To do's in the processing of this Occurrence occurrence_acknowledgement: Plain text acknowledgement of people who helped in the publication of this Occurrence. occurrence_text_status: An Occurrence text can have statuses like partially/completely (un)known occurrence_related_occurrence and occurrence_relation_definition: An Occurrence can be related to other Occurrence if (a) some of their verses share Verse Groups or (b) they share a Type. The relationship type is defined in occurrence_relation_definition. This works in one direction: if occurrenceA --> related to --> occurrenceB is set, then occurrenceB --> related to --> occurrenceA is not set. occurrence_keyword: Keywords telling what the Occurrence is about 2. Verses This table contains verse-level information about an Occurrence. Columns include id, occurrence_id, manuscript_id, text, order_in_occurrence, verse_group_id. Verse Groups are groupings of similar verses across occurrences. 3. Types This table contains prototypes of Occurrences. A lot of Occurrences have a high level of similarity. DBBE proposes prototypes for every group of similar Occurrences. Related tables: type_person_role: Links Types to Persons, indicating which Role a Person plays in the given Type. Example: Creator, Translitor, Editor, Contributor, ... type_genre: genre attributed to this Type. More than 1 Genre can be attributed. type_metre: metre attributed to this Type. More than 1 Metre can be attributed. type_management: Internal information. For example: To do's in the processing of this Type type_acknowledgement: Plain text acknowledgement of people who helped in the publication of this Type. type_text_status: Type text can be either completely known or partially unknown type_related_type: Groups of similar Types. The relationship is defined in type_relation_definition. This works in one direction: if typeA --> related to --> typeB is set, then typeB --> related to --> typeA is not set. type_tag: Explains the function of the Type (ex: introducing a subject, making a comment on the content,...). type_occurrence: Occurrences linked to this Type. Note that this is a many-to-many relationship: one occurrence can be linked to several types, one type can have several occurrence linked to it. type_editorial_status: editorial states for types. Currently only critical text / not a critical text. type_keyword: Keywords telling what the type is about 4. Manuscripts This table contains metadata about manuscripts. Related tables: manuscript_person_role: Any possible role a Person could play in the publication of this manuscript. papers.title: Asking open-ended questions promotes personal goal attainment in integrative negotiations.
papers.venue: Journal of Experimental Psychology General
papers.abstract: Prior research suggests that asking more questions improves outcomes in cooperative conversations, and a vast wisdom literature espouses the power of asking questions during conflictual conversations, too: negotiation experts suggest that questions invite counterparts to disclose information and, in doing so, put askers at an informational advantage. But is this advice necessary—and is it effective? We analyzed 61,057 speech turns from transcripts of 309 dyadic integrative negotiations and used natural language processing to estimate how often people ask questions, what types of questions they ask, and how well question-asking predicts personal goal attainment (Study 1; n = 618 MBA students). Open-ended questions were rare, occurring about once every four minutes (8% of turns). Yet, asking more open-ended questions was robustly associated with personal goal attainment. Closed-ended questions and non-question statements were not reliably related to goal attainment. We then tested causality in live chat negotiations: participants who were instructed to ask open-ended questions achieved higher personal gains than those instructed to ask closed-ended questions or to only make statements (Study 2; n = 1,452 online participants), and those instructed to prepare open-ended questions before their interactions outperformed those instructed to prepare statements (Study 3; n = 372 online participants). In all studies, the benefits of open-ended questions were tied to increased information elicitation and greater value creation. Collectively, these findings offer empirical support for the widely accepted—but rarely tested—claim that negotiators (and conversationalists broadly) focus excessively on influencing (by making statements) at the expense of learning (by asking questions).

papers.title: Designing a Framework for Evaluating Automated Requirements Elicitation Systems in Agile Projects: A Proposal Based on Quality and Reliability Criteria
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Designing a Framework for Evaluating Automated Requirements Elicitation Systems in Agile Projects: A Proposal Based on Quality and Reliability Criteria Hosein Tanabi1 1- PhD Student, Department of Computer Engineering, Islamic Azad University, Babol Branch, Babol, Iran Abstract Today, agile software development methods are recognized as a dominant approach in the software industry due to their flexibility and rapid response to changes. However, elicitation and management of user requirements in these dynamic environments remain a fundamental challenge [1]. The emergence of automated systems based on Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Large Language Models (LLMs) promises a transformation in this domain [2]. Nevertheless, the systematic evaluation of quality and reliability of these systems, particularly in the context of the Persian language, requires further investigation. This research aims to design a conceptual evaluation framework for assessing the quality and reliability of automated requirements elicitation systems in agile projects. The proposed framework is based on INVEST criteria and the INCOSE standard, and it has the potential to be implemented on real-world datasets of user stories. While some LLM-based systems demonstrate high capability in extracting functional requirements [3], they face challenges in identifying non-functional requirements and trust-related constraints, necessitating algorithmic improvements and the adoption of hybrid approaches. It is hoped that the presented framework can serve as a foundation for future research in the evaluation of automated requirements elicitation systems. Keywords : Automated Requirements Elicitation, Agile Systems, Evaluation Framework, Quality Assessment, Large Language Models, Persian Language Processing

papers.title: Neuro-Symbolic Programming with Reinforcement Learning for Automated Theorem Proving
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This research investigates a novel approach to automated theorem proving by integrating neural networks and symbolic reasoning through reinforcement learning. The core idea is to leverage the pattern recognition capabilities of neural networks to translate natural language queries into formal symbolic representations, while employing a reinforcement learning agent to strategically navigate the complex proof space. This framework aims to overcome limitations of traditional automated theorem provers by providing an adaptive and intelligent exploration mechanism. The system's performance is evaluated based on its ability to generate correct proofs for a range of mathematical theorems. The key innovation lies in the active guidance of the proof search process, enhancing both the automation and adaptability of the theorem proving system. The system utilizes a neural network encoder, a reinforcement learning agent, and a symbolic proof planner. The objective function for the reinforcement learning agent is designed to maximize proof progress, considering factors such as the reduction of logical clauses and the achievement of a valid proof structure. Experimental results demonstrate the potential of this neuro-symbolic approach for tackling complex mathematical problems.

papers.title: 基于高维几何的自然语言处理
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper explores the application of high-dimensional geometry to natural language processing (NLP). The core claim is that utilizing high-dimensional geometric structures can significantly enhance model capabilities, particularly in improving semantic relationships and contextual understanding. We investigate a novel approach involving the modeling of semantic relationships as geometric structures, leveraging the unique properties of high-dimensional space to improve model performance. This work introduces a new framework that integrates geometric representations into NLP pipelines, offering a potential pathway for advancing the field.

papers.title: 自适应几何张量优化算法
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm, termed Adaptive Geometry Tensor Optimization (AGTO), designed to enhance machine learning model performance, specifically in image recognition and natural language processing. Traditional optimization methods often require manual parameter tuning, while AGTO employs dynamic adjustments to tensor geometry and a self-adaptive learning mechanism to achieve efficient parameter matching and reduced computational complexity. The core of the algorithm lies in adapting the tensor's shape and density through a dynamic process, leveraging a novel self-learning technique to optimize the tensor's representation. We demonstrate the effectiveness of AGTO through extensive experiments comparing its performance against established optimization techniques on image classification datasets. The paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's design and performance, highlighting its potential to significantly improve model accuracy and training efficiency.

papers.title: Multi-Factor Financial Architecture: Integrating Near-Real-Time Stream Processing, Large Language Models, and Quantitative Risk Engines for Stock Advisory Systems
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper formulates an institutional-grade, multi-factor architecture for near-real-time automated stock advisory systems. By synthesizing tick-level market data from Bloomberg infrastructure with deep learning, natural language sentiment processing, and macroeconomic indicators, the proposed system provides regime-aware portfolio allocation signals [1]. We detail a multi-model ensemble combining Transformer decoders, hybrid long short-term memory (LSTM) networks, and gradient-boosted trees. To maintain empirical rigor, the methodology incorporates point-in-time data normalization to prevent look-ahead bias, cross-model LLM verification to mitigate hallucination risks, and fractional Kelly position sizing for risk optimization. Systemic dynamics—including latency constraints and correlated agent risks—are systematically analyzed to provide a clear technical blueprint for implementation and open-source benchmarking. Limited-live PoC available at https://trade.aiagentfolio.com.

papers.title: Are Climate Risk Risk Regulations Evidence-Based? Leveraging Artificial Intelligence to Bridge the Gap between Regulatory Practice and Academic Research
papers.venue: The Journal of Impact and ESG Investing
papers.abstract: This article presents an analysis of the connection between emerging climate risk policies in the banking sector and academic literature. The research focuses on regulations implemented after pivotal events such as the Paris Agreement led to increased scrutiny and mandated climate risk disclosures by financial institutions. By applying artificial intelligence and natural language processing techniques, the study analyzes 16 major global climate risk regulations, categorized into three distinct categories. We compare their outcomes with 83 peer-reviewed academic articles published from 2017 to 2024 to determine whether academic research outcomes influence those regulations. The findings reveal a moderate alignment (74.2% cosine similarity) between regulatory policies and academic research, indicating that although many regulatory bodies incorporate research insights, significant gaps remain. The article provides insights into enhancing emerging climate risk policies, suggesting a need for an evidence-based approach that integrates climate risk disclosure standards, climate risk management, and climate research into framework development. Theoretically, this study advocates for institutional collaboration among regulators through a polycentric governance system, which will help facilitate the effective integration of scientific research to strengthen climate risk policy management and development into the future.

papers.title: Adaptive Formal Semantic Learning
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to formal semantic learning, termed Adaptive Formal Semantic Learning (AFSL). The core idea is to enable a system to automatically discover and integrate new formal semantic rules from dynamic analysis of natural language text. Unlike traditional methods that rely heavily on manually crafted rules, AFSL leverages reinforcement learning to guide a model in this process. The model learns to extract and refine formal semantic rules based on contextual information and feedback, ultimately building a formal semantic knowledge base. The system's adaptive nature allows it to handle diverse linguistic phenomena and improve its understanding over time. This work addresses the limitations of static rule-based systems and presents a dynamic, self-improving framework for formal semantic learning. The key components of the system include a text analysis module, a rule learning engine utilizing reinforcement learning, and a formal semantic knowledge base. Evaluation demonstrates the system's ability to learn and apply complex semantic rules effectively.

papers.title: Automated Theorem Proving via Large Language Model Orchestration
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the potential of Large Language Models (LLMs) to contribute to automated theorem proving. The core idea is to orchestrate an LLM through a series of carefully designed steps within the theorem proving process. This involves leveraging the LLM's ability to understand and generate natural language, combined with a structured prompt engineering approach, to handle tasks such as hypothesis formulation, lemma retrieval, and inference verification. We explore a system architecture where the LLM acts as a central component, executing specific tasks based on prompts and iteratively refining its approach. The novelty lies in applying LLMs to formal proof systems rather than solely relying on traditional automated reasoning techniques. We demonstrate the feasibility of this approach through conceptual design and outline a strategy for effective prompt engineering, highlighting the challenges and potential avenues for future research. The goal is to create a system that can assist mathematicians and logicians in their work, and potentially accelerate the discovery of new mathematical knowledge.

papers.title: Arabic Emotion Classification Dataset for Large Language Model Evaluation
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This dataset contains 1,002 Arabic text samples annotated for five emotion categories: anger, neutral, joy, sadness, and fear. The dataset was collected and initially annotated by Shaima Alzubi, with a second independent annotation performed by Mohammed Almehrzi. Annotation disagreements were reviewed and adjudicated by Fady Alnajjar. The annotation process was conducted under the supervision of Fady Alnajjar, Omar Mubin, and Ons Al-Shamaileh. The dataset was prepared to support the evaluation of large language models and Arabic language models for emotion classification. It accompanies the study “Deployment-Oriented Evaluation of Large Language Models for Arabic Emotion Classification.” The dataset includes the Arabic text samples and their corresponding gold-standard emotion labels. It is intended for research on Arabic natural language processing, emotion recognition, text classification, and benchmarking of large language models.

papers.title: Neuro-Symbolic Program Synthesis via Relational Reasoning with Temporal Constraints
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neuro-symbolic program synthesis that leverages relational reasoning and temporal constraints. The core idea is to bridge the gap between neural networks, which excel at pattern recognition, and symbolic reasoning, which provides explicit modeling of constraints and dependencies. We propose a system consisting of a neural network for learning program structure, a relational database representing problem constraints and temporal rules, and a symbolic inference engine for generating candidate code. This engine utilizes the relational database to derive program logic based on relational constraints and temporal dependencies. The neural network then validates the generated code, ensuring its correctness. This approach aims to create executable programs from natural language descriptions, offering a more robust and explainable solution compared to traditional methods. The system's architecture allows for both efficient learning and transparent reasoning, addressing key challenges in program synthesis. The proposed method incorporates temporal reasoning to handle dynamic scenarios, a significant improvement over static constraint-based systems. The system's performance is evaluated through a series of synthetic benchmarks, demonstrating its ability to generate programs that satisfy both the logical constraints and the temporal requirements. The overall goal is to achieve a synergistic combination of neural and symbolic capabilities, leading to a more reliable and understandable program synthesis process.

papers.title: Supporting Artifacts for "Drone-AI Mobile Sensing Intelligence for Smart X: A Multimodal Human-in-the-Loop Architecture"
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This repository provides the supporting research materials for the study entitled “Drone-AI Mobile Sensing Intelligence for Smart X: A Multimodal Human-in-the-Loop Architecture.” The study proposes a reusable Drone-AI Mobile Sensing Intelligence architecture that reframes unmanned aerial vehicles from conventional flying cameras into multimodal mobile sensing platforms. The architecture integrates Drone-IoT payloads, telemetry, adaptive connectivity, edge-cloud artificial intelligence, data governance, and human-in-the-loop decision control to support accountable sensing and decision intelligence across multiple Smart X domains. The research follows a Design Science Research orientation and evaluates the proposed artifact analytically rather than through a full field deployment. The evaluation examines whether the architecture can support heterogeneous data capture, preserve telemetry and data quality, transform multimodal sensor streams into AI-based situational interpretation, and provide a governed pathway toward human-approved action. The repository is intended to support transparency, reproducibility, and future implementation of the proposed architecture. Supporting artifacts may include architectural diagrams, sensor taxonomies, workflow definitions, scenario parameters, analytical tables, illustrative PM2.5 data, readiness metrics, maturity levels, and other materials associated with the evaluation of the proposed Drone-AI sensing framework. The proposed architecture supports multiple sensing modalities, including: RGB, thermal, multispectral, hyperspectral, and LiDAR sensing; particulate and air-chemistry sensing such as PM2.5, PM10, CO₂, CO, SO₂, NO₂, O₃, and VOC; microclimate sensing including temperature, humidity, pressure, wind, rain, and cloudiness; acoustic sensing; telemetry including GPS, IMU, altitude, speed, battery status, route, and timestamp; and external contextual sources such as CCTV, satellite observations, fixed IoT stations, weather stations, and field reports. The repository also supports the paper’s data-to-decision workflow, in which sensing data pass through quality control, multimodal fusion, AI analytics, decision support, and post-mission learning, while a human-in-the-loop gate retains responsibility for anomaly validation, correction, approval, override, and response prioritization. The study demonstrates how the same sensing architecture can be adapted to smart city, smart environment, smart disaster, smart industry, smart mining, and smart campus applications. Representative use cases include air-quality monitoring, pollution mapping, fire and smoke detection, gas leakage inspection, dust detection, environmental assessment, safety monitoring, and institutional decision support. The current evaluation is conceptual and analytical. The PM2.5 scenario included in the study is illustrative and should not be interpreted as measured field data. Future work is expected to develop a staged prototype with modular Drone-IoT payloads, calibrated multimodal datasets, edge-cloud inference, and human-in-the-loop dashboard evaluation.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in oculoplasty: Current applications and future perspectives
papers.venue: Artificial Intelligence in Medical Imaging
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming clinical ophthalmology, with most validated applications in retinal and corneal imaging. In contrast, oculoplastic surgery – which encompasses eyelid, orbital, lacrimal, and periocular disorders – has only recently begun to incorporate AI into clinical workflows. Emerging applications include automated image analysis for eyelid malpositions, deep learning-based interpretation of orbital imaging, AI-assisted planning for dacryocystorhinostomy, and predictive modeling in reconstructive and aesthetic procedures. Despite encouraging results, challenges such as limited datasets, imaging heterogeneity, lack of multimodal integration, and regulatory readiness continue to hinder widespread clinical adoption. This mini-review summarizes current AI applications in oculoplastic surgery, identifies key knowledge gaps, and discusses future directions toward personalized, multimodal, AI-driven surgical care.

papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This repository provides the supporting research materials for the study entitled “Drone-AI Mobile Sensing Intelligence for Smart X: A Multimodal Human-in-the-Loop Architecture.” The study proposes a reusable Drone-AI Mobile Sensing Intelligence architecture that reframes unmanned aerial vehicles from conventional flying cameras into multimodal mobile sensing platforms.
