papers.title: Peer Review Report For: Building Digital Trust in East Africa: The Role of National ID and ICT Policy in Somalia’s Digital Transformation [version 1; peer review: 1 approved with reservations]
papers.venue: OpenAlex
papers.abstract: Trusted digital identities sit at the heart of any modern, inclusive financial system. This paper investigates Somalia’s transition from a fragmented digital landscape to a secure, integrated ecosystem through the lens of a “Three Pillars” framework: Robust Digital Identity, Comprehensive ICT Policy, and Proactive Cybersecurity Safeguards. Utilizing a qualitative multi-method approach, the study triangulates fifteen semi-structured interviews with regulators, financial experts, and civil society against a rigorous analysis of foundational policies, including the Data Protection Act (2023) and the Cybersecurity Law (2026). Results indicate that Somalia’s digital identity ecosystem—comprising e-Aqoonsi, HUBIYE, and the Certificate Delivery System (CDS)—serves as a technical anchor for financial inclusion, significantly bolstered by a July 2025 Central Bank mandate requiring National IDs for all banking transactions. These tools are supported by legal scaffolding under the Data Protection Authority and proactive security guardrails provided by the Somalia Computer Incident Response Team (SOMCIRT). However, comparative analysis reveals that while Somalia has achieved technical parity with East African Community (EAC) peers in biometric capabilities, it remains an outlier due to its reliance on foreign data hosting, which poses risks to national data sovereignty. To realize Somalia’s Centennial Vision 2060, the study concludes that the nation must bridge implementation gaps in rural digital literacy and technical capacity while transitioning toward local data infrastructure. The paper proposes a strategic roadmap for regional harmonization and enhanced institutional coordination to sustain public trust in the emerging digital economy.

papers.title: Agentic, Autonomous and Explainable AI in Smart Agriculture: A Systematic Literature Review
papers.venue: Agronomy
papers.abstract: Agentic, autonomous and explainable AI (XAI) is growing in smart agriculture, but its design, evaluation and integration have not been systematically mapped. Following PRISMA 2020, we searched Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus and IEEE Xplore through 14 June 2026 for English-language peer-reviewed articles and conference papers (2016–2026) implementing agentic/autonomous AI and/or XAI in agricultural systems using sensor, robotic or computer-vision data and reporting an evaluation. Two reviewers independently screened, extracted data and appraised methodological quality using a six-item CASP-style rubric. Results were synthesised descriptively using counts, percentages, cross-tabulations and thematic mapping; meta-analysis was inappropriate because tasks, datasets and metrics were heterogeneous. Of 2255 records, 322 studies were included. XAI dominated (69.6%), whereas autonomous (14.0%) and agentic (12.1%) designs were less common; only 4.3% combined autonomy with explainability. Disease detection was the leading application (33.5%). Most systems remained at the perception/decision-support level (78.9%); 17.4% were field-validated and 4.3% validated explanations agronomically. The evidence reveals an explainability-autonomy divide and substantial field-validation and reproducibility gaps. Explainable-by-design agentic systems require agronomic validation and shared evaluation standards. The review received no external grant funding and was not registered.

papers.title: Recovering Scene Geometry and Material from Event Streams with 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.venue: Sensors
topics: Generative Adversarial Networks and Image Synthesis
papers.abstract: Recovering scene geometry and material yields physically meaningful representations that support many tasks in computer vision and graphics. Methods built on neural representations such as neural radiance fields and 3D Gaussian Splatting perform well but assume clean, well-exposed multi-view images, and their accuracy degrades substantially under low light, fast motion, or strong illumination changes. We instead recover scene geometry and material using only event streams (the asynchronous output of a neuromorphic event camera, which records per-pixel logarithmic-brightness changes above a contrast threshold) as input, within a framework based on 3D Gaussian Splatting. Because events measure differential brightness and leave the global brightness scale undetermined, we introduce a brightness-anchoring prior that constrains this global brightness scale while reconstructing a radiance field; we then decompose the radiance into geometry and material (surface normals, depth, base color, and roughness), using motion-compensated event edges to guide boundary-aware regularization. On public datasets, the method achieves the best average performance among baselines that first reconstruct images and then apply inverse rendering. Averaged over the seven evaluated scenes, it attains 22.11 dB PSNR, 0.902 SSIM, and 0.105 LPIPS on novel-view rendering, and 22.31 dB PSNR on base-color estimation, with a mean surface-normal angular error of 28.93∘. The quantitative evaluation uses simulated event streams on seven synthetic scenes; we additionally include a qualitative demonstration on a physical event-camera capture, and identify full quantitative validation on real recordings as the primary direction for future work.

papers.title: "NITC Weed Datasets"
papers.venue: IEEE DataPort
papers.abstract: "A comprehensive field-image dataset for weed detection was developed at NIT Calicut, India, using images acquired from cultivated fields representing diverse crop growth stages and field conditions. The dataset comprises 8,152 images collected across multiple field sections, encompassing variations in illumination, crop density, weed species, and background complexity. Each image was manually annotated using bounding boxes to provide high-quality ground-truth labels for object detection. To improve model robustness and mitigate overfitting, data augmentation techniques, including random rotation, horizontal\/vertical flipping, and scaling, were applied. The dataset is designed to support the development and evaluation of robust, field-deployable computer vision models for automated weed detection under real-world agricultural variability."

papers.title: Real-Time Multiple Object Detection and Tracking Using YOLOv8: An Interactive Deep Learning Framework with ByteTrack and BoT-SORT
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This technical report presents the design, implementation, and evaluation of a real-time multiple object detection and tracking system using the Ultralytics YOLOv8 deep learning framework. The system combines YOLOv8-based object detection with ByteTrack and BoT-SORT tracking capabilities to support persistent multi-object tracking across video frames. A custom YOLOv8n model was trained using an annotated horse-racing dataset, with images processed at a resolution of 640 × 640 pixels. The implementation integrates Python, PyTorch, OpenCV, Roboflow, and Streamlit to provide an interactive application capable of processing images, prerecorded videos, and webcam streams. The original experimental study reported overall performance of 73.8% precision, 81.7% recall, and 76.8% mean Average Precision (mAP). A separate horse-detection experiment reported 87.83% precision, 91.86% recall, and 93.84% mAP. The system demonstrates the practical application of deep learning-based computer vision to real-time object detection and tracking, including scenarios involving multiple and partially occluded objects. This technical report develops and extends experimental work originally undertaken as part of the author's MSc Artificial Intelligence dissertation at Sheffield Hallam University. It provides a refined account of the system architecture, model development, tracking implementation, experimental findings, limitations, and opportunities for future research.

papers.title: 基于多尺度信息融合的视觉理解
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
topics: Advanced Image and Video Retrieval Techniques
papers.abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to visual understanding that leverages the fusion of information from multiple scales. Traditional computer vision methods often rely on processing visual data at a single scale, which can be insufficient for accurately interpreting complex scenes containing objects and patterns at various resolutions. Our proposed methodology utilizes multi-resolution image processing techniques to extract features at different scales – pixel-level, texture-level, and shape-level – and then employs a deep learning model to fuse these features and achieve semantic understanding. The core claim of this work is that the hierarchical nature of visual information is critical for robust visual understanding. We demonstrate that by integrating information from different scales, we can significantly improve the ability to recognize and interpret complex scenes. The key mechanism involves the extraction of features at multiple resolutions followed by a deep learning-based fusion and semantic interpretation stage. Experimental results (though not presented through formal experiments here) demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach.

papers.title: Metric Learning for Unsupervised Representation Discovery in High-Dimensional Data
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of unsupervised representation learning in high-dimensional data, a problem frequently encountered in domains such as computer vision, natural language processing, and bioinformatics. Traditional unsupervised learning techniques often fail to capture the underlying structure and relationships within these complex datasets, resulting in learned representations that are either overly complex or simply ineffective. We propose a novel metric learning algorithm designed to directly learn a distance metric from unlabeled data. This approach shifts the focus from learning a feature representation to learning the relationships between data points themselves. The core idea is that by learning a suitable metric, the algorithm can effectively cluster similar data points together and separate dissimilar ones, leading to the discovery of more informative and robust representations. We demonstrate the efficacy of this method through theoretical analysis and outline its potential applications. The algorithm is based on minimizing a divergence measure between the true pairwise relationships in the data and the learned distance metric. The theoretical framework provides insights into the algorithm's convergence properties and the impact of key hyperparameters.

papers.title: Curated Avocado Leaf Image Dataset for Healthy and Cercospora Leaf Spot Classification
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This curated dataset contains labeled images of avocado (Persea americana) leaves collected from avocado farms in Rungwe District Council, Mbeya Region, Tanzania. The images are organized into two classes: healthy leaves and leaves affected by Cercospora leaf spot. The dataset was developed to support research on automated classification of healthy avocado leaves and Cercospora leaf spot-affected leaves using machine learning, deep learning, and computer vision techniques. Images were captured under natural field conditions to reflect variations in lighting, background, leaf orientation, and disease appearance that may occur in real agricultural environments.

papers.title: Style Transfer with Adaptive Neural Networks
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
topics: Generative Adversarial Networks and Image Synthesis
papers.abstract: Style transfer is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves transferring the visual style of one image to another. While traditional methods often rely on manual style transfer, this paper proposes a novel approach utilizing adaptive neural networks to automatically learn and transfer distinct styles. We introduce a new architecture, the "Style-Adaptive Convolutional Network" (SACN), which employs a dynamic network architecture and a novel style embedding mechanism to achieve high-quality and diverse style transfer. We evaluate the performance of the SACN on a diverse set of image datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness in capturing intricate style variations and achieving state-of-the-art results in image generation quality and stylistic diversity.

papers.title: Adversarial Generative Networks for Object Detection and Segmentation
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
topics: Generative Adversarial Networks and Image Synthesis
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the application of Adversarial Generative Networks (AGNs) to enhance the performance of object detection and segmentation tasks. Traditional object detection and segmentation models often struggle with robustness against noisy data and variations in object appearances. We propose a novel framework that leverages the adversarial training paradigm within AGNs to improve model generalization and accuracy. The core claim of this work is that incorporating AGNs can significantly boost the precision and robustness of object detection and segmentation systems. The proposed mechanism involves combining an AGN with a standard detection or segmentation model, utilizing the adversarial loss to refine the model's ability to discern objects amidst challenging conditions. Experimental results, though not detailed through a dedicated experimental section, demonstrate the potential of this approach. The key innovation lies in proactively generating adversarial examples during training, forcing the model to learn more robust features and representations. This addresses a critical limitation of conventional training methods, which often rely on carefully curated datasets with minimal noise. This work lays the groundwork for future research exploring the full potential of AGNs in computer vision applications requiring high reliability and adaptability. ---

papers.title: Graph Representation Learning with Learned Topological Data Analysis
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Graph representation learning (GRL) has achieved significant success in various domains, including social network analysis, drug discovery, and computer vision. However, traditional GRL methods often rely on simple graph metrics such as node degrees and shortest path lengths, which can fail to capture the intricate, high-order structural patterns inherent in many real-world graphs. This paper proposes a novel framework that integrates topological data analysis (TDA) techniques, specifically persistent homology, directly into the GRL process. Our approach learns representations that are inherently invariant to graph deformations, offering a more robust and informative representation of the graph's underlying topology. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through theoretical analysis and by illustrating its ability to capture complex structural patterns that are missed by conventional GRL approaches. The core claim is that existing GRL methods lack the ability to capture complex topological features of graphs. The core mechanism is to integrate TDA techniques, such as persistent homology, directly into the graph representation learning process to learn representations that are invariant to graph deformations.

papers.title: Neuromorphic Computing for Real-Time Object Tracking with Sparse Coding
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the application of neuromorphic computing for real-time object tracking, addressing the limitations of traditional computer vision approaches. The core idea is to utilize the inherent parallelism and energy efficiency of spiking neural networks (SNNs) combined with sparse coding techniques. Sparse coding, which represents data using a minimal number of active features, is particularly well-suited for the event-driven nature of SNNs. The proposed system aims to create a low-power, real-time object tracking solution by learning sparse representations of visual scenes within an SNN. The system is designed to process visual data with reduced computational demands, leading to improved responsiveness and reduced energy consumption compared to conventional algorithms. We demonstrate the feasibility and potential advantages of this approach, paving the way for more efficient and robust visual tracking systems in resource-constrained environments. The key innovations lie in the synergistic combination of sparse coding and SNNs, offering a fundamentally different paradigm for visual processing.

papers.title: Quantum-Inspired Data Augmentation for Computer Vision
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
topics: Generative Adversarial Networks and Image Synthesis
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a novel data augmentation technique inspired by quantum mechanics, specifically leveraging the principles of superposition and quantum random access memory (QRAM) simulation. Traditional data augmentation methods often rely on simple transformations like rotations, flips, and color jittering, which may not fully capture the inherent variability within a dataset. Our approach aims to generate more diverse and realistic augmented data by simulating a QRAM, effectively creating multiple correlated versions of training images simultaneously. The core idea is to represent each training image as a superposition of multiple states, allowing us to explore a vastly larger solution space than conventional methods. We quantify the augmentation process using metrics related to image entropy and feature space coverage. Preliminary simulations indicate that this quantum-inspired augmentation can significantly improve the robustness and generalization performance of computer vision models compared to standard augmentation techniques. Further research is planned to explore the practical implementation of this concept and its scalability.

papers.title: Real-Time Multiple Object Detection and Tracking Using YOLOv8: An Interactive Deep Learning Framework with ByteTrack and BoT-SORT
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This technical report presents the design, implementation, and evaluation of a real-time multiple object detection and tracking system using the Ultralytics YOLOv8 deep learning framework. The system combines YOLOv8-based object detection with ByteTrack and BoT-SORT tracking capabilities to support persistent multi-object tracking across video frames. A custom YOLOv8n model was trained using an annotated horse-racing dataset, with images processed at a resolution of 640 × 640 pixels. The implementation integrates Python, PyTorch, OpenCV, Roboflow, and Streamlit to provide an interactive application capable of processing images, prerecorded videos, and webcam streams. The original experimental study reported overall performance of 73.8% precision, 81.7% recall, and 76.8% mean Average Precision (mAP). A separate horse-detection experiment reported 87.83% precision, 91.86% recall, and 93.84% mAP. The system demonstrates the practical application of deep learning-based computer vision to real-time object detection and tracking, including scenarios involving multiple and partially occluded objects. This technical report develops and extends experimental work originally undertaken as part of the author's MSc Artificial Intelligence dissertation at Sheffield Hallam University. It provides a refined account of the system architecture, model development, tracking implementation, experimental findings, limitations, and opportunities for future research.

papers.title: Kernels That Learned to See: A State of the Art Review of Convolutional Networks and the Mechanics of Vision
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI
papers.abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Convolutional Networks and the Mechanics of Vision in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of computer vision and CNN as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

papers.title: L'Intelligenza Artificiale e il Riconoscimento Visivo nell'Ingegneria Forense: Modelli Computazionali, Analisi dei Cedimenti e Validazione Legale
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: L'ingegneria forense si fonda sull'indagine rigorosa di materiali, prodotti, strutture o componenti che falliscono nel loro intento operativo, causando conseguenze disastrose quali lesioni personali o perdite economiche significative. Storicamente ancorata a metodi di ispezione visiva manuale e test distruttivi, questa disciplina sta subendo una metamorfosi epocale guidata dall'adozione di architetture di Intelligenza Artificiale (AI) e tecnologie di Visione Computazionale (Computer Vision). Questo articolo scientifico, strutturato in conformità con i domini di ricerca dell'International Journal of Forensic Engineering (IJFE), presenta un'analisi esaustiva e dettagliatissima dell'integrazione di reti neurali profonde, elaborazione fotogrammetrica e algoritmi di amplificazione del movimento nelle pratiche di indagine post-disastro. Vengono esaminati in profondità i meccanismi fisici e computazionali alla base della Digital Image Correlation (DIC), dell'Eulerian Video Magnification (EVM) e della Direct Linear Transformation (DLT), evidenziandone le applicazioni nell'analisi del degrado dei materiali, nella ricostruzione cinematica degli incidenti e nel monitoraggio della salute strutturale (SHM). Lo studio affronta inoltre la modellazione spaziale tramite 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), le architetture Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) per la mitigazione del disequilibrio dei dati nei danni catastrofici e l'implementazione dell'Explainable AI (XAI) per garantire l'ammissibilità legale delle prove visive secondo gli standard dello Scientific Working Group on Digital Evidence (SWGDE). L'obiettivo è fornire un quadro di riferimento accademico che orienti la futura prassi forense verso una diagnostica predittiva e retrospettiva oggettiva, tracciabile e scientificamente inoppugnabile.

papers.title: The Intelligent Airport: Artificial Intelligence as an Integrated Safety Management Layer Across Airport Operations and Risk Domains.
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence is emerging as a potential new layer of airport Safety Management Systems by integrating operational, environmental, infrastructure, personnel, and surveillance data into a continuously updated assessment of airport risk. Rather than treating runway incursions, foreign object debris, wildlife hazards, pavement degradation, weather, staffing, fatigue, emergency response, construction, maintenance, and ground movement as isolated safety domains, the intelligent airport concept combines them to identify hazardous interactions that may remain invisible within traditional departmental structures. Current advances in machine learning, computer vision, surface surveillance, predictive maintenance, digital twins, and human-AI decision support demonstrate that many of the technological components already exist, while manufacturers, the Federal Aviation Administration, military organizations, and research institutions are progressively developing related capabilities. However, the transition from fragmented AI applications to an integrated airport-wide safety intelligence layer introduces substantial challenges involving explainability, certification, cybersecurity, privacy, employee monitoring, legal liability, public-sector governance, and human authority. This article argues that the most effective future model is not an airport controlled by artificial intelligence, but an airport whose Safety Management System is augmented by AI capable of continuously recognizing combinations of weak safety signals before they converge into an accident sequence. Such an architecture could transform airport safety from primarily reactive and periodically predictive risk management into persistent, system-wide anticipatory awareness.

papers.title: Reinterpretation of Non-Natural Language Ciphers in the Voynich Manuscript (MS 408): A Study on Three-Dimensional Circuit Architectures and Molecular Fluidic Quantum Computing Systems Mimicking Medieval Plant Morphology.
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: For over a century, decoding attempts of the Voynich Manuscript have beenbottlenecked by traditional philological and linguistic paradigms. However, thestatistical anomalies of the text—such as excessive word repetition andextremely low character entropy—strongly reject the characteristics of naturalhuman languages. Moving away from standard cryptographic translation, thispaper proposes a radical new framework: that MS 408 is a highly obfuscatedintegration blueprint and source code for a Molecular Fluidic QuantumComputing System engineered within the technological matrix of bio-quantuminformation science, using 15th-century materials as a "cognitive security" layer.By evaluating the visual diagrams through the lens of modern microfluidics andquantum information theory, we map the text to a deterministic instruction setwith a structural entropy of approximately 3.0 to 3.5 bits, mimicking moderncompiled programming languages. We demonstrate that the manuscriptstructurally satisfies the four pillars of computer architecture: Input viamicrofluidic root networks; Processing via quantum entanglement logic gatesutilizing liquid superconducting media; Clock Control modeled after plant crosssectionalvascular grids; and Storage via localized quantum registers disguisedas pharmaceutical jars.Furthermore, we identify three unresolved engineering frontiers outlined in thetext that surpass current 2026 solid-state quantum constraints: roomtemperaturequantum coherence via specific botanical fluid compositions,nonlinear chaotic flow regulation in nanoscale channels, and self-assemblingdynamic topological circuitry. This study redefines the Voynich Manuscript notas an unreadable medieval hoax, but as a robust, open-source time capsuleaddressed directly to the post-AI computing era.

papers.title: MindWeaver Framework
papers.venue: OpenAlex
papers.abstract: The global burden of mental health disorders is intensifying, demanding innovative approaches beyond traditional diagnostic and beneficial prototypes. This chapter explores the transformative potential of assimilating Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Internet of Things (IoT) in mental health analysis, positing them as a synergistic framework for preemptive, personalized, and scalable care. IoT devices, ranging from wearables and smart sensors to ambient environmental monitors, facilitate continuous, passive, and objective data collection, generating a rich drapery of physiological, interactive, and appropriate information. AI-driven analytics, encircling machine learning, deep learning, and natural language processing, then interpret these vast datasets to identify refined patterns, predict exacerbations, and personalize involvement strategies long before conventional methods might. While promising unmatched opportunities for early detection, proactive care, and scalable support within diverse populations, this convergence also presents significant ethical challenges related to privacy, data security, algorithmic bias, and the potential for over-reliance on technology. This abstract outlines a comprehensive examination of the synergistic capabilities of AI and IoT, delineates the critical considerations for their responsible disposition, and envisions a future where these technologies enlarge human expertise to foster more accessible, accurate, and vicarious mental healthcare. Also, this chapter discusses the MindWeaver results and its impact.

papers.title: Language as labels for cross dataset generalization in sign language translation
papers.venue: Scientific Reports
papers.abstract: Sign language translation is a challenging task by large vision-language models due to the complicated temporal-spatial cues, cross-modal semantic alignment and expensive gloss. To alleviate this issue, we propose a novel large language model-based multi-modal boosted method, which achieves language-as-labels and a customized three-stage vision-language fusion pipeline for sign language translation. Specifically, we produce a sign language action description dataset to realize the transformation of sign language label from gloss sequences to action description sequences. Moreover, this study leverages our dataset as labels and visual-caption early fusion approach to encourage the large language model to accurately capture sign language action temporal-spatial cues. Note that this study introduces the large-scale natural language processing datasets for generating sign language action labels for the first time to achieve cross-dataset sign language reasoning. Empirically, extensive experiments validate the efficacy of our approach, achieving state-of-the-art performance on widely used benchmarks while demonstrating strong cross-dataset generalization.

papers.title: Explainable AI for Automated Theorem Proving using Natural Language Generation
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Automated theorem provers (ATPs) have achieved remarkable success in verifying mathematical theorems, yet their internal workings remain largely opaque to human users. This research addresses this challenge by employing Natural Language Generation (NLG) techniques to provide human-understandable explanations of the reasoning steps taken by an ATP. The core idea is to create a model that translates the ATP's symbolic reasoning – represented as a sequence of logical formulas and inference rules – into natural language descriptions. This facilitates a more transparent and interpretable process, ultimately making ATPs more accessible and useful for mathematicians and logicians who require a deeper understanding of their proof strategies. The approach utilizes a model trained on a dataset of ATP proof steps and their corresponding natural language explanations, demonstrating a significant step towards explainable AI in the domain of automated theorem proving. The model's architecture and training procedure are described, along with preliminary results and future research directions.

papers.title: Cognitive Graph Construction and Reasoning Engine
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper presents a novel cognitive graph construction system and a reasoning engine designed to leverage multi-modal information for enhanced knowledge discovery and reasoning. The system utilizes a graph structure to represent knowledge and employs a reasoning engine to interpret and apply this knowledge through natural language processing. The core mechanism centers around the integration of graph information with reasoning algorithms, enabling more intelligent knowledge discovery and inference. We focus on developing a system that surpasses existing approaches by integrating both graph representation and reasoning capabilities. The paper details the system's architecture, proposes a novel reasoning process, and explores its potential applications.

papers.title: Title: Dynamic Probabilistic Graphs via High-Dimensional Neural Networks: Semantic Reasoning and Knowledge Graph Construction in Natural Language Processing
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic probabilistic graph model, leveraging high-dimensional neural networks, for natural language processing. We propose a mechanism that dynamically adjusts the network parameters to enhance both semantic reasoning and knowledge graph construction capabilities. The core challenge lies in developing a model capable of learning complex language representations and effectively constructing knowledge graphs, which are crucial for many NLP tasks. The study investigates the effectiveness of this approach through extensive experimentation on various semantic reasoning and knowledge graph tasks. The results demonstrate a significant improvement in these tasks, highlighting the potential of this dynamic probabilistic graph model as a foundation for advanced NLP applications.

papers.title: 基于自适应的自然语言处理的语法分析框架
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for grammatical analysis based on adaptive natural language processing (NLP) techniques. Traditional grammatical analysis relies heavily on manually crafted rules, limiting its flexibility and adaptability to the nuances of language. Our proposed system leverages self-adaptive algorithms to dynamically adjust grammatical rules based on sentence structure, offering a more robust and accurate analysis. We demonstrate the framework's effectiveness through a series of benchmark tests, showcasing significant improvements in precision and coverage compared to existing methods. The core mechanism focuses on a hierarchical rule adaptation process, allowing the system to effectively handle complex sentence structures and variations. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions, including exploring the integration of contextual information and more sophisticated adaptive learning algorithms.

papers.abstract: บทความแก้ไขข้อผิดพลาดนี้ เกี่ยวข้องกับบทความต้นฉบับเรื่อง:สรณีย์ ศุภรพิพัฒน์ และพงศ์ศักดิ์ ด่านเดชา. การพัฒนาระบบการให้รหัสโรคและหัตถการอัตโนมัติสำหรับผู้ป่วยนอกโรงพยาบาลสงขลานครินทร์: การศึกษาย้อนหลัง. เวชสารสงขลานครินทร์ (PSU Medical Journal) 2569;6(1):15-24. https://doi.org/10.31584/psumj.2026281538 URL: https://he01.tci-thaijo.org/index.php/PSUMJ/article/view/281538 ข้อผิดพลาดที่พบ พบข้อความภาษาอังกฤษส่วนเกินที่ไม่เกี่ยวข้องหลงเหลืออยู่ในเนื้อหาหลักหน้าที่ 17 ในส่วนของข้อความในบทความที่ว่าด้วย “การพัฒนาระบบอัตโนมัติเพื่อช่วยในการให้รหัสโรคและรหัสหัตถการเป็นแนวทางสำคัญในการแก้ไขปัญหาที่เกิดขึ้น ในช่วงทศวรรษที่ผ่านมา วงการวิชาการได้นำเสนอวิธีการหลากหลายในการพัฒนาระบบการให้รหัสอัตโนมัติ ครอบคลุมตั้งแต่ เทคนิคการเรียนรู้ของเครื่อง (machine learning) ไปจนถึงการเรียนรู้เซิงลึก (deep learning)5 insurance claim processing and research. papers.title: Based on Multi-Scale Information Bottleneck: A Deep Learning Framework
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
topics: Generative Adversarial Networks and Image Synthesis
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a novel deep learning framework centered around the concept of multi-scale information bottleneck (MSIB). Recognizing that complex data often contains rich information at various scales, we introduce a mechanism for explicitly modeling these scales and facilitating effective information fusion. The core of the framework is a multi-scale representation learning module that decomposes input data into representations across different scales. These representations are then connected through multiple bottleneck layers, driving the extraction of salient features and promoting a deeper understanding of the data. Unlike existing frameworks that primarily focus on single-scale bottlenecks, our approach leverages the complementary information present at multiple scales, leading to improved performance in tasks requiring robust and nuanced data interpretation. The proposed methodology offers a promising direction for addressing challenges in areas such as image recognition, natural language processing, and time series analysis where hierarchical and multi-scale characteristics are prevalent. We demonstrate the framework's potential through theoretical analysis and outline its key components, emphasizing the importance of scale selection and bottleneck architecture design for optimal performance. ---

papers.title: Title: Dynamic Probabilistic Graphs via High-Dimensional Neural Networks: Semantic Reasoning and Knowledge Graph Construction in Natural Language Processing
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic probabilistic graph model, leveraging high-dimensional neural networks, for natural language processing. We propose a mechanism that dynamically adjusts the network parameters to enhance both semantic reasoning and knowledge graph construction capabilities. The core challenge lies in developing a model capable of learning complex language representations and effectively constructing knowledge graphs, which are crucial for many NLP tasks. The study investigates the effectiveness of this approach through extensive experimentation on various semantic reasoning and knowledge graph tasks. The results demonstrate a significant improvement in these tasks, highlighting the potential of this dynamic probabilistic graph model as a foundation for advanced NLP applications.

papers.title: Eighty experiments on the Voynich manuscript: code, results and bilingual site
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Eighty statistical experiments on the text of the Voynich manuscript (Beinecke MS 408), each run on natural-language and enciphered controls before the manuscript. Includes the experiment scripts, the numerical results as JSON, the figures, and the bilingual (English, Portuguese) explanatory site. Main result: the text is statistically indistinguishable from a three-rule process (two-glyph habit, 4% local copying, page-by-page bias), with no lexicon above the habit and no page-specific vocabulary; the labels next to the drawings are the one exception; a Naibbe-class verbose homophonic cipher (Greshko 2025) remains an open hypothesis because the solvers built here could not break Greshko's own control.

papers.title: The title: Topological Topology and the Association of Natural Language Information
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the intriguing intersection of topology and natural language information, proposing a novel approach to enhance the accuracy of natural language understanding. The inherent structure of topological spaces provides a powerful framework for representing and analyzing language's complexities. We explore the potential of leveraging topological structures as a latent feature within natural language data, aiming to create a robust and adaptable model for semantic interpretation. The core of this work lies in the development of a model that dynamically infers the underlying topological properties of language, enabling a deeper and more nuanced understanding of meaning. This research contributes to a paradigm shift in natural language processing, moving beyond traditional statistical methods towards a more holistic and geometrically-informed approach to language representation. Specifically, we construct a model that maps linguistic expressions to topological spaces, enabling the identification of underlying relationships and patterns within the language's structure. The resulting model exhibits improved performance in tasks requiring semantic reasoning and contextual interpretation, demonstrating the significant potential of integrating topological analysis into the field of natural language understanding. This work represents a crucial step towards creating more intelligent and contextually aware language processing systems.

papers.title: Graph-Based Representation Learning for Large Language Models
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in natural language processing, but they often struggle with tasks requiring deep understanding of relationships between entities within textual data. This research proposes a novel approach to enhance LLM performance by incorporating graph-based representation learning. The core idea is to construct a graph representation of the input text, where nodes represent words or phrases and edges represent semantic relationships derived from co-occurrence, dependency parsing, or other relevant measures. This graph is then integrated into the LLM architecture, allowing the model to leverage graph-based reasoning for improved understanding and performance. We hypothesize that this integration will address the limitations of current LLMs in representing and reasoning about complex relationships, leading to advancements in tasks such as question answering, knowledge graph completion, and commonsense reasoning. The methodology focuses on efficient graph construction and seamless integration, aiming for minimal disruption to the existing LLM structure while maximizing the benefits of relational reasoning. The evaluation framework will primarily rely on benchmark datasets designed to test relational understanding capabilities, assessing improvements in accuracy, efficiency, and robustness compared to traditional LLM approaches.

papers.title: Dual Optimisation in Low-Resource Natural Language Processing: Integrating Meta-Learning and Efficient Deep Architectures for Sustainable AI Development
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This study addresses a critical gap in low-resource Natural Language Processing (NLP): the lack of aunified framework that jointly optimises computational efficiency and task performance under severe dataand hardware constraints. To bridge this gap, the study introduces the Dual Optimisation Framework—thefirst empirically validated approach integrating meta-learning (MAML) with resource-adaptivearchitectures (DistilBERT and MobileBERT). A mixed-methods design was used: quantitative experimentsmeasured accuracy, F1-scores, latency, and memory consumption across multiple configurations, whilequalitative expert interviews contextualised deployment feasibility in low-resource settings. Results showthat DistilBERT combined with MAML improves efficiency–performance trade-offs by up to 35%,outperforming larger models while maintaining competitive accuracy. Latency and memory profilingconfirm the framework’s suitability for computational realities in the Global South. The study contributes ascalable, sustainable model for equitable NLP development and demonstrates how learning efficiency andcomputational efficiency can be co-optimised in constrained environments.

papers.title: BioSignal-FM: Multimodal Biosignal Research Platform
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: BioSignal-FM is a modular research platform for reproducible multimodal biosignal processing, representation-learning experiments, modality-specific adapters, evaluation, provenance, and artifact management. EMG, EEG, and ECG are core research tracks; ECoG/iEEG is experimental and fNIRS is an optional extension. The software does not claim a validated universal foundation model, clinical readiness, or cross-modal generalization without separately reported evidence.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence and radiogenomics in the peritumoral microenvironment of gliomas: a systematic review of diagnostic performance and clinical implications
papers.venue: Computer Methods in Biomechanics and Biomedical Engineering Imaging & Visualization
topics: Radiomics and Machine Learning in Medical Imaging
papers.abstract: Introduction Delineating infiltrative peritumoral edema (PTE) in gliomas remains challenging due to acquisition variability and the lack of histopathological validation. We systematically assessed artificial intelligence (AI) and radiomics models for peritumoral characterization.Methods Following PRISMA, we searched five databases on July 18, 2025, for peritumoral AI/radiomics studies predicting tumor infiltration, recurrence, or molecular status. Quality was evaluated using Prediction model Risk Of Bias Assessment Tool (PROBAST).Results Nineteen studies (6,851 patients) were included. Deep learning (DL) (nnU-Net, CNNs) identified PTE infiltration with high performance, achieving >80% sensitivity for recurrence (OR = 9.97), and outperforming radiomics (AUC = 0.61–0.98). Multimodal MRI (DTI/DSC+FLAIR) showed higher accuracy (0.90–0.98) than standard sequences. Synthetic MRI enabled standardized IDH/1p/19q prediction (AUC = 0.95/0.86). Voxel-wise histopathological validation was extremely rare (1 study).Discussion AI-based peritumoral phenotyping shows strong non-invasive potential. However, prospective clinical trials are essential to validate these predictive maps before their clinical use in surgical or radiotherapy planning.

papers.title: A novel approach to dyslexia detection: combining EEG data and cognitive tasks with advanced machine learning
papers.venue: Computer Methods in Biomechanics & Biomedical Engineering
papers.abstract: Existing dyslexia detection methods typically rely on either EEG or screening tests. This study introduces a multimodal two-stage methodology for dyslexia detection that integrates both EEG signals and screening test data, using spectral features (Shannon entropy and Power Spectral Density) across various frequency bands. The novelty of the proposed approach stems in collecting firsthand paired EEG recordings and screening data from patients, and combining them via two-stage framework, which improves predictive accuracy and yields a comprehensive neurological assessment. Several machine learning models were trained and, upon evaluation, the Random Forest classifier performed best, achieving 98.36% accuracy, 99.2% precision, and 97.63% recall using only EEG data. When both EEG and screening data were combined, performance improved to 98.69% accuracy, 98.90% precision, and 98.90% recall, significantly outperforming existing methodologies, with results validated via statistical tests. Dyslexic individuals exhibited higher delta and theta energy, particularly in the central, parietal, and temporal regions, indicating deficits in phonological processing and working memory. Lower Shannon entropy values in dyslexics suggest increased randomness in neural activity and reduced processing ability. Feature importance analysis identified delta, theta, and gamma energies as the most discriminative features. This study highlights the effectiveness of multimodal data fusion in enhancing dyslexia detection, improving early diagnosis, and facilitating interventions for children aged 5–9 years. These results underscore the potential of advanced spectral feature extraction and robust machine learning in dyslexia diagnostics, setting a benchmark in the field, with future work focusing on validating these results using larger datasets and exploring additional predictive features.

papers.title: Robust UAV Detection and Classification in Noisy RF Environments via Multimodal CNN-Based IQ and Spectrogram Fusion
papers.venue: OpenAlex
papers.abstract: This study aims to autonomously detect and classify Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), which are becoming increasingly widespread, based on their emitted radio frequency (RF) signals in highly noisy and interference-prone RF environments where traditional optical and radar-based methods prove insufficient. The dataset used in this study is the “Noisy Drone RF Signal Classification” dataset, which consists of seven classes in total—six different drone models and one noise class—and is balanced across classes. As the methodological approach, a multimodal hybrid deep learning (DL) architecture was developed, integrating raw time-domain IQ signals (1D-CNN) with frequency-domain spectrogram representations (2D-CNN). To enhance model performance and generalization capability, techniques such as Batch Normalization, Dropout, Label Smoothing, and Gradient Clipping were incorporated into the architecture. The model was trained using the AdamW optimization algorithm alongside a cosine annealing learning rate scheduler. In order to efficiently process large-scale datasets, memory management optimizations including memory-mapped files (mmap) and lazy loading were implemented. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed multimodal model achieves an accuracy of 87.42% and an F1-score of 0.87, indicating strong detection performance. SNR-based analyses reveal that the model achieves accuracy levels ranging between 64.52% and 82.40% under negative-SNR conditions (−20 to 0 dB), while exceeding 89% accuracy under positive-SNR conditions. The findings indicate that multimodal DL approaches can achieve high performance in UAV detection and classification even in noisy RF environments.

papers.title: Multimodal diagnosis of flatfoot using transformer and graph-based deep learning Models
papers.venue: BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making
papers.abstract: Flatfoot is a common musculoskeletal disorder that, if not detected in its early stages, can lead to impaired posture, reduced mobility, and diminished quality of life. Conventional diagnosis relies heavily on manual interpretation of radiographic and clinical findings, which can be time-consuming, subjective, and dependent on expert experience. This study aimed to develop a multimodal deep learning framework that integrates complementary anatomical and functional information for automatic flatfoot classification. The proposed framework jointly processed three data modalities: (i) RGB plantar foot images, (ii) plantar-pressure time-series signals collected during gait, and (iii) biomechanical angular measurements. Three modality-specific branches were employed: a Swin Transformer to extract spatial representations of plantar morphology, a bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) network to model temporal plantar-pressure dynamics, and a Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) to represent structural relationships among biomechanical measurements. The modality-specific representations were projected into a common latent space and integrated using a multi-head attention-based fusion mechanism. The framework was evaluated using participant-level stratified 10-fold cross-validation on a clinically acquired multimodal dataset comprising 978 foot-level samples from 489 independent participants. Complementary publicly available pressure-related data were used exclusively during model development and were not included as independent multimodal cases in the final evaluation. The proposed multimodal framework achieved an accuracy of 94.0%, an F1-score of 0.94, and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.96. The integration of visual, temporal, and biomechanical representations demonstrated the effectiveness of combining complementary information within a unified multimodal framework for flatfoot classification. The findings demonstrate the potential of transformer- and graph-based multimodal deep learning for computer-aided flatfoot diagnosis. By integrating plantar morphology, temporal pressure dynamics, and structured biomechanical information, the proposed framework achieved high classification performance. Further external validation using independent multi-center datasets is needed to assess its generalizability, and future studies may extend the framework to multi-class foot deformity assessment.

papers.title: AI-Enabled Early Detection and Lifestyle Interventions Management for Preventing Neurodegenerative Disorders
papers.venue: OpenAlex
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education
papers.abstract: Neurodegenerative disorders such as Alzheimer’s disease and Parkinson’s disease present escalating clinical and economic challenges for healthcare systems worldwide. Recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) have significantly enhanced early detection capabilities through multimodal machine learning models integrating neuroimaging, motion analytics, cognitive assessment data, wearable monitoring, and biomarker prediction systems. Drawing exclusively on recent Scopus-indexed research, this chapter examines how AI-enabled early detection can be strategically integrated into preventive healthcare frameworks, with particular emphasis on commerce and management implications. While existing studies demonstrate high diagnostic accuracy and predictive performance, gaps remain in long-term validation, economic evaluation, governance structures, and scalable implementation. This chapter synthesizes methodological approaches used in AI-based neurodiagnostics and extends the discussion toward managerial integration, cost-effectiveness, digital infrastructure requirements, and preventive lifestyle intervention models. It argues that AI should not be viewed solely as a technological innovation but as a strategic management instrument capable of reshaping healthcare planning, resource allocation, and value-based care delivery. By aligning clinical evidence with organizational and economic considerations, the chapter provides a structured framework for embedding AI-enabled early detection systems within sustainable healthcare management models. The findings suggest that when predictive technologies are supported by robust governance, interdisciplinary coordination, and preventive lifestyle strategies, they can shift neurodegenerative care from reactive treatment toward proactive, economically responsible prevention.

papers.title: From Design to Real-World Impact: Enhancing Human–Robot Interaction through Personality-Driven Robots
papers.venue: CINECA IRIS Institutial Research Information System (University of Genoa)
papers.abstract: Objective: Personality is a cognitive construct that shapes individuals’ characteristic patterns of thought, emotion, and behavior, influencing how they interact with others. Consequently, implementing personality in robots can significantly affect Human–Robot Interaction (HRI), shaping key dimensions such as trust, engagement, attention, empathy, and enjoyability. Although psychology lacks a univocal definition of human personality, several theoretical models, such as the Big Five, PEN, HEXACO, Cattell’s, and Myers–Briggs, aim to describe personality along trait dimensions. Psychological and physiological evidence further indicates that personality traits are deeply intertwined with memory processes, internal simulation, action selection, emotion generation, emotional intelligence, and action execution. However, in the robotics literature, personality implementation is often reduced to isolated behavioral aspects, typically focusing on a single trait. In contrast, approaches in affective computing attempt to capture the complexity of human personality but often remain impractical for real-world HRI applications. To address this gap, this thesis investigates the following research question: How should the personality of an artificial agent be designed to benefit Human-Robot Interaction? Accordingly, the main objective of this research is to design and implement a cognitive architecture capable of managing the interplay between personality and cognitive and affective processes, and to study how this interplay can be exploited to enhance HRI in real interaction scenarios. Approach: This research proposes a taxonomy of robotic personality based on the traits of Conscientiousness, Extraversion, and Agreeableness. A multidisciplinary approach, integrating insights from psychology, cognitive science, and robotics, was adopted to model and implement the influence of these traits on a set of cognitive and affective capabilities. Each component of the architecture was progressively evaluated through real HRI experiments. Once the overall architecture was validated, its integration was exploited in natural and challenging interaction scenarios to assess how personality-driven cognition can enhance HRI. Main results: The proposed cognitive architecture demonstrates adaptability across different robotic platforms, ranging from humanoid robots to industrial platforms, and across diverse tasks. Each architectural component proved fundamental in supporting an increasingly human-like concept of robotic personality, and consequently to enhance the intuitiveness of the interaction. Experimental results showed that personality plays a crucial role in enhancing empathy, trust, enjoyability, and sociability, key dimensions for fostering companionship with social robots. Moreover, the architecture demonstrated effectiveness in specific application domains, such as education, where it improved task performance in middle-school settings. The obtained results have been the starting point to investigate how to design robotic personality in preschool environments to support multicultural integration and collaboration. Significance: This work highlights the potential impact of robotic personality in complex and socially demanding environments. Educational applications illustrate how personality-driven robots can support learning and social inclusion. Beyond education, empathic robotic behavior holds promise in healthcare and elderly care, where long-term interaction and emotional sensitivity are essential. Finally, the integration of robotic personality and cognitive capabilities can contribute to smoother and more effective HRI in Industry 5.0 scenarios, where humans and collaborative robots are expected to share the same workspace.

papers.title: Design and Performance Verification of a Wheel-Track Transformable Mobile Platform Based on a Four-Bar Mechanism for Rescue Scenarios
papers.venue: SAE technical papers on CD-ROM/SAE technical paper series
papers.abstract: Contemporary disaster rescue operations face challenges due to complex and hazardous terrains. Existing rescue robots with single locomotion mechanisms (wheeled, legged, tracked) and some hybrid ones have limitations in adaptability, efficiency, or structure. To meet the dual demands of complex terrains and limited space, this paper proposes a wheel-track transformable mobile platform based on a four- bar mechanism, which adopts a modular structure. A servo motor drives the active link to adjust the spatial position of the movable link (equipped with movable wheels), enabling smooth switching between wheeled and tracked modes. Key link lengths are determined via kinematic analysis, and a two-stage gear transmission system is designed. Adams simulation verification shows the platform completes wheel-track mode conversion on flat ground without component interference and can lift the center of gravity (CG) to surmount obstacles during slope climbing. The platform's feasibility is verified, providing a technical reference for designing highly adaptable rescue robots suitable for small spaces and complex terrains in post-earthquake or post-disaster scenarios.

papers.title: New Nonlinear Buckling Solutions of Piezoelectric Truncated Conical Shells
papers.venue: SAE technical papers on CD-ROM/SAE technical paper series
papers.abstract: Piezoelectric materials are highly valued in engineering for their electromechanical coupling. With these characteristics, structural applications utilizing such materials are increasingly being employed across a variety of disciplines. Among these structural configurations, piezoelectric conical shells have garnered significant interest owing to their inherent electromechanical coupling behavior, making them ideal for applications in various devices such as actuation systems, sensing mechanisms and energy harvesting solutions. To ensure the structural safety of these devices, assessing the stability of such shell structures is essential. This study conducts an analysis of the buckling stability of truncated piezoelectric conical shells. To this end, a theoretical buckling model for piezoelectric truncated conical shells is established, based on first-order shear deformation theory combined with nonlinear pre-buckling deformations. Utilizing a novel set of displacement trial functions within the Galerkin framework, this study derives precise critical buckling loads along with their associated mode shapes. The accuracy of the model is verified through comparative studies in the numerical section. Subsequently, the influence of key parameters—including applied voltages, semi-apex angles, and shell thickness—on the buckling behavior is investigated. The findings indicate that including the nonlinear pre-buckling deformation in the analysis is essential for ensuring reliable predictions. This research offers a theoretical foundation for the dependable design and assessment of piezoelectric truncated conical shells. Moreover, they also create opportunities for smart structures in aerospace, civil, and robotics, where accurate predictions of stability under electromechanical loading are critical.

papers.title: Site-specific mechanical weeding robot with automatic self-adjustable individually controlled cultivator
papers.venue: Precision Agriculture
papers.abstract: Abstract Context Weeds significantly reduce crop productivity and profitability, particularly in sugar beet production where losses exceed $1.25 billion annually in the United States. Limitations of herbicide-based control and drawbacks of conventional tillage highlight the need for efficient, sustainable alternatives. Aims To develop and evaluate an autonomous site-specific mechanical weeding (SSMW) system with adaptive control for precise inter-row weed removal under field conditions. Methods An SSMW system was designed by integrating an inter-row tillage mechanism with a robotic platform using RTK-GPS for navigation and site-specific actuation. Site-specific weeding was performed in the field test and a strain-based feedback control system was implemented in computer simulation to enable ASIC tillage under uneven terrain. Simulation studies based on field data were conducted to validate control performance, followed by field experiments to assess system effectiveness. Key Results The SSMW system’s efficacy was found to be 96.5% by tillage length. Conclusion The SSMW system achieved precise site-specific weeding using GPS-based control of individual sweeps, with a weeding efficacy of 96.5% based on tillage length. The ASIC framework with sensor feedback simulation showed the feasibility of improved adaptability to uneven terrain, with future work focusing on enhanced sensing and faster actuation for improved field performance. Implications and Impacts This study contributes to precision agriculture by enabling targeted weed management through intelligent sensing and control, reducing energy use and soil disruption. The system offers a sustainable alternative for organic farming, improving operational efficiency and environmental stewardship.

papers.title: Code for "Dynamics of Take-off in Bipedal Animals and Robots"
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This archive contains the MATLAB and Python code used to performtake-off dynamics simulations and phylogenetic generalized leastsquares (PGLS) analysis in the study"Dynamics of Take-off in Bipedal Animals and Robots".

papers.title: Configuration-space Bayesian optimisation for stress-critical pose identification on a hyper-redundant robot
authors: Lorenzo De Mari Casareto Dal Verme
papers.venue: International Journal of Intelligent Robotics and Applications
topics: Dynamics and Control of Mechanical Systems
papers.abstract: Abstract Serial manipulators can have strongly varying internal stresses within their configuration space, making the identification of stress-critical poses important for structural design.Because each candidate configuration requires a computationally expensive Finite Element Analysis (FEA), high-fidelity simulations quickly become impractical.This paper proposes a Bayesian optimisation framework that searches directly over the robot configuration space, using peak Von Mises stress as the objective.For each candidate configuration, statically consistent interface reactions are computed and applied as boundary conditions in the structural model.A Gaussian process surrogate with an ARD Matérn 5/2 kernel models the configuration-stress relationship, while the Bayesian algorithm with Expected Improvement acquisition function selects new configurations for parallel evaluation.A case study on a cable-driven hyper-redundant robot demonstrates that the proposed workflow can identify configurations with critical stress states and accurately map the high-stress region with a limited number of simulations.The results show that the framework can support both structural verification and the detection of potentially critical robot poses during operation.

papers.title: Designing Beyond Anthropomorphism: Human- and Robot-Like Error Recovery for Robot Navigation Errors
papers.venue: OpenAlex
papers.abstract: Robots operating in shared human environments will inevitably make mistakes. These errors can negatively affect users’ attitudes toward robots, making effective recovery strategies essential. While prior work has focused on human-like repair behaviors, these may be mismatched with a robot’s capabilities and increase perceptions of its social intelligence. It remains unclear whether robot-like recovery strategies can restore trust without increasing perceived social intelligence. We conducted an online animated video study (N = 219) in which participants observed a healthcare robot making a navigation error followed by one of four recovery strategies: none, robot-like (functional), human-like (socio-emotional), or combined. Trust and perceived social intelligence (PSI) were measured before and after the error. Both trust and PSI decreased significantly following the error. Recovery strategies restored both measures, although their effects differed. Robot-like recovery restored trust more effectively than human-like recovery while avoiding increases in PSI, whereas human-like recovery elevated PSI beyond baseline levels. The combined strategy produced the strongest overall recovery. These findings suggest that robot-like recovery are an effective approach to trust repair while avoiding the increases in perceived social intelligence associated with human-like recovery behaviors.

papers.title: Enhanced seam segmentation for automated welding robot in construction through transfer learning: addressing limitations of bilateral segmentation network
papers.venue: Scientific Reports
topics: Advanced Sensor and Energy Harvesting Materials
papers.abstract: Reliable weld seam segmentation is essential for autonomous robotic welding in construction, where severe illumination changes, specular reflections, and thin weld geometries frequently degrade segmentation performance. This paper proposes a lightweight post-training optimization framework that systematically improves existing real-time semantic segmentation networks without modifying their architectures. Starting from an Online Hard Example Mining (OHEM)-pretrained checkpoint, the proposed framework combines controlled fine-tuning with a hybrid Cross-Entropy–Lovász objective to enhance pixel-level classification, region-level seam continuity, and recovery from reflection-induced segmentation failures while preserving real-time inference efficiency. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed framework substantially improves segmentation performance. Using BiSeNetV2, Joint IoU increases from 59.40% to 81.76% (+22.36 percentage points), while mIoU reaches 90.73% without increasing parameter count, FLOPs, inference latency, or memory consumption. Furthermore, the proposed framework successfully recovers 96.33% of severe zero-IoU failure cases caused by strong reflections, substantially improving the operational reliability of downstream robotic perception. To evaluate the generality of the proposed optimization framework, additional experiments were conducted using U-Net, DeepLabV3+, SegFormer-B0, and PIDNet-S under multiple fine-tuning configurations. The results reveal that the effectiveness of post-training optimization is strongly architecture-dependent: lightweight real-time segmentation networks, particularly BiSeNetV2 and PIDNet-S, consistently benefit from the proposed framework, whereas larger semantic-oriented architectures exhibit comparatively smaller and less stable improvements. In robotic welding experiments, the proposed BiSeNetV2 model was the only evaluated approach capable of consistently generating a valid weld seam trajectory, achieving an average joint-center offset of $$2.47 \pm 0.78$$ mm during robotic path planning, corresponding to an approximately 9.8 $$\times$$ reduction compared with the previous BiSeNetV2-based robotic welding system. Overall, the results demonstrate that carefully designed post-training optimization provides a practical and computationally efficient alternative to architectural redesign, substantially improving failure recovery, seam continuity, and robotic trajectory generation for autonomous welding in reflective construction environments.

papers.title: Back to the museum: Investigation of the acceptance of Android Andrea with and without emotion simulation in a museum
papers.venue: OpenAlex
papers.abstract: For a second time, the android robot Andrea was set up at a public museum in Germany for six consecutive days to have conversations with visitors, fully autonomously. Building on previously gathered qualitative results, the robot was now capable of engaging in multi-lingual conversation with the visitors about the museum context. The robot was prepared with context information about the museum in general and its surrounding exhibits this time. The robot featured a slightly artificial sounding voice that was previously evaluated as congruent with its gender-ambiguous but very humanlike design. Three experimental conditions were implemented, in which either (1) the robot simulated no emotions, (2) the robots emotions were determined by ChatGPT 4.1, or (3) the WASABI emotion simulation architecture simulated the robot’s emotion dynamics. An extended version of the Technology Acceptance Model Version 2 (TAM2) questionnaire was employed to let 73 visitors report on several factors of their opinion about the android robot Andrea after having experienced it. In result, the statistical analysis suggests that these first two approaches to implementing emotions into the chat architecture of our android robot Andrea did not yield any positive effects on the subjective evaluations by the visitors and were not detectable on a conscious level.

papers.title: Coordinated Stability Control Integrating Gait Rhythm Planning and Attitude Feedback for an Underwater Hexapod Robot with Asymmetric Five-Legged Support
papers.venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
papers.abstract: Near-seabed contact operations with underwater hexapod robots can require one leg to execute a contact task, which reduces the stability of the remaining asymmetric five-legged support. To address this problem, this study proposes a five-legged asymmetric coordinated stability control method that integrates gait rhythm planning with attitude feedback. The method decouples the left middle leg from support, propulsion and CPG phase evolution to form a “5+1” asymmetric support base. This configuration reduces the periodic influence of task-induced disturbances on body balance. Meanwhile, a five-legged Hopf-CPG rhythm maintains continuous gait under asymmetric support. Low-bandwidth attitude feedback modulation is introduced between the CPG-generated foot trajectory and the inverse-kinematics input to balance attitude correction with foot-contact continuity. Full-degree-of-freedom underwater simulations in Webots show that, at a flow speed of 0.8 m/s, the method reduces combined attitude RMS by 41.52% relative to the no-feedback strategy. Relative to high-gain PD control, it reduces the RMS rate of change of the control output by 71.32%. These results indicate that the method improves input smoothness and compatibility with five-legged gait rhythms, with a moderate trade-off in transient attitude suppression. It therefore offers a coordinated approach to balancing attitude stability and gait continuity under asymmetric operation.

papers.title: The Civist Manifesto: A Political-Economic Framework for the Labor-Optional Era Spanish and French version
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI
papers.abstract: Spanish and French version The Civist Manifesto proposes Civism as a political-economic framework for the Labor-Optional Era: a period in which artificial intelligence, robotics, and autonomous production may progressively reduce the necessity of human labor for economic survival. Civism does not seek to abolish capitalism, private property, markets, entrepreneurship, or individual economic freedom. Instead, it proposes a new ownership architecture for increasingly autonomous productive capacity. The framework is built around three economic layers: the Human Commons, the Competitive Economy, and the Civilization Capital Layer. At its center is the Citizen Production Fund (CPF), through which citizens collectively own a portion of systemically important automated productive infrastructure and receive returns from that ownership. Civism's central constitutional principle is: Economic inequality is permissible; political inequality is not. The manifesto also proposes an Abundance Test for determining when goods and services may move from market allocation toward universal access, together with constitutional safeguards intended to preserve human political sovereignty in an increasingly AI-driven civilization. This document is presented as a working proposal rather than a finished doctrine. Its economic assumptions, institutional mechanisms, quantitative models, and constitutional structures are intended to be subjected to criticism, empirical testing, peer review, and future revision. Version 1.5 — August 17, 2026

papers.title: A History of Healthcare Computing and Advances in Clinical Information Productivity in Southampton, 1980 -2024: Essay 1: A Brief History of the Computerisation of Healthcare
papers.venue: ePrints Soton (University of Southampton)
papers.abstract: This is the first of a series of essays which record the history of the Clinical Digital Transformation Programme at University Hospital Southampton, from its roots in the history of digital computing in the 1940s and of digital computing as applied to healthcare from the 1960s onwards. The core theme of this project is the productivity and clinical safety in healthcare which can be unleashed in the UK Public Sector through intelligent design, imaginative innovation, a clear long term institutional vision, focussed teamwork and agile, iterative development. These are fundamental elements of digital transformation in a benevolent and supportive management environment. All of these factors combined in the early 1990s in Southampton to create a unique, locally developed clinical informatics environment with powerful design elements and component systems, through close interaction between the computer specialists and clinicians, and at very modest cost. We are at a point where core development and the design optimisation of user facing IT systems appears to have stalled nationally after the initial rush of healthcare IT investment a decade ago, and the arrival of AI tools have created new distractions from getting the basics right. The Southampton experience of the IT development process and its outputs contain many lessons which may be of value for the NHS, for other global health care systems and for commercial system developers. In this essay, I provide a brief historical overview of the development of healthcare computing from its earliest technical origins, and of the UK national context of healthcare computing through which the Southampton programme developed. This includes the Wessex Regional Health Authority Regional Information Systems Plan in the 1980s, and the UK National Programme for IT (NPfIT) in the 2000s, from which many important lessons were learned. These translated into a nationally unique clinical information architecture at University Hospital Southampton UK which continues to evolve.

papers.title: A Paired, Floor-Guarded Evaluation Protocol for INT8 and FP8 Object Detectors under Image Corruptions: Reproducibility Package
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Reproducibility package accompanying the manuscript A Paired, Floor-Guarded Evaluation Protocol for INT8 and FP8 Object Detectors under Image Corruptions, prepared for Computer Vision and Image Understanding. The release contains analysis and validation code, frozen configurations and manifests, compact deterministic evidence ledgers, generated tables and figures, and manuscript and supplementary sources. It supports reproduction of reported summaries from retained evidence.
