papers.title: AI AS AN INSTRUMENT OF CORPORATE SUSTAINABILITY: PREDICTIVE MODELS FOR ENERGY EFFICIENCY AND WASTE MANAGEMENT
papers.venue: Seven Editora eBooks
papers.abstract: This article analyzes the use of predictive artificial intelligence models as an instrument of corporate sustainability, focusing on two operational fronts, energy efficiency and waste management, under a double requirement of analytical honesty: examining what the models actually deliver, beyond discourse, and incorporating into the balance the physical footprint of artificial intelligence itself, whose electricity and water consumption recent literature has begun to quantify. The research, qualitative, documentary and bibliographic, situates the question in Brazil's new regulatory environment, in which the National Solid Waste Policy, the Brazilian Emissions Trading System and the Climate Plan convert sustainability from voluntary commitment into priced obligation, and examines documented predictive applications: in energy, demand and load forecasting, predictive maintenance of motors and climate systems, and process optimization; in waste, generation forecasting, intelligent collection routing, computer-vision-assisted sorting and waste valorization within the circular economy logic. The results systematize the net balance rule, a model is only justified when the physical savings it produces exceed the footprint it adds, and the organizational conditions without which the tool does not deliver: reliable measurement data, integration with management, prepared people and external verifiability of the numbers generated, a condition that the regulated carbon market will make decisive. Finally, the article discusses the risk of algorithmic greenwashing, the green dashboard without corresponding physical reduction, and the asymmetry of access between large companies and small businesses, proposing that artificial intelligence policy and climate policy operate as a single ecosystem of incentives for verified prediction.

papers.title: Search protocol registration: structured two-database review of the sepsis-microcirculation-AI intersection and endothelial shearome analysis (TXK6)
papers.venue: Open Science Framework
papers.abstract: Registration of the search protocol and analysis plan for the TXK6 structured review (project https://osf.io/btrch/, DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/BTRCH). OBJECTIVE: quantify the sepsis x microcirculation x artificial-intelligence literature intersection and specify a methodological framework for an optical-mechanical-molecular readout. DATABASES: PubMed (NCBI E-utilities, tool id txk6_microcirculation_review) and Europe PMC (REST API, TITLE_ABS fields; MEDLINE-scope and whole-repository scope including preprints). SEARCH DATE: 2026-09-02; all raw esearch/efetch and Europe PMC responses are archived in the project (RAW_DATA/LIT_SEARCH/raw/). papers.title: The Evolution of Image Segmentation from Classical Techniques to Deep Learning: A Survey
papers.venue: Robotics
papers.abstract: Image segmentation is a fundamental step in computer vision and a cornerstone of robotic perception, serving as the foundation for interpreting data acquired from vision sensors, enabling robots to analyze complex visual environments, identify and localize objects, and support intelligent decision-making and autonomous control. It plays a critical role in applications such as autonomous navigation, robotic manipulation, medical robotics, agricultural robotics, autonomous vehicles, and human–robot interaction. Image segmentation has evolved from classical methods, which relied on handcrafted rules and mathematical models, to deep learning approaches that learn complex visual patterns directly from data. This evolution reflects advances in algorithms, computational power, and the theoretical foundations of mathematics and data science. Modern deep learning methods rely heavily on large, well-annotated datasets to train sophisticated neural networks. Yet, classical techniques remain valuable in certain scenarios, offering faster, reliable results without extensive computational requirements. Understanding the strengths and limitations of both approaches is key to selecting the right method. This paper surveys image segmentation techniques, comparing them in terms of accuracy, computational cost, and processing speed to guide informed method selection.

papers.title: Self-Supervised Learning for Graph Completion with Contrastive Predictive Coding
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Graph completion is a fundamental problem in various domains, including social network analysis, knowledge graph reasoning, and computer vision. Traditional approaches often rely on explicit supervision or complex, task-specific architectures. Self-supervised learning (SSL) offers an attractive alternative by leveraging unlabeled graph data to learn effective representations. However, existing SSL methods for graph completion frequently struggle to capture the intricate, long-range dependencies inherent in graph structures. This paper introduces a novel approach that addresses this limitation by integrating contrastive predictive coding (CPC) within a graph convolutional network (GCN). The core idea is to train the GCN to predict future nodes or edges given their surrounding context, thereby learning robust representations that explicitly model and capture these long-range dependencies. We formulate the graph completion task as a prediction problem, where the network learns to reconstruct missing edges or nodes based on observed connections. The CPC mechanism acts as a powerful regularizer, encouraging the network to learn representations that are sensitive to contextual information and resistant to noise. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and, crucially, by outlining a practical implementation strategy that can be readily adapted to different graph datasets and completion scenarios. The key contribution lies in combining the inductive bias of SSL with the predictive power of CPC, leading to significant improvements in graph completion performance compared to existing methods.

papers.title: Robust Image Enhancement and Restoration for Real-World Computer Vision
papers.venue: Advances in computational intelligence and robotics book series
topics: Generative Adversarial Networks and Image Synthesis
papers.abstract: This chapter presents a comprehensive study of image enhancement, restoration and preprocessing techniques for real-world computer vision applications. It begins by examining the physical sources of image degradation, including noise, blur, illumination variation, compression artifacts and adverse environmental conditions such as low light and weather effects. The limitations of vision systems trained under ideal conditions are highlighted through their degraded performance in unconstrained environments. The chapter reviews classical approaches, emphasizing their interpretability and efficiency. It then explores modern deep learning techniques such as convolutional neural networks, generative adversarial networks, transformers and diffusion models, which achieve superior performance through data-driven learning. Hybrid frameworks that integrate classical and learned methods are discussed as a practical solution for balancing robustness, interpretability and performance.

The review systematically categorizes technologies such as Machine Learning, Deep Learning, IoT Sensor Networks, Robotics, and Computer Vision, demonstrating how they address critical industry challenges like labor shortages, disease outbreaks, and environmental sustainability. It highlights transformative functional objectives—including health monitoring, environmental control, and animal welfare assessment—supported by compelling metrics such as up to 99.5% accuracy in detecting avian influenza, up to 10% improvement in Feed Conversion Ratios through smart feeding, and robotic systems that achieve a 95% success rate in egg collection while reducing pathogen loads by over 90%. Including keywords like Precision Livestock Farming, Automated Poultry Operations, and Avian Disease Detection alongside this summary will ensure the research effectively reaches the right audience.

papers.title: Smartphone based clinical decision support system for early detection of neonatal jaundice using artificial intelligence with temporal convolutional network
papers.venue: Technology and Health Care
papers.abstract: Abstract Physiological jaundice is present in the initial week of life in neonates owing to the rise in level of bilirubin thereby resulting in yellowish coloring of sclera and skin. Severe jaundice and lethal bilirubin levels may result from brain damage as bilirubin is located in the central nervous system. Present diagnostic techniques consist of time-consuming and a painful invasive blood test and non-invasive tests using expensive transcutaneous bilirubin meters. Then regular monitoring is important, numerous efforts are conducted to progress non-invasive devices for testing utilizing a smartphone camera. Various efforts have been deployed to automate the neonatal jaundice diagnosis applying dissimilar machine learning, image processing, and CV methods. With the rise of smartphone-based and computer vision applications in clinical environments, especially for early detection of diseases like neonatal jaundice, reliability becomes more critical. This paper develops an Advancing Early Jaundice Detection of Neonatal with a Smartphone-based Computer Vision System and Golden Jackal Optimizer algorithm (AEJDN-SCVGJO) for Clinical Decision-Making. The image pre-processing applies an adaptive median filter (AMF) to enhance image quality by removing the noise. For the feature extractor, the SE-DenseNet has been deployed. Moreover, the proposed AEJDN-SCVGJO model executes the temporal convolutional network (TCN) model for the classification process. Finally, the Golden Jackal Optimizer (GJO) adjusts the parameter value of the TCN model optimally and outcomes in higher solution of classification. To exhibit the enhanced execution of the presented AEJDN-SCVGJO methodology, a wide-ranging experimental investigation is made. The comparative outcomes reported the improvised characteristics of the AEJDN-SCVGJO model.

papers.title: Predictive Coding with Holographic Representations of Sensory Data
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to predictive coding leveraging holographic representations of sensory data. The core idea is to encode sensory information using holographic transforms, creating a compressed and structured representation that facilitates efficient prediction and anomaly detection. We hypothesize that the brain's ability to rapidly process sensory information stems, in part, from a fundamentally holographic encoding. This framework aims to mimic this process computationally, offering a potentially more robust and efficient system compared to traditional predictive coding models. The proposed method utilizes a multi-layered holographic transform to decompose sensory input, extracting both spatial and temporal features. The resulting holographic representation is then used to predict subsequent sensory events, with deviations from the prediction highlighting potential anomalies. Mathematical formulations detail the transform process, prediction equations, and anomaly detection criteria. The ultimate goal is to develop a computational model capable of exhibiting similar perceptual efficiencies as the biological brain, with applications in areas such as artificial intelligence, computer vision, and neuroscience research.

papers.title: Video-based fruit detection and tracking: effects of scanning conditions on fruit load estimation
papers.venue: Computers and Electronics in Agriculture
papers.abstract: Automated fruit counting and yield estimation systems are necessary for efficient orchard management. This study presents a computer vision system based on video multi-object-tracking for fruit load estimation in apple orchards and provides a comprehensive analysis of the system performance under diverse scanning conditions. The system integrates fruit detection, tracking, localization within orchard, and fruit load map generation. Experiments were carried out in an experimental apple orchard containing 420 apple trees. Data was collected with two different RGB-D sensors (Azure Kinect DK and ZED 2) at three different scanning distances (125 cm, 175 cm, and 225 cm) on two different dates prior to the harvest. Comparing the two evaluated sensors, Azure Kinect provided more consistent performance across different dates. Results also show that the longer scanning distance improves accuracy due to seeing the full tree view gives better fruit counts than close partial views. Between the two dates, best results were achieved near harvest due to fruit color at this stage, achieving a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 6.91 % and a determination coefficient (R 2 ) of 0.733 (using ZED2 sensor at 225 cm distance). Finally, a test comparing scanning from one or both sides of the tree row showed that bilateral scanning improved fruit load estimation at the stretch level by incorporating information from both sides of the canopy. The results of this work demonstrate the effectiveness of the video fruit tracking systems as a useful tool for automating fruit load estimation.

papers.title: PROJECT BASIRA: A SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE FOR AI-POWERED SMART GLASSES WITH SPATIAL MEMORY FOR ENVIRONMENTAL AWARENESS AND SAFE NAVIGATION FOR VISUALLY IMPAIRED INDIVIDUALS
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: PROJECT BASIRA presents a proposed system architecture for AI-powered smart glasses designed to support environmental awareness, spatial understanding, and safer navigation for visually impaired individuals. The architecture integrates multimodal environmental perception, semantic scene understanding, persistent spatial memory, temporal context, distance and motion estimation, context-aware risk analysis, intelligent alert prioritization, voice interaction, haptic feedback, facility recognition, indoor spatial awareness, adaptive assistance, and emergency-oriented functions. The proposed framework combines sensing, perception, environmental representation, spatial memory, motion and proximity reasoning, risk analysis, information prioritization, and multimodal human-computer interaction within a unified architecture. Its central contribution is the integration of environmental perception with persistent spatial context and contextual risk prioritization rather than the introduction of a new individual computer-vision algorithm. A substantial portion of BASIRA has been implemented as a browser-based Three.js 3D simulation and Digital-Twin-Inspired evaluation environment. The prototype represents metric three-dimensional urban and indoor scenarios containing roads, sidewalks, buildings, hospitals, schools, pharmacies, libraries, elevators, stairs, gates, pedestrians, vehicles, traffic lights, pedestrian crossings, tactile paths, environmental landmarks, weather and visibility variations, construction zones, and emergency scenarios. The simulation incorporates spatial memory, temporal snapshots, place memory, voice interaction, speech synthesis, haptic feedback, line-of-sight analysis, occlusion analysis, and a rule-based risk engine incorporating distance, object motion, approach direction, and heuristic time-to-collision. BASIRA v1.0 defines the system architecture, eleven functional intelligence engines, spatial-memory representation, dynamic risk-analysis formulation, context-aware assistance mechanisms, privacy-oriented processing principles, simulation methodology, and a reproducible framework for future quantitative evaluation. Proposed evaluation metrics include object detection, distance estimation, navigation safety, risk recognition, spatial-memory retrieval, voice interaction, computational performance, system latency, and usability. This release is a technical research preprint and proposed system architecture. The current implementation is a research prototype and simulation environment. Simulated confidence values, predefined thresholds, theoretical benchmarks, and proposed performance targets are not presented as experimentally measured accuracy or validated real-world performance. Physical deployment, real-world safety, clinical effectiveness, and user-centered performance require future validation using real hardware, real datasets, controlled experiments, and ethically approved human-subject studies. papers.title: Robust Image Processing Under Real-World Conditions

papers.abstract: This chapter proposes a comprehensive study of robust image processing techniques designed to address real-world imaging challenges that commonly degrade visual data quality. Hybrid strategies that combine interpretability with performance are emphasized to improve reliability. The chapter underscores how effective preprocessing directly enhances the robustness, accuracy, and trustworthiness of downstream computer vision systems operating in unconstrained environments.

papers.title: Empathetic-Driven Robot Interaction
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper explores the development of empathetic-driven robot interaction, a novel approach to human-robot interaction (HRI) focused on enabling robots to understand and respond to human emotions. The core claim is that robots can achieve more natural and effective interactions by simulating empathetic behaviors through the analysis of human expressions and body language. This research leverages computer vision and natural language processing (NLP) techniques to recognize human emotions and subsequently adapts the robot's behavior and language accordingly. The proposed system moves beyond simple task-oriented interaction to facilitate a deeper connection between humans and robots. We outline the key components of this system, including emotion recognition, response generation, and behavioral adaptation. The paper culminates in a discussion of the potential applications and future research directions within this field. ---

papers.title: Explainable and Interpretable Vision Models for Trust and Accountability in Real-World Image Processing Systems
papers.venue: Advances in computational intelligence and robotics book series
papers.abstract: As computer vision systems are increasingly used in safety-critical and real-world settings, explainability is essential for trust, accountability, and responsible deployment. This chapter explores explainable and interpretable AI techniques for image processing, including gradient-based methods like saliency maps and Grad-CAM, as well as concept-based explanations, counterfactual reasoning, and model-agnostic approaches such as LIME and SHAP. It highlights how interpretability supports debugging, bias detection, regulatory compliance, uncertainty estimation, and human-in-the-loop decision-making. The chapter also examines integrating explainability into deployment pipelines, MLOps workflows, and monitoring systems. Key challenges discussed include robustness, computational efficiency, and trade-offs between interpretability and model performance. Through real-world applications, it demonstrates how explainability enhances transparency and reliability, ultimately providing a roadmap for building trustworthy and deployable computer vision systems.

papers.title: BoilingBench-CV Dataset
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Overview BoilingBench-CV is a benchmark dataset package for evaluating computer-vision methods for two-dimensional bubble instance segmentation and per-frame bubble morphometry. It is designed to measure within-domain performance and generalization across water and HFE-7100 imaging domains. This package does not yet establish a tracking or bubble-dynamics benchmark. Per-image contours do not encode reviewed temporal bubble identities, coalescence/breakup events, or departure times. Contents - `raw/`: immutable copies of source annotated-image subsets and their original annotation formats. - `derived/`: canonical COCO-style annotations and manifests generated from the raw data. - `splits/`: immutable grouped benchmark partitions. - `metadata/`: source, rights, annotation, and quality-assurance records. - `docs/`: data-card and release notes. The source video collections are deliberately not duplicated here. The benchmark uses annotated still images; original videos remain in their source archives. Data domains The initial pool-boiling component includes FCu-H2O, PCu-H2O, PSi-HFE, and SSi-HFE annotated subsets. They form a valuable but compound domain shift: fluid, surface, image geometry, optical arrangement, and facility may differ. Water-versus-HFE results must not be interpreted as a fluid-only causal effect. Use rules 1. Preserve `raw/` unchanged. 2. Use only the supplied grouped split files for reported benchmark results. 3. Do not split frames from the same `(regime, source video/power condition)` across partitions. 4. Report performance by regime, not only a pooled score. 5. Treat annotations flagged in `metadata/annotation_qa.md` according to the benchmark evaluator's documented ignore policy. Attribution When using the package, cite the BoilingBench-CV dataset version and the source dataset records listed in `metadata/data_sources.csv`, together with the assigned Zenodo DOI: [10.5281/zenodo.22264378](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22264378).

papers.title: AI applications in physical retail: technologies, consumer interaction, and operational impact
papers.venue: The International Review of Retail Distribution and Consumer Research
papers.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in physical retail environments is transforming customer experiences and operational efficiency. While research on AI technologies such as chatbots, virtual assistants, computer vision, and machine learning has grown rapidly, it remains fragmented, often focusing on isolated technologies or single aspects of the retail experience. This study addresses this fragmentation by systematically synthesizing prior findings through a systematic literature review (SLR) of 50 peer-reviewed studies to develop a unified understanding of how AI transforms the in-store customer journey. AI applications were categorized along three dimensions: (A) AI technologies, (B) application areas, and (C) resulting impacts. The synthesis reveals that AI enhances customer engagement through personalized recommendations and interactive service tools while optimizing backend processes such as inventory management, pricing, and checkout automation. However, three key challenges persist: (1) AI’s limited emotional intelligence, (2) ethical concerns regarding data privacy and algorithmic transparency, and (3) scalability and integration constraints in physical retail settings. This research contributes to the existing literature by offering a conceptual framework for AI adoption in retail, synthesizing prior research across the pre-engagement, in-store experience, and post-purchase phases. It highlights the strategic tensions between customer engagement and operational goals, emphasizing the need for ethical governance and cross-functional AI integration. The study advances theoretical understanding and provides actionable insights for both academics and practitioners, outlining avenues for future research on AI-driven retail innovations.

papers.abstract: The Oreochromis niloticus 8 cm Dataset is a curated repository of annotated images designed for the development and benchmarking of Artificial Intelligence models in precision aquaculture, particularly for fish detection and counting tasks annotated using the Bounding Box method. The dataset contains images of Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) at the 8 cm growth stage captured in a controlled environment, which enhances visual contrast and facilitates object detection and segmentation processes. The images were obtained under consistent lighting and background conditions, minimizing environmental variability while still preserving common computer vision challenges such as:Variations in orientation and positioningSubtle scale differences among the 8 cm specimensVisual similarity between instances (low inter-class variance)All images are annotated with bounding boxes in YOLO format, supporting direct use in state-of-the-art object detection frameworks.This dataset is highly recommended for training and evaluating deep learning architectures, including the YOLO family (v8 to v11) and Faster R-CNN, particularly in scenarios requiring precise counting and detection under controlled densities and specific growth stages. papers.title: Empathetic-Driven Robot Interaction
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper explores the development of empathetic-driven robot interaction, a novel approach to human-robot interaction (HRI) focused on enabling robots to understand and respond to human emotions. The core claim is that robots can achieve more natural and effective interactions by simulating empathetic behaviors through the analysis of human expressions and body language. This research leverages computer vision and natural language processing (NLP) techniques to recognize human emotions and subsequently adapts the robot's behavior and language accordingly. The proposed system moves beyond simple task-oriented interaction to facilitate a deeper connection between humans and robots. We outline the key components of this system, including emotion recognition, response generation, and behavioral adaptation. The paper culminates in a discussion of the potential applications and future research directions within this field. ---

papers.title: Geometric Information Fusion for Dynamic Matching
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
topics: Advanced Image and Video Retrieval Techniques
papers.abstract: Geometric information fusion is a crucial component of many data analysis and modeling tasks, particularly in areas such as computer vision, robotics, and structural engineering. However, traditional approaches often rely on static feature extraction and mapping, failing to fully leverage the rich geometric context available in diverse datasets. This paper introduces a novel dynamic geometric information fusion algorithm, termed "Dynamic Geometry Matching" (DGM), designed to address this limitation. DGM dynamically integrates geometric information from multiple data sources, adapting to the specific characteristics of each data point. We demonstrate the effectiveness of DGM through rigorous experimental analysis, showing significant improvements in accuracy and robustness compared to existing methods. The core mechanism focuses on establishing a flexible and adaptive mapping between data sources and a shared geometric representation, enabling intelligent data integration. This advancement promises to unlock new possibilities in data analysis, leading to more accurate and reliable modeling.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Poultry Farms: Current Applications, Opportunities, Challenges and Future Trends (Systematic Literature Review)
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence in Poultry Farms: Current Applications, Opportunities, Challenges, and Future Trends (Systematic Literature Review), an in-depth evaluation of AI integration in modern poultry management. The review systematically categorizes technologies such as Machine Learning, Deep Learning, IoT Sensor Networks, Robotics, and Computer Vision, demonstrating how they address critical industry challenges like labor shortages, disease outbreaks, and environmental sustainability. It highlights transformative functional objectives—including health monitoring, environmental control, and animal welfare assessment—supported by compelling metrics such as up to 99.5% accuracy in detecting avian influenza, up to 10% improvement in Feed Conversion Ratios through smart feeding, and robotic systems that achieve a 95% success rate in egg collection while reducing pathogen loads by over 90%. Including keywords like Precision Livestock Farming, Automated Poultry Operations, and Avian Disease Detection alongside this summary will ensure the research effectively reaches the right audience.

papers.title: Peripheral Visual Perception and Flag Football Experience in Quarterbacks and Their Associations with Decision-Making in a Computer-Based Read-and-React Task
papers.venue: Current Issues in Sport Science (CISS)
papers.abstract: Introduction & Purpose Quarterback (QB) performance in flag football requires rapid selection of relevant visual information and decision-making under pressure. Perceptual-cognitive expertise is associated with more accurate decisions and more efficient visual information use in sport (Mann et al., 2007; Vaeyens et al., 2007). Peripheral information may contribute to such decisions in dynamic game situations (Ryu et al., 2013). The Attention-Window Task (AWT) assesses the breadth and spatial distribution of attention independently of a particular sport. However, attention-window profiles may reflect sport-specific spatial demands: athletes from sports characterised by predominantly horizontal or vertical information demands demonstrate correspondingly wider attentional breadth (Hüttermann et al., 2014). This partly exploratory study combined the sport-unspecific AWT with a newly developed, computer-based Read-and-React (R&R) task to investigate associations between peripheral attentional performance, flag football experience and QB-specific decision accuracy. Methods A sample of twenty athletes (15 male, 5 female; age: M = 22.3, SD = 5.5 years) was included after data-quality exclusions from two Pro Day testing sessions organised by the American Football Association Austria (AFBÖ). Participants had 10.8 ± 5.3 years of flag football experience. In the R&R task, schematic flag football pass plays were presented as dynamic sequences, and participants selected the most appropriate receiver by key press. The AWT assessed overall, horizontal, vertical, and diagonal attentional breadth. Associations were analysed using Spearman rank correlations. Exploratory Mann–Whitney U tests compared athletes with the five highest and five lowest overall AWT scores. Results R&R decision accuracy was not significantly associated with overall AWT performance (ρ = .29, p = .218), horizontal (ρ = −.00, p = .986), vertical (ρ = .33, p = .153) or diagonal attentional breadth (ρ = .18, p = .447), nor with flag football experience (ρ = .33, p = .153). Exploratory analyses identified a significant positive association between flag football experience and vertical attentional breadth (ρ = .53, p = .015). Athletes with the five highest overall AWT scores showed descriptively higher R&R accuracy than those with the five lowest scores, although the large difference did not reach statistical significance (U = 22.00, p = .057, absolute rrb = .76). Discussion This study provides initial insights into relationships between QB-specific decision accuracy, peripheral attentional performance and flag football experience. Although attention-window performance was not significantly associated with Read-and-React decision accuracy, greater flag football experience was associated with greater vertical attentional breadth. In line with previous findings that attentional profiles may reflect the spatial demands of specific sports (Hüttermann et al., 2014), this result provides preliminary evidence that experience in flag football may be linked to the spatial distribution of peripheral attention. However, the observed relevance of the vertical dimension should be interpreted cautiously: the screen-based R&R task may emphasize vertically developing visual information differently from actual on-field play. Conclusion The small, performance-oriented sample limits generalisability, and transfer from a screen- based task to on-field decisions remains unclear, particularly where the display may emphasise vertically developing information. Overall, the findings provide an initial basis for further examining the relationship between the R&R task and peripheral awareness. References Hüttermann, S., Memmert, D., & Simons, D. J. (2014). The size and shape of the attentional “spotlight” varies with differences in sports expertise. Journal of Experimental Psychology: Applied, 20(2), 147–157. https://doi.org/10.1037/xap0000012 Mann, D.
